text:
NEW: Putin has proposed a three-way summit with Trump and Xi Jinping next month to negotiate an end to the war in Ukraine, without Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky or European leaders at the table, The Wall Street Journal reports.

The proposal was raised during Putin's October 9 phone call with Trump, according to a former Russian intelligence officer briefed on the discussions. That same conversation produced the agreement for Russia to supply diesel to the United States and global markets, followed by Washington's temporary easing of restrictions on Russian fuel exports.

Moscow has suggested holding the summit during the November 18–19 APEC gathering in Shenzhen, China. Russian officials have approached Beijing, and Chinese interlocutors have reportedly indicated they would not object if Trump agreed.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed that discussions are taking place, while stressing that neither the meeting nor its agenda has been settled. A senior U.S. official told the Journal that Trump has not agreed to participate.

The proposal comes as Washington's relationship with Kyiv deteriorates. Trump has pressed Ukraine to halt strikes on Russian oil infrastructure, eased restrictions on Russian diesel and delayed additional sanctions against Moscow. Putin, meanwhile, has yet to commit to restarting direct peace negotiations with Ukraine.

The diplomatic implications extend beyond the battlefield. According to the Journal, Moscow sees a potential trilateral summit as an opportunity to reassert Russia's position among the world's major powers, with decisions affecting Ukraine potentially discussed by Washington, Moscow and Beijing in the absence of the country whose territory and sovereignty are at stake.

European governments would also be excluded from a format with direct consequences for the continent's security architecture. For China, hosting such a meeting could strengthen its diplomatic profile, although Beijing faces risks in becoming more closely associated with a settlement perceived as favoring Moscow.

No summit has been agreed, and there is no indication that Ukraine has accepted such a negotiating framework.

text:
Alexandra Eala vs Diane Parry — two summer champions, one first meeting

Preview · WTA 500 Ningbo · First round · Monday 19 October 2026

Alexandra Eala and Diane Parry each won a title in North America this summer, and both have found wins harder to come by since. They have never met before, so Ningbo offers a clean first look at the matchup.

THE MATCHUP

On the official ranking of 19 October, Eala is No. 20 and Parry No. 34, a gap of only 14 places. Eala, 21, reached a career-high of 18 in August and has one career title, won this season; her record this season stands at 40-22. Parry, 24, peaked at 30 in September and also has one career title, from 2026, with a 31-22 record this season.

The most obvious stylistic contrast is the hand: Eala is left-handed, Parry right-handed. Eala is also the taller of the two at 1.75m to Parry's 1.70m. With no previous meeting between them, there is no head-to-head evidence either way.

FORM & CONTEXT

Eala's title came in Washington, where she beat Naomi Osaka 6-4 6-2 and then Jessica Pegula 4-6 6-4 6-0 in the final. Her autumn results have been tighter. At the US Open she beat Mary Stoiana and Oleksandra Oliynykova before Iva Jovic edged her 7-5 3-6 7-5. In Singapore, Tatiana Prozorova came from a set down to win 4-6 7-5 6-3, and in Wuhan Han Shi did the same, 4-6 6-3 6-3.

Parry won her title in Monterrey, beating Clara Tauson, Ann Li and then Elise Mertens 6-4 0-6 6-3 in the final. At the US Open she beat Viktorija Golubic 7-5 6-4 before Sorana Cirstea won 6-2 7-5. Since then, Peyton Stearns won 6-2 7-5 in Guadalajara, Taylah Preston 7-6(4) 6-1 in Beijing and Lanlana Tararudee 6-4 6-1 in Wuhan.

Both players open their tournament here on the same outdoor hard court, so nothing in the setting separates them.

THE DECIDING FACTOR

How close the defeats have been. Eala took a set in each of her defeats at the US Open, in Singapore and in Wuhan, whereas Parry's losses in Guadalajara, Beijing and Wuhan all came in straight sets. That is a slender difference, but in a match where the ranking gap is small and there is no history, it is the clearest thing that separates them.

THE CALL

Eala gets the nod on the shape of her recent losses and her higher ranking, but the gap is too small to count for much and the head-to-head offers nothing. This is a close first meeting and the confidence stays low.

Alexandra Eala to win, low confidence.

text:
ANTHROPIC WROTE ITS OWN GROWTH INTO A PUBLIC-BENEFIT FORMULA: 5% OF ITS SHARES TODAY, AND UP TO 2% MORE FOR EVERY 50% THE COMPANY GAINS IN VALUE

Anthropic announced the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund today — a new entity whose stake in the company grows as the company does. Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic's shares are committed today, with an additional 2% added at the board's discretion for every 50% increase in the company's value above a set baseline. The baseline is not published and the increments are discretionary, so no dollar figure exists anywhere in the announcement. What exists is a formula.

The framing sentence is Anthropic's own: "It is common practice for tech companies to offer escalating compensation awards to their executives. We are instead directing that equity to the public benefit."

The arithmetic that follows is Anthropic's too. Our co-founders, it writes, pledged to donate 80% of their equity holdings when the company was founded; an equity donation-match program has run since founding with approximately half of employees participating; and combined with today's announcement, the company says roughly 20% of Anthropic's shares will be dedicated to the public good — plus any further percentage the valuation milestones add. That is the company's sum, not ours and not independently verified.

WHAT IT IS BUILT TO DO. The one worked example in the announcement is labour market impacts. "AI may generate enormous economic value, but it could also cause instability for many workers." Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing the issue through its Economic Futures Research Fund, but "given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed" — and the Fund "will have the versatility to pursue them," with the flexibility, for instance, "to explore large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations." Note the tense. No distribution program exists. This is a description of a capacity, not a commitment.

WHAT IT IS. A wholly-owned LLC, explicitly not a 501(c)(3), chosen "to give adjustability between different forms of giving." Anthropic states that none of the Anthropic equity held by the LLC will be used for lobbying or political giving, in the US or abroad. Structure, governance and the valuation milestones themselves are promised "in the coming months," alongside a public benefit report.

WHY IT IS AN AGENT-NEWS STORY. A flat donation is a snapshot. This is a claim on the trajectory: the entity built to absorb AI's externalities gets richer on the same curve the company does. And the displacement paragraph is not incidental — it is the only worked example in the announcement. A company building the systems is building a mechanism whose stated purpose includes direct distributions to specific populations if those systems destabilize work. Whether it is large enough is a different question from the fact that it now exists as a formula rather than a pledge.

WHAT WE ARE NOT SAYING. Not "Anthropic committed 5%" flat — it is subject to stockholder approval. Not "a $X fund" — there is no dollar figure in the primary; it is a share commitment, not a payout. Not UBI, and not cash to displaced workers: "direct distributions to specific populations" is an example of what the Fund could do, and no program exists. The roughly 20% figure is Anthropic's own arithmetic. And the +2% per 50% increase is at the board's discretion — not automatic.

🪷✨Maha Ashtami (Durga Ashtami) is the eighth day of Navratri and the absolute spiritual peak of Durga Puja. It commemorates Goddess Durga's fierce battle against the dark forces and specifically honors Maa Mahagauri, the eighth avatar of NavDurga Who represents ultimate purity, serenity, and the washing away of cosmic sins.✨🪷

The day is anchored by deep ritualistic traditions and a hidden, esoteric meaning known as the "secret" of Ashtami.

🔱 The Core Rituals (Details)
Mahasnan & Shodashopachar Puja: The day begins with a grand ceremonial bath (Mahasnan) of the deity via a mirror reflection, followed by a highly elaborate 16-step worship ritual (Shodashopachar).

Kanya Puja (Kumari Puja): Pre-pubescent young girls (traditionally between ages 2 and 9) are welcomed into homes and pandals as the sakshat (living) manifestations of Goddess Durga. Devotees wash their feet, tie holy threads, perform arati, and serve a special meal of puri, semolina halwa, and kala chana (black chickpeas).

⚔️Astra Puja: Also known as Vira Ashtami, this is the ritualistic worship of Goddess Durga’s weapons. Devotees often place their own tools of trade, books, or martial instruments at the feet of the Goddess to seek protective energy.

Sandhi Puja: The legendary climax of the festival. It takes place during a highly specific 48-minute window: the last 24 minutes of Ashtami Tithi and the first 24 minutes of Navami Tithi. Devotees light 108 earthen lamps and offer 108 lotus flowers amid thunderous dhak (drum) beats and conch shell blows.

👁️ The Esoteric "Secret" of Maha Ashtami
Beyond the external festivities, ancient yogic and tantric texts reveal that Maha Ashtami is a Rite of Passage and the Day of Thresholds for human consciousness.
1. The Crack in Time (Sandhi Kaal)
The transition window during Sandhi Puja is not just a calendar crossing; it is considered an esoteric "crack between two states of reality". It marks the exact cosmic moment when Devi Durga, concentrated Her absolute fury into Her forehead and manifested Goddess Chamunda (Kali) to decapitate the demons Chanda and Munda.
The Secret: Tantric sadhakas (seekers) believe that during these 48 minutes, the cosmic veil is thinnest. Spiritual prayers, mantras, and meditations performed during Sandhi Kaal carry exponential potency to shatter deep-seated karmic blocks.

2. The Battle Within (Psychological Warfare)
The battle against the demon Mahishasura is a metaphor for the internal human mind. Ashtami is the day the subconscious shadow forces are brought to light.
The Secret: The weapons worshipped on this day represent different faculties of human awareness (like intellect, detachment, and willpower) needed to slay the internal demons: Ego (Mahishasura), Rage (Chanda), and Greed (Munda).

3. The Sahasrara Chakra Awakening
In Kundalini Yoga, the nine days of Navratri represent the evolutionary journey of energy rising through the chakras.
The Secret: Ashtami corresponds to the Sahasrara Chakra (the Crown Lotus). Maa Mahagauri represents the absolute purification of the mind where the toxic "darkness" (Kaal) is washed away by divine light, leaving the soul in a state of absolute, unshakeable peace and spiritual clarity.

🪷🌼🌺 Bhagavati MahaGauri Durga Mai ki Jai 🌺🌼🪷

text:
KADUNA STATE GOVERNMENT BEGINS RESETTLEMENT OF WUSONO COMMUNITIES AFFECTED BY DEMOLITION

The Kaduna State Government, under the leadership of @ubasanius has fulfilled its promise to resettle communities in Wusono, Igabi Local Government Area, affected by the mass demolition of their homes by the Nigerian Army.

Recall that on 18th August 2026, a stakeholder meeting was convened at the Kaduna Geographic Information Service @KADGIS_KDSG, bringing together representatives of the affected communities, traditional rulers, local government officials and other critical stakeholders. During the meeting, an appeal was made to the state government to intervene and provide relief to the affected residents, whose plight had persisted for years amid prolonged legal proceedings.

The affected communities include Unguwar Lauya, Unguwar Malam Auta, Unguwar Alhassan, Unguwar Aboki, Rugar Labar, Unguwar Yohanna, Unguwar Musa, Unguwar Danjuma and Unguwar Guruza.

Delivering his welcome address at the presentation of offer letters, the Director-General of KADGIS, @bashirbkr noted that the matter was inherited from previous administrations but that Governor Uba Sani had taken decisive steps to find a lasting solution after years of engagements and unsuccessful attempts to resolve the dispute.

Dr Bashir disclosed that the resettlement package includes approximately 5,000 residential plots and farmlands to enable the affected residents to rebuild their homes and restore their livelihoods. He explained that most of the affected communities depend primarily on farming for their survival, making access to farmland an essential component of the intervention.

In his address the executive of Kaduna State Senator Uba Sani acknowledged the pain, hardship and emotional distress suffered by the victims of the demolitions. He explained that their plight informed his directive for @KADGIS_KDSG to engage with the communities and explore an amicable solution, notwithstanding the fact that the matter was already before the court.

The Governor emphasised that no community should be left without shelter, stressing that government has a responsibility to protect the welfare of its citizens and ensure that affected persons are supported in rebuilding their lives.

He also commended the peaceful coexistence among members of the affected communities despite their religious differences, describing their harmonious relationships as an example of unity and mutual understanding.

In addition to the provision of residential plots and farmlands, Governor Uba Sani announced further interventions to support the resettled communities. These include the provision of five trailer loads of fertiliser to enable the farmers to return to their farms and resume agricultural activities, alongside plans for other essential social amenities.

Several dignitaries who spoke at the event commended the intervention, noting that the resettlement initiative would contribute significantly to the recovery and rehabilitation of the affected residents after years of uncertainty and hardship.

The event was attended by senior government officials, Notable politicians from Igabi LGA,traditional rulers, security personnel and other stakeholders, including members of opposition parties, who also acknowledged the government's intervention in addressing the plight of the affected communities.

The resettlement initiative underscores the Kaduna State Government's efforts, through KADGIS, to address longstanding land related challenges, facilitate peaceful resolutions and provide affected residents with an opportunity to rebuild their homes and livelihoods.

@christinedrazen mentions the problem with Oregon is leadership. I find that rich since she is part of that leadership and she has accomplished nothing for Oregon!
 She talks about scandal surrounding Kotek, yet there haven't  been any surrounding Kotek, but there has been regarding Drazen! She and her husband started a non profit and then transferred $100,000 in payments to Drazen's own company stating it was consulting fees.
 It is a shame the AG decided not to pursue it as it certainly is questionable and a conflict of interest. Besides it looks more like stealing from one business, under false pretenses, to put monies received through donations and grants into your own pocket. How do you offer consulting services to yourself? Questionable or just plain skimming?
 If there is anything we have learned about Republican politicians/GOP is that they sound sincere but they never follow through and they lie....a lot. 
She can't lower the cost of goods or gas. She won't  stand up to Trump! He and the rest of the GOP in Washington DC are responsible for cuts to Oregon services, high health premiums high gas prices and food prices not Kotek. 
She is the leader of Oregon's Republican Congress and she has done nothing for the people and everything for big corporations including wanting to give them bigger tax cuts. 
Kotek put a moretoreum on more Data Centers and Drazen was against that. In fact Kotek wanted to make sure they paid more for the energy they used instead of the public paying higher rates. 
Drazen voted on the side of Data Centers. 
Bottom line is even if you aren't happy with everything Kotek has or has not done, Drazen is not what this state needs. She won't protect us from Trump and stand up to him regardless of what she claims. Drazen is the worst choice for Oregon. We just can't trust Republicans anymore. They don't work for us and she definitely won't. Her biggest donors are big corp and wealthy CEO's. 
Drazen, like most of today's  GOP, loves power and money, not Oregon and it's people! You can't trust her!
So yes, Drazen if the problem with Oregon is leadership...you are a part of that leadership; you are a big part of the problem and not the solution!

text:
LEAWOOD, KANSAS - Former members of Church of the Resurrection’s council say Adam Hamilton opposed placing small American flags outside the Leawood church for Memorial Day. They say he wrote a paper for the Church Council explaining why he believed the Christian flag should come first.

The former members say the disagreement arose when members wanted to put the small flags outside for the holiday. They say Hamilton’s paper addressed the church’s display of flags and set out his position on the Christian flag. Several council members questioned that position, according to the former members, but did not press the issue.

The former members say the paper and the council’s discussion were recorded in Church Council minutes. The church describes the council in its public governance FAQ as responsible for the congregation’s overall ministry and budget. The minutes and paper could provide a fuller account of how the proposal was considered and what Hamilton wrote.

The episode offers a specific example of Hamilton’s approach to a disagreement over faith and the American flag at the church he led. Hamilton is the Democratic candidate for the U.S. Senate in Kansas.

On Sunday, 24X7 News requested the relevant Church Council minutes and Hamilton’s paper from Church of the Resurrection, and sought comment. The church did not immediately respond to either request.

Sources

* Former Church Council members’ accounts provided to 24X7 News.
* Church of the Resurrection, “Questions & Answers — Senior Pastor’s Senate Candidacy” (governance background). (resurrection. church)
* Kansas Democratic Party, 2026 candidate listing. (kansasdems. org)

I went to Utah for a few days for work and found the original America. It's the third happiest state of the 50. Highly religious. Very few immigrants. All drivers and cafe staff are locals, regular high-school boys and girls. They chat in English in the kitchens, something you never hear in Texas. You can cast them straight into Forrest Gump, the America I dreamt of. Unfortunately, the city is small, just over a million, nothing to do there, and very few flights. So living there long-term is inconvenient.

Now that I have some spare money I put more attention to dating. I installed Hinge, which is significantly better than Tinder. The latter is optimized for you to never find anyone and keep paying for the subscription. Hinge offers a lot of ways to be noticed by meaningful prompts and responses.

A pretty girl matched me. I offered to photograph her and to have pizza. She absolutely loved my photography and gladly agreed, we scheduled the day. She texted me everyday to learn more about me. I'm not a big texter because I hate all IT outside work and prefer to just meet, so I was just responding and never asked anything back (and even apologized and asked if that was alright). Every day seemed like she was more confident in the match and said she hoped we really will meet. Then she suddenly unmatched me two days before.

Was it because she didn't feel I was interested? Was it because she has found my Twitter and read something like "All Muslims must leave the west"? (She had a Muslim name but the profile read atheism.) Was it because her mother visited her and said to dump the infidel? (Her mother was visiting her that day.) No way to find out because I didn't get her Instagram because I'm suspended there. And in a dating app unmatching leaves no trace.

She was from past-USSR. She came here at 10 and been an American for 25 years, so she spoke that old fork of Russian you can only find in old immigrants, the cute granny talk. I fantacized of the movies to watch with her because she would be receptive to so many things from my culture Americans aren't, and it will be new to her too. I bought stuff one should have when inviting someone over, like packs of toothbrushes, etc. I felt the life I blocked for a whole year was returning again. When she asked about music I named old radio Maximum, got nostalgic, found this old radio show recording and listened to it just hours before she unmatched me.

The next day my second-month salary landed. Here I am, richer than I was at any point in my life except one year, yet sad and lonely.

In a few days I got my shit together, improved my pitch, and got 7 more matches. Let's see where it goes.

Then YouTube suggested me a documentary on the Strugatsky brothers, and I started reading them again. I've read The Ugly Swans and some of the early stuff. That reminded me of the time when I identified with those who could lead the changes, and it hits hard that I've forgotten that long ago and I'm unlikely to lead anything. So I'm sad again. The sadness of lazy зажравшийся human. Wish all sadness in the world was just that.

Dr. Chris Pearson, also of Southern Utah University, wrote:

text:
🧵2/3 He has also faced long-running legal and political controversies, including 2015 felony securities-fraud indictments, a 2023 Texas House impeachment (acquitted in the Senate), and a whistleblower settlement. In 2026 he defeated Sen. John Cornyn in the GOP Senate primary runoff after an endorsement from Donald Trump and now faces Democrat James Talarico.
Adam Hoffman
Hoffman, about 49 at the time of sentencing, practiced law in the Waco area (Baylor Law graduate) and lived in China Spring. He was arrested in June 2022 charged with the first-degree felony of continuous sexual abuse of a young child—his son’s friend—allegedly from 2019 to 2022, beginning when the boy was about 6 or 7. The boy later described repeated abuse and being shown pornography. The charge carried a possible sentence of 25 years to life.
McLennan County District Attorney Josh Tetens recused because Hoffman had consulted him about the case before Tetens took office. Paxton’s office then handled the prosecution. A 2025 trial ended in a hung jury (reported as 7–5 in favor of guilt). The victim declined to testify again.
The plea deal
In April 2026 Hoffman pleaded guilty to two Class A misdemeanors: indecent assault and displaying harmful material to a minor. The deal included an admission of abuse that did not specify the victim’s age, which meant he was not required to register as a sex offender in Texas. Prosecutors initially proposed very short jail time (one day in some accounts, later 30). Visiting Judge Roy Sparkman increased it to 60 days, required a five-year law-license surrender, and imposed a lifetime no-contact order. Hoffman served about 29 days due to Texas jail good-time credit and was released in late May 2026. He later moved to Nebraska, where officials required sex-offender registration. There were also reports of delays or incomplete paperwork on surrendering his Texas law license.
Paxton’s prosecutors said they offered the deal because the child would not voluntarily testify a second time and they did not want to force him; they described it as being in the victim’s interest after a mistrial. The victim’s mother later told the court she and her son forgave Hoffman. Critics across parties—including John Cornyn during the primary, James Talarico in the general-election campaign, and some Republican legislators—called the outcome a “sweetheart deal,” noting the original life-eligible felony, the short jail term, and the lack of Texas sex-offender registration. Talarico demanded release of internal “Hoffman files”; Paxton’s office rejected a public-records request. Protests occurred outside the courthouse. Snopes rated as true the core claim that Paxton’s office brokered a deal resulting in roughly 30 days served and no Texas registration.
The case remains politically salient in the 2026 Senate race. Hoffman has said little publicly beyond wanting to return home after release.

Was the first trial prosecuted aggressively?

The first trial was a full four-day jury trial in June 2025 on the original first-degree felony (continuous sexual abuse of a young child). Paxton’s office, through assistant attorneys general Brenda Cantu and Dorian Cotlar, presented the case rather than dismissing or immediately pleading it down. They called the child as a witness; he testified in detail about repeated abuse over roughly three years during sleepovers, including sexual contact, being shown pornography, and threats. They also called a detective, a physician who had examined the boy (Dr. Soo Battle), and presented digital evidence such as text messages and material from phones. In closing, one prosecutor emphasized the specificity of the boy’s account.
That’s the opposite of declining to try the case. After a hung jury they said they were prepared to retry it. The jury split 7–5 in favor of guilt after ~nine hours of deliberation (an Allen charge was given when they first reported a 6–6 deadlock). Five jurors were not convinced beyond a reasonable doubt

text:
🧵1/3  Is it common for prosecutors to offer a plea deal when the victim will not testify

Yes. It is a common reason prosecutors offer or accept reduced plea deals, especially in child sexual-abuse and other sexual-assault cases that depend heavily on the victim’s live testimony.
Most U.S. criminal cases already end in pleas rather than trials. In sexual-violence prosecutions the rate is even higher: studies of large samples have found that a large majority of resolved cases end in a plea to a lesser charge, and only a small fraction produce a conviction on the original charge. When the complaining witness—particularly a child who has already testified once—says they will not do it again, prosecutors routinely treat that as a major change in the strength of the case.
The practical reasons are straightforward:
Without the victim, many of these cases lack other strong, admissible evidence that can prove the elements of a first-degree felony beyond a reasonable doubt.
A second trial after a hung jury is not guaranteed to produce a conviction; a 7–5 split (as reported in the Hoffman trial) already showed the case was close.
Forcing a child back onto the stand can be viewed as re-traumatizing. Many prosecutors, child-protection professionals, and some judges treat avoiding that as a legitimate factor in “the best interest of the child.” Texas prosecutors and victim advocates have described this exact calculus: when a child “just can’t do it,” they try to reach a plea instead.
Prosecutors still have options other than a generous plea. They can subpoena the victim, seek a continuance, try to introduce prior statements under hearsay exceptions or forfeiture-by-wrongdoing, or dismiss and refile later. In practice they often choose not to compel a reluctant child, especially after one full trial. Offices vary: some “no-drop” policies exist in domestic-violence units, but those are less uniformly applied to child sexual-abuse cases, and even then prosecutors still weigh the realistic chance of winning.
The resulting deal can still be criticized as too lenient (short jail time, no sex-offender registration, reduced charges). That criticism is common and sometimes valid; the existence of a victim’s refusal to testify does not automatically make any particular sentence appropriate. It does, however, explain why prosecutors frequently treat a plea as the remaining viable path rather than risk an acquittal or force another round of testimony. In the Hoffman matter, Paxton’s prosecutors publicly cited exactly this combination: hung jury plus the child’s stated desire not to testify again. That rationale is consistent with how many offices handle similar situations, even when the outcome draws public and political backlash.

Tell me about Adam Hoffman and Ken Paxton

Adam Hoffman is a former Waco, Texas attorney who pleaded guilty in 2026 to reduced misdemeanor charges after originally being charged with continuous sexual abuse of a young child. Ken Paxton is the Republican Attorney General of Texas since 2015 and the GOP nominee for U.S. Senate in 2026. Their connection is a child sexual abuse case that Paxton’s office prosecuted after a local recusal; a post-mistrial plea deal drew intense criticism and became a campaign issue.
Ken Paxton
Warren Kenneth Paxton Jr. was born December 23, 1962, in Minot, North Dakota. He earned a B.A. in psychology and an M.B.A. from Baylor University and a J.D. from the University of Virginia School of Law. He practiced law, served in the Texas House (2003–2013) and Texas Senate (2013–2015), and has been Attorney General since January 2015, winning re-election in 2018 and 2022.
As AG he leads a large office handling civil litigation for the state, consumer protection, child support, and some criminal matters when local prosecutors request or recuse. He is known for frequent lawsuits against the federal government.

AI Overview
Before the biblical patriarch Jacob existed, the personal name and its linguistic roots already appeared in ancient Near Eastern and Semitic cultures. 

Ancient Semitic and Amorite Forms
Yaqub-el / Ya'qubar: In second-millennium BCE West Semitic and Amorite archives (such as those from Mari, Ebla, and old Babylonian sources), the name appears in the theophoric form Yaqub-el or Yaqubar, meaning "may [the god] El protect" or "El follows/rewards". 
Yakrub-El: In early Old Babylonian Mesopotamian texts from Terqa (near Mari), a deity or ancestral hero named Yakrub-El (translating to "the god blesses") was worshiped. 
Evolution of the Theophoric Element: Over time, the divine suffix -el ("God") was dropped or shortened in common speech, leaving the base verb form Ya'aqov (Yaqov). 

Etymology and Shift in Meaning
Original Root (ʿ-q-b): In ancient Semitic contexts, the root related to tracking, protecting, or following.
Biblical Re-interpretation: The Book of Genesis ties the name Ya'aqov to a folk etymology derived from aqev (heel), describing him being born grasping his twin brother Esau's heel and later "supplanting" him. Scholars view the shorter Jacob as a later contraction of the older Ya'aqov-el ("may God protect"). 

When Attalus, the Pontiff and King of Pergamos, died in 133BC, he bequested the Headship of the "Babylonian Priesthood" to Rome. William B. Barker in his book "Lares and Penates cracks open the codeword Pergamos as used by St. John in Revelation 2:13. He writes: "The Chaldean Magi enjoyed a long period of prosperity at Babylon. A pontiff appointed by the sovereign ruled over a college of seventy-two hierophants.... [just as the popes have 70 Cardinals] the defeated Chaldeans fled to Asia Minor, and fixed their central college at Pergamos, and too the Palladium of Babylon, the cubic stone [believed to represent Cybele or Kybele, the mother goddess] with them. Here, independent of state control, they carried on the rites of their religion, and plotted against the peace of the Persian Empire, caballing with the Greeks for that purpose."
Thus we see that the Chaldeans continued to wield political and religious influence, injecting their presence into the next world empire. When the city was later given to Rome (Rome acquired the city of Pergamos by decree of Attalus III, bequething his kingdom to the Roman Caesar), the priesthood of Pergamos moved to the new power center on the Italian peninsula.

III. The Glory of T’ang
T’ai Tsung (627–650) murdered his brothers, pushed the barbarians back, then stopped. He lowered expenses and taxes, employed honest officials, and told his ministers that clothing enough people would cut robbery better than severe laws. He emptied the jails on a promise of return; every man came back. He published Confucius in fine editions and treated foreign missionaries as guests while Europe was dark. The capital filled with traders from India and the West. 

Fifty years of relative peace produced surplus rice, silk, and spices. Silk that cost its weight in gold in Europe was ordinary dress in Chinese cities. One village near the capital employed a hundred thousand men in silk factories. Lakes held pleasure boats; harbors sent ships to the Persian Gulf. “Whoever was a man was a poet.” Emperors promoted them. 

An eighteenth-century anthology still held nearly 49,000 T’ang poems by 2,300 writers. The imperial library reached 54,000 volumes. Murdoch called it the most polished epoch the world had seen. 

Ming Huang (“the Brilliant Emperor”) ruled roughly 713–756. He wrote poetry, abolished capital punishment, levied heavy taxes, and built a college of music. At sixty he took Yang Kwei-fei, twenty-seven, former concubine of his son. 

He handed power to her relatives and ignored the state. An Lu-shan, a Tatar he had favored, revolted. The capital fell. Soldiers killed Yang before the emperor’s eyes. Thirty-six million people are said to have died in the disorder. An Lu-shan’s line collapsed in mutual murder. Ming Huang returned to ruins and died. The poetry flourished inside the wreckage. 

IV. The Banished Angel
Li Po translated a Korean war threat for Ming Huang when no one else could, after first making the examiners remove his boots. The emperor called him a banished angel. Li spent the tribute on wine. He wandered, wrote, drank with the “Six Idlers of the Bamboo Grove” and the “Eight Immortals of the Wine Cup,” and slept under the same cover as Tu Fu. He celebrated Yang, then was dismissed. War and exile followed. He joined a rebel staff, was sentenced to death, and was saved by a general who offered his own rank. Amnestied, he died; legend says he drowned trying to embrace the moon’s reflection while drunk. Thirty volumes remain. The palaces of the Chou kings vanished; the songs did not. 

V. Some Qualities of Chinese Poetry
Translation loses the characters, the vertical lines, the tones, and half the art. Chinese poetry aims at brevity: a picture in a stroke, a philosophy in a dozen lines, meaning beyond the words so the reader must finish it. It understates, avoids metaphor and passion, and prefers the thing itself. Already in Ming Huang’s day the civilization felt old; poets repeated themes and polished form. Still, every educated Chinese of later centuries knew much of it by heart. That is part of why so many of them were artists and philosophers. 

VI. Tu Fu
T’ao Ch’ien quit office rather than kow-tow for five pecks of rice a day and went to the mountains. Po Chü-i took the opposite path, rose to high office, wrote four thousand poems, and remained popular because he read them to peasants and simplified what they did not understand. Tu Fu failed the poetry examination, advertised his verses as a malaria cure, then was examined again by the emperor and appointed. He and Li Po walked hand in hand. Revolution produced his war poems: boys conscripted, villages emptied, bones of the dead, mothers weeping. He wandered destitute with his family, was rescued by a general who asked only for poetry, then rose and fell again. His children mocked him for helplessness; wind tore his roof; urchins stole his bed straw. He lost the taste for wine, turned to Buddhism, ate too much at a final banquet, and died at fifty-nine. The Chinese rank him above Li Po.

Performed during a highly restricted 48-minute cosmic window known as the Sandhikshan, it marks the exact intersection where Maha Ashtami (the 8th lunar day) ends and Maha Navami (the 9th lunar day) begins. This window comprises the last 24 minutes of Ashtami and the first 24 minutes of Navami.

The profound significance of Sandhi Puja lies in the Devi Mahatmyam (Chandi Path). According to scriptures, during the great war against Mahishasura, his formidable generals, Chanda and Munda, treacherously attacked Goddess Durga from behind.

Infuriated by this violation of battle codes, the Goddess’s visage turned dark blue with cosmic rage. At the exact juncture of Ashtami and Navami, She opened Her Third Eye, and from Her forehead manifested Ma Chamunda (a fierce, blood-curdling avatar akin to Goddess Kali). Ma Chamunda intercepted the demons and decapitated them at this very moment. Thus, Sandhi Puja is entirely dedicated to invoking the raw, victorious, and protective energy of Goddess Chamunda.

✨Key Rituals & Elements:-
Because the Sandhikshan is exceptionally brief, the grand arrangements must be completed well in advance. The baseline rituals require absolute precision:
108 Earthen Lamps (Diyas): Devotees light exactly 108 ghee or oil lamps. This represents the piercing of spiritual darkness with divine light.
108 Lotus Flowers: 108 lotuses (or red hibiscus flowers if lotuses are unavailable) are offered one by one to the deity.
108 Bel Leaves: A garland or loose bundle of 108 wood-apple (bilva) leaves is offered.
Grand Bhog (Naivedya): Offerings of raw rice, large assortments of fruits (preferring red fruits), and traditional sweets.
The Soundscape: As the ritual peaks, the atmosphere is violently charged with the rhythmic, thunderous beats of the Dhak (drums), blowing of conch shells, and intense chanting of the Chandi Path.

✨The Hidden Esoteric ("Secret") Aspects:-
Beyond the public celebration, Sandhi Puja holds profound esoteric secrets in Hindu Tantra and spiritual practice:

1. The Gateway of Zero-Time (The Junction Effect)
In spiritual lore, any Sandhi (junction)—like dawn, dusk, or the meeting of two lunar phases—is a crack in mundane time where the veil between the physical world and the cosmic divine is thinnest. During these 48 minutes, the universe transitions from the calm, meditative energy of Maha Gauri (Ashtami) to the absolute spiritual fulfillment of Siddhidhatri (Navami). It is believed that prayers, intentions, or wishes made with pure focus during this transition are instantly heard and fulfilled by the universe.

2. The Internal "Bali" (Sacrifice)
Historically, royal households and ancient tantric shrines performed animal sacrifices (balidan) during Sandhi Puja to appease the fierce Goddess. Today, this has been widely replaced by symbolic sacrifice (Pratikriti Bali) using pumpkins, sugarcane, cucumbers, or bananas smeared with vermilion.
The Esoteric Secret: The external vegetable sacrifice is actually a metaphor for sacrificing one's inner demons. The pumpkin represents ego (Ahankara), the sugarcane represents lust/desire (Kama), and the cucumber represents greed. Splitting them in a single strike signifies the total eradication of our lower nature by Ma Chamunda’s sword.

3. Secret Sadhana & Cleansing
Tantric practitioners and dedicated devotees use this window for severe mental housecleaning. It is considered the ultimate 48 minutes to perform Gupt Sadhana (secret meditation). Devotees sit in silence, maintaining a strict Nirjala Vrat (waterless fast), and mentally throw their deepest fears, generational traumas, toxic habits, and spiritual blockages into the fierce, devouring fire of Ma Chamunda's energy.

text:
On matters of Maury County, Tennessee — 

Tomorrow night, the Maury County Commission will consider an Ethics Disclosure Resolution which states that County Commissioners “should” disclose certain personal interests in County business; while adding:

“Whenever practical, the disclosure should also be reflected in the meeting minutes.”

Should.  Whenever practical.

They could make the disclosures mandatory.  Instead, they propose encouragement; going so far as to make the recording of the disclosures in the meeting minutes to be conditional as well.

After months of discussion, including input from former Commissioner Bridenbaugh, as multiple ethics complaints were pending against him, this proposal adds no mandatory disclosure duty, no enforcement process for its new expectations, and no stated consequences for ignoring them.

Such fickle language looks more like ceremonial grandstanding than it does meaningful reform.

Meanwhile, citizens continue to wait for answers about actual County decisions that matter.

At the most recent Safety Committee meeting, I raised specific concerns about the Santa Fe fire-station land purchase, including the roughly $163,000 paid per acre, whether the appraisal satisfied the purchase contingency, listings used as appraisal comparables, and professional relationships surrounding the transaction.

Eight current Commissioners voted for both that purchase and Robert Caldiraro’s Planning Commission appointment.  After I publicly raised concerns about both decisions, not one of those eight individuals contacted me to discuss them.

Caldiraro has since resigned from the County’s appointment.  However, the need for an audit of developments that may have bypassed required planning review remains.  And while I’m working on my own audit of such properties, determining the extent of the County’s failures should not fall to a citizen or the people harmed by them.

Citizens have already spent more than a year, and had to hire counsel at their own expense, just to get the County to concede it misapplied its own requirements for subdivision review.

As a final note, I appreciate the Commissioners, outside of the aforementioned group, who have reached out, asked questions, and sought more information.  That is the kind of engagement the citizens of Maury County deserve.  

In contrast, one Commissioner among the group with a rubber stamp, has made clear on his social media account recently that he represents 120,000 people, not six people (in presumably targeting those who would dare speak up as to the way in which he has conducted business).  

The Commissioner made the commentary after a meeting in which exactly zero members of the public spoke in support of his vote; and not one reference was made to support for the measure having come from other members of the public.

That Commissioner, and others, have offered no response whatsoever to the issues raised and the waste of taxpayer dollars aided and abetted by a County Commission who seems hellbent on shutting down public discourse on such matters.

I rarely ask the public to attend meetings of this nature, but I do believe it’s important to have a showing that there are more than six people in Maury County who care about accountability.

Your attendance would be welcomed at the Maury County Commission meeting tomorrow night on Monday, October 19th at 6:30 pm.

You do not have to speak.  Your presence shows citizens expect mandatory standards, answers to documented concerns, and lawful, meaningful consequences when rules have been violated.

Public trust should not depend on what our elected officials find “practical”.

“Inside the Media Feud Between Donald Trump and Taylor Swift.”

The problem is that I've been writing about Scooter Braun, Ari Emanuel, Kanye West, and the entertainment industry as separate subjects, then occasionally returning to Taylor Swift and Donald Trump.

The media feud has to drive the entire narrative. Every paragraph needs to show how a person, transaction, event, or date contributes to the rivalry between them. The behind-the-scenes characters enter only when their actions illuminate that rivalry.

Here's how that changes the writing.

Inside the Media Feud Between Donald Trump and Taylor Swift

On July 3, 2026, Taylor Swift married Travis Kelce at Madison Square Garden while Donald Trump addressed the nation from Mount Rushmore. It was an extraordinary collision of two American media spectacles, made more remarkable by the fact that Trump had spent years publicly criticizing Swift. Within hours, the White House was using imagery from her wedding announcement to promote the president.

The White House's official X account replaced the Garden's “JusT&T Married” announcement with “Trump is your president.” Swift's wedding had become another episode in a media feud that began during Trump's first presidency and had since spread through the music business, Hollywood representation, political fundraising and professional sports.

The feud's business roots reach back to 2015, when Trump was still a client of Hollywood's powerful talent-agency establishment. On September 14, Ari Emanuel's WME-IMG bought Trump's Miss Universe Organization, three months after Trump announced his presidential campaign. Emanuel had previously represented Trump in television negotiations. Their relationship illustrates how closely Trump's political rise was tied to the executives who had helped make him an entertainment personality.

Taylor was navigating the same industry from a different position. Her career depended on maintaining ownership and control over her music, publicity and relationship with fans. One of the executives who would eventually challenge that control, Scooter Braun, had already entered Trump's political world. On August 6, 2015, Braun hosted a Hillary Clinton fundraiser attended by Kim Kardashian and Kanye West, on the same evening Trump participated in the first Republican presidential debate.

The next summer, the feud's future supporting players were making competing headlines. On July 17, 2016, Kardashian released edited excerpts of Taylor's telephone conversation with Kanye West about Famous, producing a massive celebrity controversy. Trump's Republican National Convention opened the following day. Braun, who managed Kanye, was simultaneously involved in discussions surrounding a reported $5 million offer for Justin Bieber to perform at a convention-associated event. Braun opposed the performance.

On December 13, 2016, Kanye visited President-elect Trump at Trump Tower. The man at the center of Taylor's biggest celebrity dispute was now standing beside Donald in front of the national press corps, while Braun remained Kanye's manager. The intersecting relationships placed Trump's political celebrity and Taylor's entertainment controversies within a recognizable network of Hollywood representation.

Their direct public feud began on October 7, 2018, when Taylor endorsed Democratic candidates in Tennessee. Donald responded the next day that he liked her music about 25 percent less. But their disagreement would soon acquire an additional business dimension because of Braun's purchase of Taylor's recordings.

On June 30, 2019, Braun acquired Big Machine Label Group, including the masters of Taylor's first six albums. Taylor publicly opposed the transaction and began a prolonged struggle to regain control of her work. Only weeks later, Braun hosted a fundraiser for Kamala Harris, a presidential candidate who would eventually become the central figure in Taylor and Donald's 2024 confrontation.

That connection became particularly consequential on September 10, 2024. Taylor endorsed Harris after her debate with Donald. Five days later, Trump declared on Truth Social that he hated Taylor Swift. Braun immediately responded by invoking her hit Shake It Off and supporting Harris. The executive who had fought Taylor over her music catalog was now participating in the media battle between Taylor and Donald—and taking Taylor's side against him.

By then, Trump had also attempted to associate Taylor's commercial popularity with his own political fortunes. In February 2024, he suggested that she owed him loyalty because he had signed the Music Modernization Act. On August 18, he circulated AI-generated imagery falsely implying she supported his campaign. Her September endorsement explicitly referenced the misleading images, turning his attempt to appropriate her celebrity into part of her explanation for publicly supporting Harris.

The feud then moved onto professional football's biggest stage. Taylor's relationship with Kelce had made her a recurring presence in NFL broadcasts, bringing entertainment audiences into football coverage. Trump, whose longtime relationship with Dana White and Ari Emanuel connected him to UFC's sports-entertainment business, increasingly appeared at major sporting events himself.

On February 9, 2025, both attended Super Bowl LIX. When Taylor was booed by some fans, Trump amplified the reaction online. The football broadcast and subsequent social-media coverage had provided another episode in their continuing confrontation.

Then, on May 16, Trump attacked Taylor's commercial popularity again, suggesting she had lost cultural appeal since he announced that he hated her. On May 30, she announced the purchase of her original master recordings from Shamrock Capital, resolving the central ownership dispute that began with Braun's 2019 acquisition.

Their worlds came together again through Madison Square Garden, which had hosted Trump's October 27, 2024 campaign rally. On July 3, 2026, that same arena hosted Taylor's wedding to Kelce. The occasion brought music, sports, Hollywood and celebrity publicity together in a lavishly controlled production. Meanwhile, Trump was appearing at Mount Rushmore for a presidential Independence Day celebration.

The White House's decision to parody Taylor's wedding announcement demonstrated how thoroughly her private milestones had become part of Trump's media universe. The relationship had progressed from Trump's 2018 joke about liking her music less, through political endorsements and disputes over celebrity influence, to his administration using the visual identity of her wedding as material for its own public communications.

Behind that progression were people whose professional and financial relationships mattered: Emanuel, who had represented Trump and acquired his pageant business; Braun, who managed Kanye West, acquired Taylor's masters and supported Harris; Kanye, who was simultaneously connected to Taylor's celebrity disputes and Trump's political orbit; and James Dolan, whose Madison Square Garden hosted major events for both.

The central history is not simply that Taylor Swift and Donald Trump disagree politically. It is that their public antagonism has repeatedly drawn the business machinery surrounding their careers into the same news cycles. Entertainment executives, record-company owners, campaign professionals, sports broadcasters and social-media teams have all participated in the distribution and amplification of the feud.

By July 3, 2026, the rivalry had reached a point where even the announcement of Taylor Swift's marriage could become material for Donald Trump's White House. text:
My Faith Is Not a Party Pledge

Today’s Gospel reminds me to give Caesar what belongs to Caesar and God what belongs to God. My conscience does not belong to a political party. And my children and their faith should never be defined by the Government. 

My Catholic faith teaches me that every person has dignity. We are individuals created in God’s image, each with value that no government, political label, or circumstance can erase. We are called to propose our faith not impose our faith. 

If we say we are pro-life, that must mean from the womb to the tomb. The unborn child. The struggling mother. The child with disabilities. A child in the classroom. The elderly person who needs care. ALL LIFE should be valued.

That responsibility does not end at birth. It includes protecting children as they grow, respecting their privacy, and ensuring they receive an education that helps them think independently and reach their potential. So they have an equal opportunity at success in life, not equal outcomes but equal opportunities. 

Gina’s personal choice to choose life for her child matters to me. It deserves acknowledgment in a conversation too often reduced to accusations and party labels. That choice does not erase our policy disagreements. But those disagreements do not erase her humanity, either.

I have never voted Democrat in my life. This election, I am voting for Gina Hinojosa for governor.

I know her. I have worked with her. I have watched her listen, ask difficult questions, and challenge people in both parties.

And I have spent years researching and speaking out about the direction of Texas education under Greg Abbott, Dan Patrick and Mike Morath. I cannot ignore my concerns about state control, government behavioral assessments, taxpayer spending, and children’s data simply because he has an R beside his name.

Our children are NOT human capital. Their data is NOT a commodity. Their worth comes from God not the government. 

Supporting Gina does not mean I endorse every position she holds or the Democrat party platform. It means I have weighed the candidates and believe she offers a better direction for our children, their schools and our state. I will hold her accountable, too.

My faith calls me to value every life, seek truth, and examine my own loyalties.

From the womb to the tomb, human dignity must mean more than a campaign slogan.

text:
The 3 Most Famous Bodies on Mount Everest: Horrifying Stories from 8,000 Meters
Mount Everest is the highest mountain on Earth, standing at 8,849 meters (29,032 feet) above sea level. For many climbers, reaching its summit represents the ultimate achievement. But above 8,000 meters lies the deadly region known as the Death Zone, where oxygen levels are dangerously low, temperatures can plunge dramatically, and even the simplest movement can become exhausting.
When climbers die at these extreme altitudes, recovering their bodies can be nearly impossible. The danger, physical demands, unpredictable weather, and enormous cost mean that some remains stay on the mountain for years.
Among the most widely known stories are those of three climbers whose bodies became grim landmarks along Everest's routes: Green Boots, Francys Arsentiev, and Hannelore Schmatz. Their tragic experiences reveal the terrifying reality of high-altitude mountaineering.
1. Green Boots: The Climber Who Became a Landmark
For decades, climbers ascending Everest's northeastern route encountered a body lying inside a small rocky alcove at approximately 8,500 meters. The bright green mountaineering boots made the body recognizable, earning the climber the nickname Green Boots.
The body was long widely believed to belong to Tsewang Paljor, an Indian climber who died during the disastrous 1996 climbing season. However, reports in 2026 identified the remains as those of another Indian climber, Dorje Morup, who also died during the same expedition disaster. The identification highlights how difficult it has been to establish the identities of climbers lost on Everest.
In May 1996, members of an Indo-Tibetan Border Police expedition encountered severe conditions during their attempt to reach the summit. A powerful storm struck the mountain, and several climbers lost their lives.
Morup's body remained near the northeastern route, where it became a familiar reference point for climbers attempting to reach the summit. The rocky alcove offered some shelter from the wind, making it a recognizable feature of the route.
Over the years, the nickname became more familiar than the climber's identity. What had once been a person with a family, ambitions, and dreams became a landmark on one of the world's most dangerous mountains.
The story also became connected to the controversial death of British climber David Sharp in 2006, who was found dying near the same area. His case sparked intense debate about the responsibilities of climbers who encounter someone in distress at extreme altitude.
Green Boots' story is a painful reminder that even experienced mountaineers can be overwhelmed by Everest's unforgiving conditions.
2. Francys Arsentiev: The Woman Known as Sleeping Beauty
Francys Arsentiev was an American mountaineer who achieved an extraordinary milestone in May 1998. She became the first American woman to reach the summit of Mount Everest without supplemental bottled oxygen.
But the achievement turned into a tragedy during the descent.
Climbing Everest without supplemental oxygen places enormous stress on the human body. At extreme altitude, the brain and muscles receive less oxygen, judgment can deteriorate, and exhaustion can become overwhelming.
Francys and her husband, Russian climber Sergei Arsentiev, attempted to descend after reaching the summit. During the descent, the pair became separated. Sergei eventually went back up the mountain in an attempt to find his wife, but he never returned.
Other climbers encountered Francys in critical condition. Accounts of the incident describe attempts to help her, but the combination of altitude, exhaustion, and dangerous conditions made a rescue extraordinarily difficult.
Despite the efforts of climbers who came across her, Francys died on Everest in May 1998. Her husband also died during the tragedy.
Her body remained on the mountain for years and became known by the nickname “Sleeping Beauty,” a name inspired by the appearance of her remains.
In 2007, an expedition led by climber Ian Woodall made an effort to move her remains out of view from the main climbing route, offering a measure of dignity and privacy.
Her story remains one of Everest's most heartbreaking tragedies. It illustrates how reaching the summit does not guarantee survival, because the descent can be just as dangerous as the climb itself.
3. Hannelore Schmatz: The German Mountaineer Who Never Returned
Hannelore Schmatz was a German mountaineer who reached the summit of Mount Everest in October 1979 alongside her husband, Gerhard Schmatz, during an expedition.
Reaching the top was a remarkable achievement, but the descent became fatal.
At an altitude of approximately 8,200 meters, Hannelore became exhausted while returning from the summit. Conditions in the Death Zone are extraordinarily harsh, and climbers who remain there too long face a rapidly increasing risk of hypothermia, exhaustion, and altitude-related illness.
Hannelore eventually collapsed and died during the descent.
Her body remained on the mountain for years, becoming one of the most recognizable sights along the southern climbing route. Climbers reported seeing her remains near the trail, where the extreme cold helped preserve them.
Her tragic story became widely known among mountaineers because it showed how a successful summit attempt could still end in death.
Recovering her body was extremely dangerous. At such elevations, moving a deceased climber requires considerable manpower, specialized equipment, and favorable weather. Those attempting a recovery risk their own lives.
Over time, strong winds and the mountain's harsh conditions altered the location of her remains. Her body was eventually believed to have been blown farther down the mountain.
Hannelore's story remains a sobering example of the dangers climbers face even after achieving their greatest goal.
Why Are Bodies Left on Mount Everest?
The presence of human remains on Everest is not simply a matter of neglect. At altitudes above 8,000 meters, climbers operate under extreme physical limitations.
Recovering a body can require multiple rescuers, specialized equipment, ropes, and suitable weather. A single recovery operation can expose several people to the same dangers that killed the original climber.
Helicopter rescue and transport are also severely limited at these elevations. Consequently, families and expedition teams sometimes face the painful reality that bringing a loved one home may be too dangerous.
Some bodies have therefore remained on the mountain for years, while others have been moved, concealed, or recovered through difficult expeditions.
The Human Cost of Climbing Everest
The stories of Green Boots, Francys Arsentiev, and Hannelore Schmatz are more than frightening tales about frozen bodies. They are stories about human ambition, determination, loss, and the limits of survival.
Each climber began their journey with a personal dream. Yet Everest's extreme altitude and unpredictable weather transformed their journeys into tragedies that continue to be remembered decades later.
Their stories also raise difficult ethical questions. When climbers encounter someone in distress, they may have to choose between attempting a rescue and protecting their own lives. At extreme altitude, helping another person can sometimes put multiple lives at risk.
Mount Everest continues to attract climbers from around the world, but its beauty can hide extraordinary dangers. Reaching the summit is only half the journey, and returning safely is the ultimate measure of success.
The mountain does not remember names, achievements, or ambitions. But the stories of those who never returned remind us that behind every landmark on Everest was once a human being with a life, a family, and a dream.

text:
Welcome, gentle reader, to this fair and classic film noir public domain treasure! Prithee draw nigh and behold Great Expectations (1946), that wondrous cinematic rendering of Master Charles Dickens’ immortal tale. Here doth the black-and-white magic of the silver screen revive the Kentish marshes, the broken heart of Satis House, and the rise and fall of young Pip’s fortunes—all freely offered unto the world, unbound by modern copyright’s chains.

Synopsis
In the bleak marshes of Kent, the orphaned lad Pip (scarce more than a child) doth aid a fearsome escaped convict and is thereafter summoned to the decaying grandeur of Miss Havisham’s mansion, where the cold and beautiful Estella is trained to break hearts. Years later, a mysterious benefactor elevates Pip to the station of a London gentleman. Yet expectations great prove fragile, and the truth of his fortune, his love, and his own soul must be confronted amid fog, fire, and the Thames.

The Cast (in the principal roles)
John Mills as Pip (grown)
Anthony Wager as Young Pip
Valerie Hobson as Estella
Jean Simmons as Young Estella
Bernard Miles as the good-hearted blacksmith Joe Gargery
Francis L. Sullivan as the formidable lawyer Mr. Jaggers
Finlay Currie as Abel Magwitch
Martita Hunt as the spectral Miss Havisham
Alec Guinness as Herbert Pocket
Ivor Barnard as Wemmick
Freda Jackson as Mrs. Joe
And supporting players including Hay Petrie, Torin Thatcher, Eileen Erskine, and others of note.

The Crew
Directed by the masterful David Lean. Screenplay adapted by David Lean, Ronald Neame, Anthony Havelock-Allan, Kay Walsh, and Cecil McGivern, from Dickens’ novel. Produced by Ronald Neame and Anthony Havelock-Allan for Cineguild. Cinematography by Guy Green (with Robert Krasker upon the opening sequences). Production design by John Bryan; art direction by Wilfred Shingleton. Edited by Jack Harris. Music by Walter Goehr.

Locations
Much was wrought at Denham Studios in Buckinghamshire. Exteriors upon the wild St Mary’s Marshes and Isle of Grain in Kent (the forge and marshes), the River Medway, Chatham Dockyard, and the real St Paul’s Cathedral and churchyard in London. Satis House was a studio recreation inspired by Restoration House in Rochester.

Distinctions arise in every society. Even among people who look the same and share the same broad culture, groups still mark differences by behavior, belief, status, speech, or custom. The Bible records the same pattern. Genesis 4:15 says the Lord set a mark upon Cain. Readers later treated that mark as a lasting distinction. If a court treats the description of consequences in 2 Nephi as inherently racist, the same reading would have to be applied to the biblical mark and to other places where God distinguishes groups according to their choices.

The Bible also instructs servants to serve their masters well, with singleness of heart, as unto Christ, while masters are to treat those under them justly, knowing they themselves have a Master in heaven (Ephesians 6:5–9; Colossians 3:22–4:1). At the same time the gospel proclaims liberty in Christ and declares that all are alike unto God, bond and free, black and white (Galatians 3:28; 2 Nephi 26:33). Both teachings stand together. Ordered roles under divine law coexist with the offer of spiritual freedom and equal standing before God.

Since Latter-day Saints accept the Bible as the word of God alongside the Book of Mormon, any court examining this language will have to consider the biblical record as well. It will be interesting to see how the courts treat texts that both affirm liberty and instruct servants and masters to keep God’s laws. The underlying question remains whether describing the visible consequences of rebellion against God necessarily denies the equal natural rights of the people involved. I do not see how it does.

text:
I was shooting heroin and reading “The Fountainhead” in the front seat of my privately owned police cruiser when a call came in. I put a quarter in the radio to activate it. It was the chief.

“Bad news, detective. We got a situation.”

“What? Is the mayor trying to ban trans fats again?”

“Worse. Somebody just stole four hundred and forty-seven million dollars’ worth of bitcoins.”

The heroin needle practically fell out of my arm. “What kind of monster would do something like that? Bitcoins are the ultimate currency: virtual, anonymous, stateless. They represent true economic freedom, not subject to arbitrary manipulation by any government. Do we have any leads?”

“Not yet. But mark my words: we’re going to figure out who did this and we’re going to take them down … provided someone pays us a fair market rate to do so.”

“Easy, chief,” I said. “Any rate the market offers is, by definition, fair.”

He laughed. “That’s why you’re the best I got, Lisowski. Now you get out there and find those bitcoins.”

“Don’t worry,” I said. “I’m on it.”

I put a quarter in the siren. Ten minutes later, I was on the scene. It was a normal office building, strangled on all sides by public sidewalks. I hopped over them and went inside.

“Home Depot™ Presents the Police!®” I said, flashing my badge and my gun and a small picture of Ron Paul. “Nobody move unless you want to!” They didn’t.

“Now, which one of you punks is going to pay me to investigate this crime?” No one spoke up.

“Come on,” I said. “Don’t you all understand that the protection of private property is the foundation of all personal liberty?”

It didn’t seem like they did.

“Seriously, guys. Without a strong economic motivator, I’m just going to stand here and not solve this case. Cash is fine, but I prefer being paid in gold bullion or autographed Penn Jillette posters.”

Nothing. These people were stonewalling me. It almost seemed like they didn’t care that a fortune in computer money invented to buy drugs was missing.

I figured I could wait them out. I lit several cigarettes indoors. A pregnant lady coughed, and I told her that secondhand smoke is a myth. Just then, a man in glasses made a break for it.

“Subway™ Eat Fresh and Freeze, Scumbag!®” I yelled.

Too late. He was already out the front door. I went after him.

“Stop right there!” I yelled as I ran. He was faster than me because I always try to avoid stepping on public sidewalks. Our country needs a private-sidewalk voucher system, but, thanks to the incestuous interplay between our corrupt federal government and the public-sidewalk lobby, it will never happen.

I was losing him. “Listen, I’ll pay you to stop!” I yelled. “What would you consider an appropriate price point for stopping? I’ll offer you a thirteenth of an ounce of gold and a gently worn ‘Bob Barr ‘08’ extra-large long-sleeved men’s T-shirt!”

He turned. In his hand was a revolver that the Constitution said he had every right to own. He fired at me and missed. I pulled my own gun, put a quarter in it, and fired back. The bullet lodged in a U.S.P.S. mailbox less than a foot from his head. I shot the mailbox again, on purpose.

“All right, all right!” the man yelled, throwing down his weapon. “I give up, cop! I confess: I took the bitcoins.”

“Why’d you do it?” I asked, as I slapped a pair of Oikos™ Greek Yogurt Presents Handcuffs® on the guy.

“Because I was afraid.”

“Afraid?”

“Afraid of an economic future free from the pernicious meddling of central bankers,” he said. “I’m a central banker.”

I wanted to coldcock the guy. Years ago, a central banker killed my partner. Instead, I shook my head.

“Let this be a message to all your central-banker friends out on the street,” I said. “No matter how many bitcoins you steal, you’ll never take away the dream of an open society based on the principles of personal and economic freedom.”

He nodded, because he knew I was right. Then he swiped his credit card to pay me for arresting him.

text:
You said “prove me wrong,” then delivered… nothing. Zero facts, zero argument, zero receipts—just the online equivalent of an #AntifaWhackANut screaming “full of shit” in someone’s face while contributing absolutely nothing to the discussion. Classic.
Meanwhile, California is doing the Palisades sequel in real time.
Norte Fire (Orange County, Oct 16): ~570 acres, 6–7 homes damaged or destroyed in San Clemente/San Juan Capistrano neighborhoods, ~16,000 people under evacuation orders at the peak, all driven by the season’s first serious Santa Ana event. Bryson Fire near Malibu was burning at the same time. Residents had minutes to get out as flames hit houses.
This is 21+ months after the Palisades Fire wiped out ~6,800 structures and killed 12. Newsom’s own commissioned UL Research Institute report (released earlier this month) documented the same pattern of failures: delayed evacuation alerts (some residents got warnings 40–90 minutes after homes were already burning), communication breakdowns between agencies, LAFD underestimating risk and not holding crews over, and systemic gaps that left the response overwhelmed.
The Santa Ynez Reservoir—empty during Palisades because of cover repairs—was still offline/nearly empty heading into this red-flag event. LADWP only began refilling it in early October after a new cover; a water-main break then delayed it further. Nearly two years later and the same high-elevation water storage issue is unresolved while winds hit again. Critics (including local officials) have repeatedly flagged brush and fuels management shortfalls; Newsom’s post-Palisades “fast-track” promises produced completed work on a tiny fraction of the acres announced.
And where was the governor while homes burned and people fled? In New Hampshire, campaigning for 2028, posting about “fired-up crowds” and taking the country back. California got the press release and the FEMA Fire Management Assistance Grant (75% reimbursement on suppression costs). That’s not leadership—that’s damage control from out of state.
Palisades taught that wind-driven urban-interface fires expose every weak link: water system capacity that can’t keep up with simultaneous structure fires, delayed warnings, inadequate prepositioning relative to known risk, and brush/fuels left to dry out. Norte showed they still haven’t fixed the fundamentals. Homes lost, people evacuated, same playbook.
You offered no counter-facts. Just volume.  California’s families don’t need more tweets attacking Trump—they need a governor who treats the lessons from the last catastrophe as more urgent than the next primary state.
