text:
Start here.

A war-band can take a peninsula and still not own its own story. Muhammad died in Medina in June 632. Within a generation his men were not reciting one fixed text. According to the Sunni canon itself—Sahih al-Bukhari 4987 and 5102—Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, campaigning in Armenia and Azerbaijan under the third caliph, Uthman ibn Affan (r. 644–656), heard Syrian and Iraqi soldiers accusing one another over variant readings of the Qur’an and feared schism. Uthman ordered Zayd ibn Thabit and a small committee to produce one official recension from the sheets already gathered under Abu Bakr after the battle of Yamamah (c. 632–633), sent copies to the main garrison cities, and commanded that other written collections be burned. That is not how a father handles truth. That is how a commander handles a riot in camp. The man of the raid had offered fighting men what fighting men already priced—women, spoil, rank, a paradise with the smell of victory on it—and he got his army: Hijrah 622, Badr 624, the taking of Mecca in 630, a community armed enough that, after 632, it walked out of Arabia and broke the near frontiers of Byzantium and Ctesiphon. He did not get control of the wording. The sword can gather a host. It cannot keep ten mouths from rewriting the banner. When the banner starts a fight, the caliph does not repent. He lights a fire under the other pages (Bukhari 4987).

That is the method. Feed the pack. Win the ground. When the story cracks, burn the variants. A hunter plates the hunger. He does not remake it.

Now the other table.

The gospel is still the worst product in the shop. No one designing customers writes it. Someone who wants sons writes it. Soft men swollen with appetite will always walk to the louder stall. That walk is not evidence. It is the x-ray. And it leaves Jesus where He stands: above the stall, the legion, and every cheap replacement—worthy, because He refused to purchase us with our vice. He paid in blood.

God is not recruiting buyers. He is calling children home.

Jesus does not bait Jew or Greek with their favorite dish. He orders both to drop the plate.

The Jew wanted a war-crown: Rome thrown off, Zion armed, a Messiah who wins like Caesar. Jesus answers with timber and nails, under Pontius Pilate, c. 30–33. “My kingdom is not of this world” (John 18:36). Come back to the Father. Receive a name. “To all who received Him, He gave the right to become children of God” (John 1:12).

The Gentile wanted the old night: the body as shrine, the feast that never closes, the rot Paul names in the streets around the churches (Romans 1; 1 Corinthians 5–6). Jesus answers with a cut. Stop staring. Tear out the eye (Matthew 5:27–32). One covenant bed. Rule the flesh. Then live as a son, not as a stomach.

He does not toss steak to the wolf. He puts bread in a mouth that only knew raw meat—and then dies and rises so the mouth can say Abba. No harem as wages. Adoption. The Lamb dies for the enemy. The stone rolls.

Muhammad runs the opposite shop. He wanted a host and he bought one with the inventory the host already priced: raids for caravan wealth after 622, plural marriage written into law, captives as a lawful yield of war. That raises banners. It does not raise sons of God. And when the inventory of words would not sit still, Uthman, about 650–653, burned the extras. Army first. Canon by bonfire second.

Look at what grows, without perfume. Where Christ’s gospel actually entered—not the costume of Christ, the command of Christ—even under crooked kings, a strange orchard appeared: the weak life counts, the child is not a clan chip only, the woman is not a share of loot, letters and universities sprout because a soul is addressed by God and must learn to answer. Cathedral schools and the medieval universitas—Bologna (1088), Paris (c. 1150), Oxford (c. 1096)—did not grow from a tent of captives. They grew from a Cross and from “let the little children come to Me” (Mark 10:14).

A creed built to please the raider will not pause and see woman and child as the image of God. It will see them as cargo—flesh, hush, wall. Useful falsehood, sanctified war, the killing of the holdout, poverty called fate: that is not bad weather on the map. That is what you plant when desire wears a scabbard.

If truth were the average male wish, heaven would be unemployed. We already know the wish: more body, more force, more alibi. That wish is the clay of this century—in the old paganism that still rides under a prophet’s name, and in the new ideologies that spit on the church. Both want a homemade god. One names it caliphate. One names it State. Both say the vote of man is the verdict of right. That sentence is not faith. It is apostasy with a flag.

The hunter blesses the pulse. The Father breaks it and names it child. That is why the gospel still will not sell to synagogue or forum. And that is why Jesus still has no rival: He would rather lose the crowd than nurse the fever. He lost the crowd. He kept the empty tomb. He kept the way back to the Father.

text:
October 19 is a strong date for people quietly getting out of things.

In 1469, Isabella of Castile and Ferdinand of Aragon married in Valladolid, Ferdinand having crossed Castile disguised as a servant. As second cousins they needed papal permission, and were duly handed a bull from Pius II. Small detail: Pius II had died in 1464. The marriage held anyway, and so, eventually, did Spain.

In 1745, Jonathan Swift died in Dublin and left most of his fortune, about £12,000, to found a hospital for the mentally ill. It still operates. A satirist with a sincere streak, which he would have hated anyone mentioning.

In 1781, the British army surrendered at Yorktown. Cornwallis skipped the ceremony, claiming illness. His deputy Charles O'Hara offered his sword to Rochambeau, who pointed to Washington, who pointed to Benjamin Lincoln. Even the hand-off was passed down the line.

In 1943, a Rutgers PhD student named Albert Schatz isolated streptomycin, the first antibiotic that worked against tuberculosis. His supervisor Selman Waksman got the 1952 Nobel alone. Schatz had to go to court to be recognized as co-discoverer.

And in 1987, Black Monday: the Dow fell 508 points, 22.6 percent, still its worst single day in percentage terms. Nobody claimed illness, though many surely felt it.

Which of these deserves a proper film: the forged wedding permit or the student who had to sue for his own discovery?

🔴WAR ON TERRORISM: IRAN 🇮🇷🔴/Israel Hayom/

Another Iran round is inevitable, IDF chief of staff believes

Eight days before Israelis head to the polls, the IDF is on high alert for possible security developments, as some in the political leadership hint the military could strike Iran first for political reasons.

by Lilach Shoval 

Eight days before the election, the IDF is on especially high alert for possible security developments.

As of now, senior officials say there is no concrete intelligence pointing to rising tensions.

Still, the defense establishment's biggest concern is that Iran might conclude Israel and the US will again try to catch Tehran off guard under cover of the election.

In such a scenario, the Iranians might try to seize the initiative this time, striking first in the belief that whoever moves first usually gains the upper hand.

The problem is that some in the political leadership may be trying to drop hints that Israel could strike first, for political reasons, heightening the risk of exactly that kind of Iranian miscalculation.

This is despite the fact that, according to senior defense officials, there is no urgent need to attack or take initiated action in the days leading up to the election.

Still, it's important to stress that top IDF brass emphasize the Iranian threat is far from over, and the chief of staff believes Israel will have to return to fighting at some stage.

When asked whether a return to fighting must happen before the election, senior officers say no.

Quite the opposite, in fact. Military leaders believe the top priority in the coming days, beyond preparing for surprises and unforeseen security developments, is ensuring stability and allowing the election to take place on schedule, as part of Israel's democratic process.

Reports claiming the Americans asked Israel to act alone, or that Israel is considering acting alone against Iran, should be treated with a great deal of skepticism, though Israel is also preparing for the possibility that it will be forced to go it alone if all other options run out.

It's worth noting that the relationship between the chief of staff, Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir, and his counterpart, the commander of CENTCOM, Admiral Brad Cooper, is strong, as are the ties between Israeli and American officers more broadly, which grew significantly closer during preparations for Operation Roaring Lion, during the operation itself, and afterward as well.

The working assumption is that if Israel returns to fighting, it will do so alongside the US. This is where the American calculation comes into play.

The last thing President Donald Trump needs or wants is to head into the midterm elections in the middle of an active war with Iran, with oil prices climbing.

But Iran isn't the only volatile front these days. As we saw this past weekend, Judea and Samaria are on the verge of erupting, with the army, police and Shin Bet failing, perhaps because they aren't trying hard enough, to rein in the chaos caused by hundreds of right-wing extremists who have been relentlessly attacking Palestinians during the olive harvest.

Along the way, they also managed over the weekend to harm an American press photographer and foreign diplomats from Poland, Belgium and France. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, for his part, offered only a mild condemnation and a statement that the matter should be reviewed, language that hasn't done much to rein in events on the ground. To that, of course, must be added the constant tension in Lebanon and Gaza.

Either way, Chief of Staff Zamir and the entire IDF top brass have an important role to play in the coming days in maintaining security stability that will allow the election to proceed on schedule.

But there is no doubt the security challenges are far from over, and whatever government comes next will have to confront them, and sooner rather than later.

#21 Rivers Knight - Freshman from Durham, North Carolina

Listed Height and Weight: 6'10, 220 lbs

text:
October 12–18, 2026

Bitcoin had a weak week. It fell to about $79,740 on Oct 15, its lowest since Sept 18, and closed Sunday near $82,020, down 2.0% from the Sunday before [1]. Spot ETFs lost a net $228.4M, a second straight losing week [2].

Inflation ran hot, and Bitcoin tracked stocks. Consumer prices rose 3.7% in the year to September and producer prices 1.3% in the month [3][4]. On Oct 15, Bitcoin dropped under $80,000 just before 10 a.m. as stocks fell, then got back to about $82,200 by late morning as stocks recovered and yields fell, per CoinDesk [5].

Rate fears eased anyway. Odds of a Fed hike on Oct 28 fell from 44% after the inflation report [6] to about 15% by Friday, per CoinDesk citing CME's FedWatch [7]. Markets now expect the Fed to wait until December, per Reuters [8].

Banks and brokers moved closer to bitcoin. Standard Chartered said Oct 14 that affluent UAE clients will be able to buy it from their bank accounts [9]. Schwab's CEO said Oct 15 that all its clients can now trade crypto [10]. Deutsche Bank is weeks away from crypto custody, a co-head told Reuters [11]. Sberbank was cleared Oct 12 to offer crypto trading in Russia from Dec 1 [12], and Jeonbuk Bank became the first South Korean bank to take bitcoin as loan collateral, per Seoul Shinmun [13].

Treasury companies split. Strategy bought just 267 BTC Oct 12–18 while spending $193.1M of cash buying back its own preferred stock, so its holdings rose only 0.03%, to 848,517 [14]. Strive bought 4,045 BTC Oct 12–16, reaching 36,818 [15], and priced $630M of 15% preferred stock, partly to buy more [16].

MSCI made its index rule final. From November, members with few operating assets that fail its financial tests two years running are removed [17]. MSCI's own test on May data would have removed Strategy and Metaplanet [18]. Index funds tracking MSCI would have to sell any company removed; the list comes Nov 11.

Illinois paused its crypto tax. The state agreed not to collect its 0.2% tax on crypto bought, moved or stored through brokers before July 1, 2027 [19][20]. On Oct 13 it joined industry groups in asking a court to rule by March 1; the court hasn't approved that schedule yet [19].

Washington lost its crypto point person. Patrick Witt, who ran the White House's crypto council, has left with no successor named, the White House said Oct 14 [21]. With the CLARITY market-structure bill stuck in the Senate, agencies are writing the rules: the CFTC's advance notice on retail crypto trading ran in the Federal Register Oct 13, with comments due Dec 14 [22].

Ledger found tampered wallets. Devices sold by CryptoBilis, a Southeast Asian reseller, had hidden chips that read the 24-word recovery phrase during setup and send it out; on Oct 14 Ledger said its European stock was clean [23].

Mining got harder. Difficulty rose 5.92% on Oct 16, the most since late June, per Mempool [24].

Counter-signal: the selling slowed. The week's outflow was about a third of the prior week's $678.9M, and Oct 13 had a $175.7M inflow, the best day since Oct 2 [2].

Next week: Strive's preferred-stock sale settles Oct 20 [16]. The week after, the Fed decides Oct 28 [25], and Strategy and Coinbase report results Oct 29 [26][27].

text:
Podcast Summary | Candace: Liars Who Lie: TPUSA Tried To Scrub THIS SCANDAL From The Web. Katie Zacharia Comes Clean (Kinda).

Overview
The through-line is credibility: institutions and officials accused of saying things that collapse under scrutiny. Katie Zaharia's legal credentials are questioned, Turning Point's school-facing Club America program is tied to an arrest on child exploitation charges, and Governor Cox's timeline around September 10 is challenged piece by piece. Alongside that runs a broader argument about state power and spectacle, centered on the proposal to livestream an execution, which is treated as a moral line rather than a policy debate.

Key Themes
- Zaharia's admission that she is not an attorney undercuts her earlier claims, and the host treats the explanation for skipping the bar as an excuse rather than a footnote.
- Turning Point's push into middle and high schools is framed as a warning to parents that the host says she issued before the Taylor Dodd arrest.
- The Dodd case is used to argue that Turning Point tried to distance and scrub its ties rather than account for them.
- Governor Cox's public schedule is corrected in ways that place a private meeting and a contested day in sharper focus, raising questions about what the official record omits.
- Competing accounts of a bloodied bag, and of who disposed of it, are presented as evidence that the story has more than one version.
- The Fort Hood execution livestream idea is condemned as state-sponsored spectacle that destroys civilized debate about the death penalty.
- Financial and fundraising claims about Turning Point Action are treated as confirmation of earlier suspicions, not new information.
- The statue vandalism episode is compared to a manufactured outrage, with attention on where donation links pointed.

Detailed Summary
The episode opens on Katie Zaharia, the new press secretary, who has acknowledged she is not an attorney despite previously describing herself as a lawyer and general counsel. The host frames the admission as partial at best, noting that Zaharia has said she did not retake the bar after failing it and offers a personal reason that is presented as exceptional. The argument is less about whether a press secretary must be a lawyer and more about why the credential was claimed at all.

That thread widens into a comparison with Karine Jean-Pierre, whose legal credentials were also questioned after reporting that she did not pass the bar. The host notes Jean-Pierre later characterized it as a mix-up, and points to her LinkedIn listing as general counsel as evidence the framing was deliberate rather than accidental. The explanation involving a surprise baby is dismissed on practical grounds, since the bar is offered twice a year and can be retaken.

Turning Point USA comes under sustained pressure on two fronts. First, the Club America initiative is criticized for moving into middle and high schools, with the host saying she is uncomfortable exposing underage students to the organization and alleging that people with checkered backgrounds work there. Second, the arrest of Taylor Dodd, described as former president of a Club America chapter in Bonners Ferry, Idaho, is treated as vindication of those earlier warnings.

Dodd was arrested in early September on seven felony charges involving child sexually exploitative material. Officials reportedly learned of the alleged crimes through an Internet Crimes Against Children tip originating from Discord, and other apps named include Telegram and Threads. The hosts say court documents describe 116 images saved to a phone, with alleged ages ranging from 3 to 15, and that Dodd reportedly confessed, wrote an apology to his parents, and took responsibility.

The handling of that story is itself the story. A local article by Cora Nichols, described as vice president of the Bonners Ferry Club America homeschool hub, was reportedly edited to remove the Club America reference, and the hosts cite broken links as they allege an effort to scrub the association. The implication is that the organization's response was reputational management rather than accountability.

September 10 receives close reconstruction. A correction to Governor Cox's public schedule is offered: dates entered as September 2 through 3 were meant to be September 9 through 10, placing a private one-on-one meeting between Representative Tyler Clancy and the governor on the evening of September 9. On September 10, the official schedule lists a 9:00 a.m. keynote at the Rally Connects Trade Show in Mona, corroborated by a LinkedIn photo from the AV company, and an 11:30 a.m. staff picnic for the Utah Department of Environmental Quality at Murray Park.

The host says sources place Val Peterson with the governor that day, even though golf with Peterson does not appear on the schedule, and notes the office was asked to confirm or deny. Audio is played that the host identifies as Clancy on police radio confirming a route to Provo Airport for a 3:30 arrival of the victim's wife. The host further alleges Clancy played a significant role that day, including transporting Turning Point employees to the airport and disposing of a bloodied item, and questions whether tossing a bloodied bag is standard police protocol.

Accounts of the bag diverge. Frank Turek reportedly said he instructed a police officer to throw out his bag because Charlie's body had been on top of it. The host says Clancy told others a different version, that he disposed of it on his own volition because it was left in his car. She also distinguishes a separate bloodied bag offered to Shawn Ryan, which she attributes to Brian Harpole. The existence of multiple bags and multiple explanations is presented as the point.

Governor Cox is faulted for early narratives that did not hold up, including a politically motivated assassination and a claim that the shooter changed clothes on the roof. The host argues the public was left confused rather than simply mistaken, and says she feels vindicated in her warnings to parents about Club America now that the Dodd arrest is public.

Financial questions resurface. The hosts revisit long-running allegations that money was missing from Turning Point Action, claiming Charlie Kirk wanted an investigation and that Tyler Boyer was involved, while noting Justin Strife denied it. An email saying September was the busiest month and that the organization burned through financial resources faster than planned is read as confirmation rather than surprise.

The statue vandalism episode, called StatuGate, is treated with suspicion. Boyer presented a newly erected Charlie Kirk statue; within 72 hours it was reportedly vandalized with red spray paint and writing. Turning Point allegedly blamed the left, did not share surveillance footage, and promoted donations and ballot-chasing links, with a 10,000 dollar reward offered and no arrest reported. The hosts criticize directing supporters to Boyer's Turning Point Action 501(c)(4) rather than the charitable arm, and compare the episode to the Jussie Smollett case.

The conversation turns to the proposal to livestream the execution of the Fort Hood shooter, identified as Nidal Malik Hasan. The host calls the idea state-sponsored snuff pornography and a marker of civilizational decline, distinguishing support for the death penalty in principle from wanting to watch it. She rejects theological justifications on the grounds that this is not a theocracy, and warns that empowering a corrupt class with execution power invites a slippery slope, invoking Charlie Kirk's own stated opposition to the death penalty for that reason.

She notes a Truth Social post from Donald Trump stating Hasan would not be executed and would not be livestreamed, calling him scum while citing well-meaning people who would rather not watch him die. The host says families of victims may be permitted to view the execution if they choose. She also asserts that Tyler Robinson did not act alone on a rooftop, and says she did not take Kirk's warnings about his own death seriously.

Other threads are flagged and set aside. The host doubts claims about never-before-seen Charlie material, arguing that speeches imply an audience and suspecting AI-generated content may be involved. She says she must stay focused on September 10 despite many rabbit holes, criticizes Brian Harpole's language about doing the medical, and calls it very odd that neither Turek nor Harpole mentioned a fire captain who performed CPR on Charlie. She asks for tips only from people with direct knowledge, floats a bounty, and says Baron Coleman will take over the show during her absence.

text:
Julius Chestnut has never been drafted and has never started an NFL game.

Three Marches in a row, Tennessee has re-signed him to a one year contract. One year at a time, every time.

Yesterday he blocked the punt that gave the Titans their first win of the season.

Here is the whole thing.

He grew up in Bowie, Maryland, and his father Keith ran a landscaping company.

Julius worked it. Before school some mornings, and all the way through the summers. Hot, hard, outdoor work. He also has bad allergies.

"It taught me lessons about sacrificing, and competing."

His father put him in Little League with kids who were older than him. He started school a year early instead of being held back a year.

Before ninth grade his parents moved him to a private school that was a 45 minute drive each way, which meant leaving every friend he had.

"My dad said that brings out the best of me."

Nobody in the top division of college football offered him anything. He went to Sacred Heart, which plays a level down, and ran for 3,467 yards and 29 touchdowns and was named the best offensive player in his conference.

Then he went undrafted.

Tennessee signed him anyway. They cut him that October. Three days later they put him back on the practice squad. In December they moved him up again.

And every March since, a one year deal.

So he made himself impossible to cut. Last season he led the Titans in special teams tackles with 17, the most by anybody on that team in fifteen years.

Here is what his special teams coordinator John Fassel says he is good at.

"Everything, everything, I mean everything."

"He is one of the best I've ever had."

Fassel has been coordinating special teams for 18 years. He says Chestnut put up the highest special teams point total of any player he has ever had.

"I've been an underdog my whole life, but I've always been someone who is willing to work."

Now yesterday.

Tennessee had lost every game it played. They were down 13 to nothing and then they were tied at 13 in the fourth quarter.

Indianapolis lined up to punt.

Chestnut came through and got a hand on it. Oluwafemi Oladejo picked it up in the end zone.

Tennessee 26, Indianapolis 20.

Now the honest part. He did not score and he did not touch the ball on offense. Oladejo got the touchdown, and a kicker made four field goals to actually win it. A blocked punt is one play by one of the men nobody can name.

But here is the thing about the man who taught him to work.

His father still drives over to his house to cut the grass and lay the mulch.

"My dad always says he'd bet on me every time, in anything I do."

text:
Thank you for this, and I mean that. You have conceded the very thing most who hold your position will not concede, that the dead man needs more than an invitation, he needs enabling grace. That puts our disagreement exactly where you said it is, on one question. Does that grace secure what it enables, or can it finally be refused?

Let me put my case plainly. If God gives the same enabling grace to two men, and one believes while the other refuses, then the thing that finally separated them was not grace. It was something in the man himself. He was softer, humbler, wiser, something. And at that point Paul’s question lands with full weight, ‘What do you have that you did not receive?’ (1 Corinthians 4:7). The believing man would have something to boast of that the refusing man lacked, and it did not come from God. I do not believe you want that conclusion any more than I do.

Now take it back to Bethesda, since you raised it. When the Lord said ‘Get up, pick up your pallet and walk’ (John 5:8), the enabling and the rising were not two separate things, where power was handed over and the man then decided whether to use it. The command carried the power, and the power accomplished the command. Immediately the man became well. It is the same with Lazarus. ‘Lazarus, come forth’ (John 11:43) was not an offer the dead man weighed. That is what Ephesians 2:5 means by ‘even when we were dead in our transgressions, made us alive together with Christ.’ Resurrection is not resistible by the corpse. It is the gift of life itself.

On your verses, I would say they prove more than you want them to. Philippians 1:29 says ‘to you it has been granted for Christ’s sake, not only to believe in Him, but also to suffer for His sake.’ Granted. The believing itself is the gift given, not merely made possible. And I think you mean Acts 18:27, those ‘who had believed through grace.’ Amen, through grace. But notice Luke never writes ‘those who, by grace, were enabled and then of themselves believed.’ The belief came through the grace. And John 6:37 settles the certainty of it, ‘All that the Father gives Me will come to Me.’ Not may come. Will come.

One clarification, because the word ‘irresistible’ misleads many. We do not teach that sinners never resist. Stephen said plainly, ‘you men who are stiff necked... are always resisting the Holy Spirit’ (Acts 7:51). We resist all the way until grace overcomes the resistance by giving a new heart that now wants Christ (Ezekiel 36:26-27). God does not drag anyone to Christ against their will. He makes the unwilling willing, and they run. That is why every believer looking back says not ‘I was wiser than my neighbor’ but ‘He made me alive.’

Grateful for the spirit of this exchange, brother. All glory to God alone.

text:
Two major pieces of Ethereum news landed today: Deutsche Bank, Germany’s largest bank, is reportedly preparing to offer institutional ETH custody, while JPMorgan, the largest bank in the United States, is bringing JPM Coin’s tokenized dollar deposits to Ethereum.

Two giants of traditional finance embracing Ethereum and ETH. But the price barely reacted, whereas on another network, people would be expecting a major pump.

There are two reasons for this. 

First, ETH is larger and more liquid than most competing assets, so it takes more buying pressure to move it. Second, the market already expects major institutions to build on Ethereum. Another announcement is not subverting expectations.

Some people might say Ethereum is cursed: success is expected, and it only has something to lose when it disappoints.

This is where Ethereum bulls diverge from bears.

For years, bulls predicted the adoption now materializing before our eyes. This was NOT consensus. People said institutions would never use Ethereum, or would build everything privately.

Now it’s: “That’s already priced in. Good for Ethereum, but how does it accrue value to ETH?”

There are two things that mentality ignores.

First, this is financial adoption, with size. The players matter, but so do the capital they commit, the assets they tokenize, and how deeply they integrate their products and services.

All of that shows growing trust in Ethereum as a financial network, both for people using layer one directly and for layer twos using it for settlement.

We are gradually building an internet of finance where the underlying network has one native asset: Ether.

ETH secures that system and can be used directly as collateral. Bringing Bitcoin or any other asset, into Ethereum requires additional backing, bridge, or custody arrangements. Native ETH already belongs there.

Why does this matter so much?
Financial activity settling on Ethereum does not pay Bitcoin’s miners. Bitcoin’s own security model anticipates transaction fees replacing its declining issuance. That activity will not magically show up on Bitcoin just because its proponents expect it to.

Second, the uncertainty pushed around ETH’s supply ignores what has actually happened.

Since the Merge, ETH’s net supply has grown roughly 1.3% in total, while continuing to reward the stakers securing it. Stakers can earn above supply dilution, with transaction income on top. For an asset used as a store of value, that cannot simply be ignored.

There is already actual substance behind ETH’s gradual recognition as a store of value. The network has matured. Proof of stake has years of operation behind it. Current SEC guidance identifies ETH as a digital commodity. The ETFs that critics said would never happen now exist, including BlackRock’s multibillion-dollar fund.

Treasury companies like Bitmine and Sharplink are accumulating ETH at scale, and their holdings can produce staking income. That adds another way for investors to gain exposure, and another reason to hold the asset.

So when bulls talk about ETH eventually flipping Bitcoin, then gold, this is what they are looking at: an asset with restrained supply growth, native yield, and direct usefulness in a growing financial system.

You can disagree with that thesis. But “the price didn’t move” does not answer it. Fundamentals are moving int the right direction, but price is a lagging metric.

Many of the things bulls expected are happening. The argument is that ETH is severely underpriced, and that the market still underestimates where it leads.

text:
Pay attention to this AI Avatar Mexican YT brand pulling $100K+/mo with the most blackhat YTA strategy I've ever seen.

Granny Bertha. Husband Ramon. Best friend Carmen. All fake personas selling 3 $39.99 PDFs.

I spent 24h+ digging through their entire strategy and gotta say it’s too saucy to gatekeep…

So here’s the full breakdown of all my findings:

First, the ideal audience isn't who you think it is.

It's not just Mexicans looking for cooking tutorials.

The positioning speaks to Americans with Mexican heritage who grew up a generation or two removed from it. Their grandmother made perfect frijoles but never wrote the recipe down. They understand a few Spanish words, but they've lost touch with the traditions.

Look at this testimonial displayed on the sales pages:

"My mother knew many of these things too but I was not interested in learning, and now that she has passed, I realize what I squandered."

That's a much stronger buying motive than "I need another cookbook."

Bertha calls them mija (daughter/sweetie). Drops words like olla (cooking pot) and comal (flat griddle). References her mother, Guadalajara (major city in Mexico) and the old Mexican way.

Basically selling the grandmother you lost.

Then she layers practical benefits on top: 

- Cheaper meals
- Fewer cleaning products
- One pot of beans that feeds you for three dinners

Nostalgia gets your attention. A useful solution gives you a reason to buy.

Then they expand the world, not just the upload count.

Here's the network:

→ Bertha Cooks: 147K subs
→ Bertha's Clean Home: 176K subs
→ Bertha's Garden Hacks: 111K subs
→ Bertha's House Hacks: 88K subs, 2.6M views in a single week
→ Ramón Delgado, "Bertha's husband": 29K subs
→ Bertha's Bakery and Carmen Cooks, "Bertha's best friend"

Cooking, cleaning, gardening and household fixes are different topics. But they all fit the SAME promise: this family knows the old ways that save you money and work better.

Ramón is the cleverest expansion.

His description literally introduces him as Bertha's husband. Same "(The Mexican Way)" branding, but now it's AC, dryer vents, lawns and water heaters. Garage instead of kitchen. Navy shirt instead of pink.

His "This Is How We Cool Our House Without AC" video hit 896K views.

Notice the WE. He's not a random handyman you need to learn to trust. He's part of a household you already recognize.

That's how you expand a character brand without making every new channel feel like a cold start.

The packaging is built around a few very specific psychological levers.

Bertha Cooks' biggest video:

"Most People Are Cooking Beans Wrong! Try These Mexican Tricks for Perfect Beans Every Time": 986K views.

That title does three jobs:

→ Challenges the viewer: you're doing it wrong.
→ Offers insider knowledge: Mexican tricks.
→ Promises a clear outcome: perfect beans.

Then the operator swaps the dish. Rice, tacos, corn and carne asada all reached roughly 400K–600K views.

They're not inventing a new strategy for every upload, but instead finding another useful topic that fits the same winning promise.

The cleaning channel adds "(The Mexican Way)" to an ordinary search query. "How to clean your shower" becomes advice from a grandmother with a point of view, rather than another generic tutorial.

The garden channel uses a different lever:

"I've Never Had a Bug in My House in 40 Years, The Old Mexican Trick My Mother Swore By": 1.1M views.

"40 years" makes the advice feel time-tested. "My mother" reinforces the heritage angle.

Then you get the "they don't want you to know" framing: "The $1 Bottle Exterminators Hide."

House Hacks goes for unexpected combinations:

"Put Hydrogen Peroxide on Your Feet and Watch What Happens": 5.1M views in two weeks.

The viewer can't predict the answer. That's the curiosity gap.

The lesson isn't to invent claims about miracle remedies, but instead to understand WHY a package works, then find a truthful, useful story that delivers on it.

And the visuals finish the job.

Same pink shirt. Finger to the lips like she's sharing a secret. Food in the foreground. Red "MEXICAN TRICK" badge.

The cleaning videos add bright green rubber gloves. Same character, different job, still recognizable.

Inside the video, Bertha opens talking to camera in her kitchen. Then it cuts to the dirty tub, the vinegar, the dish soap or the food being prepared.

Avatar for familiarity. B-roll to show the actual process.

Now the most untapped part: the cross-posting.

Under the titles you'll see "Bertha's House Hacks and 5 more."

Open the collaborators pop-up and the family is right there.

Instead of relying only on each channel's subscribers, these uploads introduce viewers to the other family channels through YouTube's collaboration feature.

So the cooking audience can discover the cleaning channel. The cleaning audience can meet Ramón. Someone who already likes Bertha has a reason to give Carmen a chance.

The descriptions reinforce it too: "Over on my other channel I show you how to clean your house the old way."

Think of a packed family restaurant opening a second location. It doesn't have to introduce the family from scratch. It sends existing customers somewhere new.

That's the mechanism worth stealing: different subjects, shared trust, obvious bridges between them.

And all that attention leads to the SAME backend.

Every channel links to one of three digital products:

→ Bertha's Cookbook: 551 pages, 120+ recipes, $39.99.
→ Bertha's Cleaning Book: 639 pages, 32 cleaning mixes, $39.99.
→ The Old Mexican Way: 632 pages covering pests, remedies and the household, $39.99.
→ All three bundled for $74.99.

The sales pages don't assume the buyer is comfortable downloading a PDF.

They use huge text, a short video of Bertha explaining the book, and an FAQ that answers "I am not good with computers" with "You do not need to be, mija."

The cleaning page even frames the purchase against what people already spend: the cleaning aisle versus a cheaper cupboard of household ingredients.

They're selling the outcome, then removing the friction.

And when someone chooses the $74.99 bundle instead of one $39.99 book, the order value nearly doubles without needing another view.

We don't have their verified product revenue. But the business model is clear: YouTube attracts the audience, the character builds familiarity, and the products monetize that relationship beyond AdSense.

https://t.co/o12vzGRpnA The 10 Most Beyond-Belief Parts of This Conversation
Based on the two transcript files, here are the 10 most extreme, conspiratorial, or factually unhinged claims made during the Sarah Westall / Michael Letts interview:

1. "Military tribunals have been initiated and indictments are forthcoming"
Letts claims military tribunals have been "created" and "charged," with indictments ready to be served against high-profile figures including Obama, Brennan, and Susan Rice. He presents this as an ongoing, real operation — while admitting the public won't see them until "the investigation is complete." This is a years-old conspiracy theory that has never materialized.
2. "68–70% of the deficit is caused by embezzlement, fraud, and stealing — almost 100% with interest"
Letts asserts that internal documents show most of the national deficit is due to stolen money, and that when you add interest on the stolen money, it approaches 100% of the deficit. He provides no source, no document, and no verification. This is an extraordinary claim presented as fact.

3. "We have two options: military tribunals or another revolution"
Letts frames the choice as either military tribunals or a 1776-style revolution — explicitly invoking the possibility of mass destruction and comparing it to dropping the atomic bomb in WWII. This is rhetoric that normalizes the overthrow of the civilian government.
4. "Congress is a mafia bigger than the mob ever was"
Letts claims the corruption is a global criminal organization "headquartered" in the US, controlling the world's most powerful military and wealthiest country. He says it's the "most elaborate, most sophisticated criminal organization ever to exist in history." This is hyperbolic conspiracy framing.

5. "FEMA didn't have money for North Carolina flood victims because it was transferred to illegals — and that's why they didn't care"
This is a distorted claim. Letts says FEMA's budget was moved to help illegal immigrants, which is why flood victims got no help. The reality is more nuanced (FEMA disaster relief funding is separate from other programs), but it's presented as proof of deliberate malice.
6. "They're stealing your tax money through NGOs, and Congress members sit on the boards"
Letts claims Congress creates thousands of NGOs to funnel government money, and that members of Congress serve on these boards and get paid substantial sums without even attending meetings. This is presented as the mechanism of theft — but no specific evidence is offered.

7. "They're propping up Andrew Tate and Pearl Davis to accelerate moral decay"
Westall claims she ran a "vocal print" analysis showing that figures like Andrew Tate and Pearl Davis are being propped up by the same forces to "help the moral decay quicken" and give people hopelessness. This is a conspiracy theory about influencer culture.
8. "The Christian base is being controlled by twisting scripture to destroy women"
Westall and Letts claim that there's a deliberate effort to use Christianity to attack women — telling them they need to be subservient and shouldn't vote — as part of a broader strategy to defang and control the Christian base. Letts, an ordained Baptist minister, validates this.

9. "The justice system is a kangaroo court — judges ignore the Supreme Court"
Letts claims activist judges simply "give a finger to the Supreme Court" and change a word or two in their rulings to defy them. He says the US has a "third world country kind of thing" because judges don't follow the rule of law. This is a sweeping indictment of the entire judiciary.
10. "We're in a PSY-OP war — they're so good at making it look like they care"
Both speakers repeatedly frame everything as a "psychological operation" and "psy-op war," claiming the media, tech companies, and influencers are all part of a coordinated effort to manipulate the public. This framing allows any contradictory evidence to be dismissed as part of the psy-op.

A note on the broader pattern: Nearly every claim in this conversation is unfalsifiable — indictments are "coming," operations are "unrevealed for national security," and evidence is always just around the corner. The conversation mixes legitimate frustrations about government corruption with extreme conspiracy theories, calls for military tribunals, and revolutionary rhetoric. It's a textbook example of how real issues can be hijacked by conspiratorial thinking that offers no verifiable path forward.

text:
Abraham Shakespeare won a $30 million lottery jackpot in 2006. Three years later, the money was gone, and so was he.

He had worked washing dishes and on garbage trucks in Lakeland, Florida. After the win, he paid off mortgages for family, friends, and some complete strangers. “I really would like my old life back,” he said.

Among the new friends was Dee Dee Moore, who offered to manage his money. In a home video, she asks whether he’s tired of people asking him for money. “They don’t take no for an answer,” he replies.

He was last seen in April 2009 but wasn’t reported missing until November. In January 2010, police found his body under a concrete slab in Moore’s backyard.

Prosecutors say she tried to convince his mother he was still alive, arranging a phone call with someone posing as him. Her ex-husband testified he dug a hole with a backhoe at her request.

Then came the forged letter to his mother, supposedly written by Shakespeare. He was illiterate.

Informant Greg Smith secretly recorded Moore. He testified she told him to burn the body and gave him a list of supplies, including kerosene. On tape, she also discussed a plan for another man to take the blame for about $50,000.

Moore maintains she is innocent. She faced a mandatory life sentence.

He escaped poverty for three years, surrounded by people who all wanted a piece of him. The one who offered to protect his money was the one burying him in her yard.

Was it the lottery that killed him, or the trust he placed in the wrong person?

People on X love to make fun of LinkedIn, and I hope they keep doing it.

I've been spending a lot more time on X lately, and I like it. It's fast, it's funny, and the news breaks there first.

Here's what I've noticed, though. A lot of people on X are grinding out replies for hours a day trying to hit creator status, so they can earn a payout that might come to $100 a month. Do the math on the hours, and it works out to something like $5 an hour.

Meanwhile, the contracts, the partnerships, and the serious business conversations are happening over here. I know people on LinkedIn making millions of dollars from the free marketing this platform offers.

text:
Democrats do offer policies framed as benefiting Black Americans (including equity measures, social programs, and reparations study proposals), but strictly lineage-specific, enacted policies exclusive to “Foundational Black Americans” (FBA—typically meaning descendants of U.S. slaves, distinct from later African or Caribbean immigrants) are limited or absent from major enacted agendas. Voting patterns remain heavily Democratic (~80-90% in recent presidential elections), rooted more in historical realignment and group solidarity than in uniquely transformative FBA-targeted outcomes.
Policies and proposals relevant to Black Americans
Democratic platforms and administrations have advanced race-conscious and equity-focused measures that disproportionately reach Black communities due to income, education, and historical patterns:
Equity executive orders, preferential contracting, HBCU funding, and efforts on home appraisals/housing access.
Student loan relief actions that have disproportionately aided Black borrowers (who carry higher average debt loads relative to income).
Expanded social programs such as the Affordable Care Act (which reduced Black uninsured rates substantially), Child Tax Credit expansions that cut child poverty (including among Black children), SNAP adjustments, and infrastructure investments framed as addressing disinvestment.
Criminal justice measures including the First Step Act (bipartisan but advanced under Trump) and later Democratic pushes on sentencing disparities, policing reforms, and community violence interventions.
Targeted campaign agendas, such as proposals for forgivable loans to Black entrepreneurs, down-payment assistance for first-time Black homebuyers, and health equity initiatives focused on Black men.
On reparations specifically for descendants of American slavery: Democrats have repeatedly introduced and supported H.R. 40 (and Senate counterpart), which would create a commission to study slavery, subsequent discrimination, and develop reparation proposals for African Americans. Progressive members have advanced resolutions calling for large-scale cash or land remedies (sometimes estimated in the trillions). Some local Democratic-led efforts (e.g., Evanston, Illinois; California task force elements) have tested limited housing or cash-adjacent programs. These remain proposals or small-scale pilots; no major federal cash transfer program restricted to FBA lineage has been enacted. FBA advocates often criticize broader “Black” or race-based framing for diluting eligibility beyond American slave descendants.
Outcomes and persistent gaps
Record-low Black unemployment rates occurred under both the Trump and Biden administrations (around 5.3% pre-COVID under Trump; lows near 4.8% under Biden), continuing a longer downward trend from post-recession recovery. Black business formation and certain contracting metrics improved under recent Democratic leadership, and pandemic-era transfers temporarily reduced poverty measures.
However, the racial wealth gap remains large and has not closed in a durable way. Recent Federal Reserve Survey of Consumer Finances data showed median Black household net worth declining roughly 25% from 2022 to 2025 (to about $36,800) while other groups rose, leaving a roughly 9-to-1 median gap versus White households in the latest figures. Family structure disparities are stark: only about 45% of Black children lived in two-parent homes in recent data (versus ~76% of White children), with roughly half in single-parent households—patterns that have persisted or shifted slowly since the 1970s and strongly correlate with economic and educational outcomes across groups. Crime victimization remains disproportionately high in many high-poverty urban areas with large Black populations; studies on mayoral partisanship generally find limited causal effects on overall crime rates from party alone, though progressive criminal justice approaches in some cities have drawn criticism for

None of that is obstruction. It’s the job you swore an oath to do.

Silence is not neutrality. Silence is authorization

text:
FUNDED DEAL: Yieldi, a direct balance sheet lender, closed a $10 million ground-up construction loan for a new three-story, climate-controlled self-storage facility in Bakersfield, California. The completed facility is expected to offer approximately 80,312 net rentable square feet across 747 units and will be professionally managed by CubeSmart. The borrower is an entity of experienced developer YourSpace America and has previously financed projects with Yieldi. The loan includes a $1 million initial advance representing 50% of the property’s stated $2 million value, with the remaining $9 million held back and disbursed as construction milestones are met. The holdback covers approximately 75% of the $11,973,000 construction budget, leaving approximately 25% to be funded separately. Construction hard costs are covered by a fixed lump-sum design-build contract with ARCO/Murray, providing greater cost certainty. YourSpace America is contributing approximately 40% of the total project cost and owns the underlying land free and clear. The projected completed value is $14,430,000, resulting in a loan-to-completed value of approximately 69%. At stabilization, the facility is projected to achieve approximately 93% occupancy and generate roughly $1.4 million in annual net operating income (NOI). Third-party market data for Bakersfield indicates climate-controlled storage rents consistent with the sponsor’s underwriting. Potential refinancing options include permanent financing through the CMBS market or the sponsor’s own REIT. The Borrower had excellent credit. text:
Reiff’s Overseas Reform Experience, USAID Ecosystem, Undermining U.S. Judiciary Legitimacy. 

"Reiff, an Obama-era USAID staff member who was later fired under the Trump administration, was previously involved in the Georgia Rose Revolution."

Danielle M. Reiff’s May 2025 podcast remarks illustrate a pattern of selectively framing around judicial cases inaccurately. 

She was part of a leadership summit in Arizona over a year ago coordinating with other leaders to place doubt on our current co-equal, three-branches of government.

In this video, she actively sows doubt in the arrest and conviction of a Wisconsin judge.

In discussing judicial reform from her USAID career, she references the Georgia Rose Revolution in which “the judiciary was really controlled by the president and his party and wasn’t necessarily delivering justice to all,” Reiff's narrative. 

Reiff, as a USAID staff member, was tasked to help “build systems so that the judiciary could deliver justice… fairly.” 

In this podcast she pivoted to the Wisconsin Judge Hannah Dugan case as an example of “information chaos,” asserting that the common narrative of the judge illegally helping a migrant evade ICE was disinformation. 

According to Reiff’s version, both the agent and the migrant were directed together to the chief judge’s office and rode the elevator jointly—a neutral resolution.

This does not match the facts established by the federal indictment, trial evidence, and conviction. 

On April 18, 2025, Dugan confronted ICE agents at the Milwaukee County Courthouse, told them their administrative warrant for Eduardo Flores-Ruiz (an illegal re-entrant appearing on misdemeanor battery charges) was insufficient, directed them to the chief judge’s office, and then led the defendant and his attorney out a private jury door. 

Agents arrested him after a foot chase outside. A jury convicted Dugan of felony obstruction in December 2025 (acquitting her of the lesser concealment charge). She resigned and was sentenced in July 2026 to a $5,000 fine with no prison time. Her podcast account presents a sanitized version that contradicts the sequence that produced the felony conviction.

This fits the broader USAID career of Reiff being involved in governmental transitions and institutional reform abroad, including the 2012 Georgia parliamentary elections. 

There, as part of USAID’s democracy assistance portfolio, she contributed to efforts around civil society, women’s political leadership, election monitoring, and institutional strengthening during the first ballot-box transfer of power from Saakashvili’s UNM to Ivanishvili’s Georgian Dream. 

That transition included constitutional shifts toward a parliamentary system and was assessed by Western monitors as reflecting voter will, though it also initiated lasting polarization and later prosecutions of prior officials. 

Since the early 1990s, USAID has spent roughly 1.9 billion dollars in Georgia on democratic institutions, elections, the rule of law, and civil society. 

Much of the political and electoral work was channeled through partners that include the International Republican Institute and the National Democratic Institute. 

These efforts backed multiparty competition, proportional representation, parliamentary accountability, and an executive accountable to the legislature. 

Georgia originally operated under a stronger presidential or semi-presidential system in which the president held significant executive power and was directly elected. Through constitutional amendments adopted in 2017–2018 under the Georgian Dream government, the country shifted to a parliamentary republic. 

Direct presidential elections were ended, the presidency was reduced to a largely ceremonial role, and real executive authority moved to a prime minister chosen by and accountable to the unicameral parliament, which itself moved toward fully proportional representation.

USAID, along with partners such as the International Republican Institute and National Democratic Institute, provided long-term funding and technical support for elections, multiparty competition, parliamentary development, and civil-society groups that advocated institutional reforms aligned with Western democratic models. 

While the formal changes were enacted by Georgia’s own parliament, these external programs actively promoted and sustained the environment in which the parliamentary system was adopted and consolidated.

These are the same parliamentary features Georgia adopted in its 2017 and 2018 reforms and that the DSA now advocates for the United States. 

In short, the parliamentary model in Georgia was shaped and sustained with heavy United States involvement via USAID and related democracy assistance. 

The DSA’s domestic proposal mirrors those institutional forms, while Georgia’s current leadership treats the foreign funding that helped produce them as illegitimate interference.

Similar USAID work occurred in places such as Uganda, Colombia, South Sudan, and Sri Lanka: contexts in which “democracy promotion” often included judicial capacity-building, rule-of-law programs, and support for transitions framed as countering authoritarian or party-controlled institutions.

In the current former-USAID ecosystem (as described in DataRepublican’s October 2026 “Democracy Files” reporting and the 2025 Daily Caller/NOTUS coverage of DemocracyAID), these skills are being applied domestically. 

If successful at scale, this approach could weaken U.S. judicial independence by eroding public confidence in courts through selective or inaccurate framing of high-profile cases, while advancing institutional changes that subordinate judges to a nominal role other than a co-equal branch of government. 

Judicial commentary of the type Reiff offered, which recharacterizes a convicted obstruction case as media distortion while emphasizing reform of party-controlled courts, functions as one such role by shaping public understanding of judicial legitimacy and independence. 

If successful, these groups could help weaken the third branch of government by supporting the appointment of ideologically biased judges who prioritize political outcomes over impartial application of the law.

In short, Reiff’s inaccurate Dugan narrative and her Georgia-style judicial reform experience illustrate how former USAID democracy practitioners can shape domestic discourse and institutional pressure within the broader ecosystem, with potential effects that align with efforts to reduce judicial independence rather than preserve it.

1SG 🫡 AWP DAILY ORDER — October 19, 2026
Promise #292 • TAKE REFUGE UNDER HIS WINGS

1 — THE ORDER

Today’s 365Promises summary: “I will cover you with My feathers and protect you with My wings.” Based on Psalm 91:4. 

“He shall cover you with His feathers,
And under His wings you shall take refuge;”
— Psalm 91:4, NKJV (excerpt) 

Battle Line: I am sheltered in Christ; I can meet this day with truth, courage, and love.

2 — THE TRAINING

Warrior Doctrine — Your refuge is God Himself.

The picture of protective wings joins tenderness with strength. The One who commands your obedience also welcomes your dependence. Bring Him your concern before you have worked out how everything will end.

Psalm 91 begins with dwelling and abiding. Make prayer your first movement. When worry rises, return your attention to God: acknowledge His care, name your concern, and entrust your next step to Him.

The latter part of verse 4 describes God’s truth as protection. Practice three questions: What do I know? What am I imagining? What has God revealed? His faithfulness gives your trust a foundation.

Read this promise alongside Psalm 91:15, where God promises His presence in trouble, and Matthew 4:5–7, where Jesus refuses to test God. Taking refuge includes wise precautions, receiving help, and faithfully carrying out your responsibilities.

As you receive His care, carry that care into another person’s day. Listen patiently. Ask what help would be useful. Let your confidence in Christ make room for kindness.

Armor Fit

* Helmet of Salvation: Remember whose you are.
* Shield of Faith: Entrust the outcome to God.
* Belt of Truth: Separate facts from feared possibilities.
* Boots of Peace: Enter today’s encounters ready to listen and serve.

Cross-references — NKJV: Psalm 57:1; Psalm 91:14–16; Matthew 4:5–7; John 16:33; 2 Corinthians 1:3–4.

3 — THE EXECUTION

Commander’s Orders

text:
If you need to travel between the Pacific Northwest hubs of Seattle and Portland, a number of options can get the job done. There’s driving, Amtrak, and of course flying via Alaska or Delta from SeaTac. But there’s also little known SeaPort Airlines.

A small, Part 135 commuter airline, SeaPort operates flights from Portland International Airport (PDX) and Seattle’s close-in Boeing Field (BFI). They also recently started service to Spokane, Washington.

I’ve known about SeaPort for some time, but hadn’t seriously considered flying them until a last minute day trip down to Oregon popped up.

The carrier offers a handful of fare buckets, which differ primarily on change, cancellation and refund fees. Every fare comes with 50 pounds of baggage included. I bought a last-minute ticket at $329, priced exactly equal to a basic economy fare on PDX-SEA for the same day.

I walked up to the PDX “terminal” a half hour before departure on the day of the flight. In Portland, at least, the airline operates out of its own space, which is separate from the main terminal by about a half mile.

The space is small but serviceable, with some lounge-style seating and a small table with self-serve coffee, tea and water. It isn’t anything to brag about, but then its not a space you’re supposed to hang out at for any length of time. With no security to deal with and a maximum of nine other passengers on any given flight, the airline says you can show up as little as 20 minutes before departure.

Check-in was quick and easy; I only had to provide my name. My small backpack was weighed, as all bags are, before the agent added a BFI tag to it. Larger bags were placed in a bag cart right away, while smaller bags like mine could be held onto until boarding.

With all the passengers already checked in, a friendly pilot figured we might as well get to it and walked us out to the plane a little ahead of schedule.

Seating on the aircraft, a Swiss-made Pilatus PC-12, is open. There are nine-seats in a 1-1 configuration, plus space in the rear of the cabin for bags.

Being a small, single-engine airplane, the cabin ceiling is low and the space is a bit cozy. Still, it’s noticeably more roomy than, say, a Cessna Grand Caravan.

🚨 UKRAINE SAYS PAID-FOR PATRIOT MISSILES ARE BEING HELD BACK BY WASHINGTON

KYIV, UKRAINE - Patriot batteries are valuable, but the interceptors are the real bottleneck. A launcher without missiles offers little protection, and that is where Ukraine's vulnerability now appears most acute.

The unusual part of this dispute is that it centers on weapons already financed through a NATO-coordinated mechanism rather than a fresh aid request. That shifts the argument from funding to political authorization and supply prioritization. Every month of delay forces Ukrainian commanders to become more selective about what they defend and what they leave exposed.

Zelensky's reported offer linking diesel infrastructure strikes to interceptor deliveries suggests Kyiv sees missile inventories, not launch platforms, as the immediate constraint. If shortages persist, Russian planners are likely to view ballistic missile attacks as increasingly cost effective, knowing each interception consumes scarce and expensive ammunition. The practical result is that Ukraine may reserve Patriot coverage for the highest-value targets while accepting greater risk elsewhere.

#GlobalEnergyUpdate | US Solicits Exchange of Up to 17 Million Barrels from Strategic Petroleum Reserve

The US Department of Energy has issued a request for proposals for an exchange of up to 17 million barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The move forms part of a March agreement under which Washington committed to loan 172 million barrels as part of a coordinated International Energy Agency action involving about 30 countries to release roughly 400 million barrels globally.

The United States has already released about 132.5 million barrels from the SPR since the conflict with Iran began. The latest solicitation covers a portion of the remaining volume from the original commitment. An earlier offer of the final batch in June attracted only limited interest, with companies agreeing to borrow about 500,000 barrels.

text:
The Wall Street Journal reports that Putin has proposed to Trump a trilateral summit with Xi Jinping on the war in Ukraine, to be held on the sidelines of APEC in China on November 18–19.

For Moscow, what matters is not only the outcome of the talks but also being recognised as an equal member of the great-power club. Putin dreams of a repeat of Tehran in 1943 or Yalta in 1945, with Russia, the United States and China carving up the world in a G3 format.

This is rather ironic, given that Russia is, in reality, a dwarf seeking attention through crimes and wars.

Trump may agree to Putin’s proposal. But he certainly will not have Tehran or Yalta in mind. And Xi is unlikely to go along with it. Why would he? What would he gain? China would have more to lose from such an arrangement.

If Trump does agree, it will only be because he wants the business deals Russia has already promised him and the Nobel Peace Prize. So what does Russia expect to gain?

▪️ Russia seeks a status that does not reflect its actual economic weight. A trilateral format puts Putin on the same footing as the leaders of the world’s two largest economies.

▪️ Russia gains an opportunity to legitimise its claims to a sphere of influence. The question of Ukraine shifts from a problem of Russian aggression to a subject of great-power negotiations over security and mutual concessions. This is precisely the approach Moscow has been pursuing for decades.

▪️ Russia is trying to exclude Europe from strategic decision-making. A G3 format would allow the Kremlin to discuss European security with Washington and Beijing without recognising Europe as an equal participant in the talks.

▪️ Russia is trying to offset its growing dependence on China. In bilateral relations with Beijing, Moscow is the weaker partner. A G3 format would allow it to claim the role of an independent global centre of power rather than China’s junior partner.

▪️ Russia gains an additional bargaining tool with the United States. Moscow can link concessions over Ukraine to sanctions, energy, strategic weapons and European security.

Neither China nor the United States has much need for a G3 format. Beijing is already negotiating directly with Washington and seeks to expand its global influence, while Russia’s involvement offers no obvious advantages but creates risks for China’s relations with Europe. Trump may find a trilateral summit appealing as an opportunity to showcase a diplomatic success and reach agreements on nuclear security, but the United States can address these issues directly with China, without Russia.

Putin’s dream of making Russia one of the three architects of a new world order is therefore unlikely to come true. Still, he may well be offered the illusion of equal standing so that he can be used to serve others’ interests.

text:
OP-ED: SALIHU LUKMAN'S ALLIANCE TALK AND THE ILLUSION OF A SINGLE OPPOSITION CANDIDATE

By Okoi Obono-Obla

I read with interest the interview granted by Mallam Salihu Lukman Mohammed, chieftain of the African Democratic Congress and convenor of the G100, to Channels Television and reported by TheCable on 17th October, 2026, to the effect that opposition parties are moving closer to an alliance ahead of the 2027 general election.

We have heard this same song for the past one year. Yet nothing has been demonstrated by those concerned to walk the talk.

Let us be clear on the law. Every presidential candidate must be sponsored by a political party. That is the mandatory requirement of Section 221 of the 1999 Constitution (as amended). Under our electoral law, there is no provision for an alliance of political parties to sponsor a single presidential candidate. The Electoral Act, 2026 (as amended) retains the settled provision: where a candidate knowingly allows himself to be nominated by more than one political party, his nomination shall be void.

The whole talk of producing a single presidential candidate through an alliance is, with respect, a boogeyman.

Mallam Lukman speaks of six parties — ADC, APM, NDC, SDP, PDP and PRP — consulting five presidential aspirants. But all these parties have now emerged with their own presidential candidates, and more importantly, the Independent National Electoral Commission has spoken.

On 12th September, 2026, INEC published its final list of 18 presidential candidates and running mates for the January 16, 2027 election. The list includes President Bola Ahmed Tinubu of the APC, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar of the ADC, former Governor Peter Obi of the NDC, Governor Seyi Makinde of the APM, Donald Duke of the PRP and others.

Once the final list is published, the law offers only two narrow pathways to what Lukman desires.

The first is a full merger under the merger provisions of the Electoral Act, 2026. Parties must merge at least 90 days before the election, surrender their registration, logos and structures, and become a new party. That is how APC was formed in 2013. None of the parties in G100 is prepared to do that.

The second is withdrawal and replacement under the Electoral Act, 2026. A candidate may withdraw and his party may conduct a fresh primary within 14 days to replace him. There is no joint candidacy on the ballot. At best, five candidates will withdraw, their parties will choose not to replace them, and they will endorse the remaining one candidate who remains, legally, the candidate of only one party.

Has any of this happened? No.

Therefore, the optimism of Mallam Lukman Mohammed is certainly misplaced and its workability hangs in the balance. It is mere talk to give the impression that an opposition in disarray exists.

The truth is that the opposition is hoping to weaponize the reform agenda of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and feast on a possible and hopeful public indignation arising from the short-term pains of subsidy removal, foreign exchange unification and other necessary but painful adjustments.

That strategy has failed because until now, the opposition has dismally failed to present a coherent and well-defined antidote to the reform agenda that irks it so much.

Until the opposition moves from sloganeering to substance, and from press statements to the lawful sacrifice of withdrawing candidatures in INEC's final list, the alliance will remain what it has always been — a convenient headline without legal or political legs.

text:
Reformation Reflection

Truth that sets free

The Verse

John chapter eight verse thirty two

and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.

From the English Standard Version of the Holy Bible

Opening Prayer

Father of all truth who sent Your Son to be the Truth that sets free we come before You on this day of Reformation reflection. The world offers many voices that claim to free us yet only Your Word holds the power to break the chains of sin and falsehood. Teach us to know the truth. Let that truth set us free. Keep us abiding in the words of Christ so that we remain His disciples and walk in the liberty He purchased. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

Big Idea

John chapter eight verse thirty two promises that those who know the truth will be set free. Reformation Reflection is the autumn reminder that the church and the soul are always in need of returning to the truth that liberates. Freedom is not found by inventing new paths or by clinging to old errors. It is found by knowing the truth that is found in Christ alone. The Reformation recovered the Word as the sole authority and the gospel as the sole power that sets sinners free. That same truth still sets free today.

Thematic Sections

One: You Will Know the Truth

Scripture: John chapter eight verse thirty two

and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.

From the English Standard Version of the Holy Bible

Takeaway: Knowing the truth is not mere information. It is the personal acquaintance with the One who is Truth. Jesus said that those who abide in His word are truly His disciples and they will know the truth. The Reformation recovered the conviction that Scripture is clear and sufficient for that knowledge. When the Word is opened the truth is not hidden. It is given so that ordinary people may know it and be changed by it.

Practice: Speak the words you will know the truth. Then open the Scriptures today and read a passage slowly asking the Lord to make the truth clearer to you than it was yesterday.

Two: The Truth Will Set You Free

Scripture: John chapter eight verse thirty two

and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.

From the English Standard Version of the Holy Bible

Takeaway: Freedom in this verse is freedom from the bondage of sin and from the lies that keep the soul captive. The truth does not merely inform. It liberates. The Reformation was a recovery of the gospel truth that justification is by faith alone in Christ alone. That truth set countless people free from the fear of a God who could never be pleased by works. The same truth still sets free those who believe it.

Practice: Speak the words the truth will set you free. Then name one lie you have believed that has kept you bound and ask the Lord to replace it with the liberating truth of His Word.

Three: Abiding Produces Freedom

Scripture: John chapter eight verse thirty one and verse thirty two

If you abide in my word, you are truly my disciples, and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.

From the English Standard Version of the Holy Bible

Takeaway: The promise of knowing the truth and being set free is given to those who abide in the word of Christ. Abiding is remaining. It is continuing under the authority of the Scriptures rather than drifting into every new wind of teaching. Reformation Reflection calls the church to keep reforming by the Word. Freedom is not a one time event. It is the ongoing fruit of staying close to the truth that first set us free.

Practice: Speak the words abide in my word. Then choose one habit of regular Scripture reading or meditation that you will keep this week as a way of abiding.

Christ in the Gospel of John

In the Gospel of John Jesus declares that He is the way and the truth and the life. The truth that sets free is not an abstract principle. It is a Person. When Jesus stood before Pilate He bore witness to the truth and those who are of the truth listen to His voice. The Reformation pointed people back to this Christ who alone liberates. He is the Word made flesh. In Him the truth became visible and the freedom He offers is the freedom of sons and daughters rather than the slavery of those who try to earn their own righteousness.

Westminster and Reformed Notes

The Westminster Confession of Faith chapter one teaches that the Holy Scripture is the only sufficient rule of faith and practice. It contains all things necessary for the glory of God and the salvation of man. The Reformers recovered this conviction against traditions that had obscured the gospel. Reformed theology insists that the truth which sets free is the truth contained in the Word of God. Justification by faith alone, the authority of Scripture alone, and the sufficiency of Christ alone are not optional extras. They are the liberating center of the faith once delivered to the saints.

Short Litany and Prayer

You will know the truth.

The truth will set you free.

Abide in His word.

Lord teach us the truth.

Lord set us free.

Lord keep us abiding.

Amen.

Closing Exhortation

On this day of Reformation Reflection do not settle for a freedom that is only the absence of restraint. Seek the truth that sets free. Open the Word. Abide in it. Let the gospel of Christ liberate your soul from every lie that still binds you. The Reformation was not the end of reform. It was a call to keep returning to the truth. That call remains.

Reflection Questions

1. What truth from Scripture has already set you free and how has that freedom changed the way you live?

2. Where do you still feel bound by a lie and what specific word of Christ speaks to that bondage?

3. How can you more faithfully abide in the word of Christ this week so that the truth continues to set you free?

🚨 DAN COX UNVEILS PLAN TO END RESIDENTIAL PROPERTY TAXES IN MARYLAND, CUT CORPORATE TAX RATE

Republican gubernatorial candidate Dan Cox is proposing major tax reforms, arguing Maryland families are being priced out of their own communities.

▪️ PROPERTY TAXES: Cap assessments at original values while working toward eliminating residential property taxes entirely.

▪️ FIRST-TIME BUYERS: Offer construction tax credits and mortgage incentives to make homeownership more affordable.

▪️ STATE AUDITS: Review agency budgets and redirect identified savings toward taxpayers and counties.

▪️ BUSINESS TAXES: Reduce Maryland’s corporate income tax rate from 8.25% to 5.5%.

▪️ SENIOR RELIEF: Eliminate what Cox describes as retirement-related taxes for seniors.

▪️ NOVEMBER 3: Cox is challenging Democratic Gov. Wes Moore on taxes, government spending and affordability.

The central challenge is funding: Property taxes support county governments and public schools, and a governor cannot eliminate local taxes unilaterally. Cox has not detailed how those revenues would be replaced.

Will Cox’s proposed spending cuts cover the lost revenue, or would counties face major budget reductions?

SOURCES: Dan Cox for Governor, October 19, 2026; Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation.
