text:
Why does Gary come and lecture you on why some children need to see their mums burn to death for the good of humanity? 
You may think Gary passionately believes Israel has the right to defend itself by blowing up apartment blocks with sleeping children, but that’s not why he does it. He does it because he needs something. It’s hard to get. We’ll soon find out what it is. 
 
You only see an avatar and a mystifying handle. You don’t see Gary’s potbelly. You don’t see how tired Gary is. You can’t tell how detached Gary tries to look. How above it all. How unfazed by it all. Reddish nose from daily night caps. Usually muscatel. Sometimes old whiskey. Not mixed with cola, though he prefers it that way. He knows that’s primitive. 
 
Most of all you can’t see Gary’s pain. 
 
A lot of pain. 
 
Pain that’s been there for so long that Gary himself doesn’t notice it’s there anymore. 
 
His pain has become a certain kind of attitude, a behaviour. 
 
Gary is not evil. 
 
He has two kids that even though they are in their mid twenties he still supports financially. 
 
He has a wife he’s never beaten. He also hasn’t had intercourse with her in the last 6,5 years. And he doesn’t want to remind himself of the last time they tried. When about halfway through she gave him a quick peck on the cheek, giggled to hide her shame and guilt and said: ‘I guess that ship has sailed.’ 
 
By that ship Gary assumes she meant the passion between them. 
 
But there never had been any of that. 
 
The most intense, most satisfying moment of Gary’s life happened in the late nineties. With a Portugese woman named Silvana. When he got to second base with her in dimly lit bar in the barro alto, not too far from the Fernando Pessoa statue. She’d given him a book with Pessoa’s poem. On the title page she had written: ‘His melancholy reminds me of yours. Whatever you carry inside you, you can show to me.’ 
 
He never did. 
 
When the project for which his US company had sent him to Lisbon ended he returned to Michigan. They chatted over ICQ for a bit and email. It petered out. When he found her on Facebook eleven years later she was married to a Brazilian guy who trains horses. It stung. He asked her if she had married the Horse Whisperer. She never replied. 
 
His wife looks nothing like Silvana, but she is practical, dependable, not a spendthrift and never does anything to embarrass him. At least not in public. 
 
Why do we need to know all this? 
 
Why can’t we know why Gary calls people idiot, retard, moron several times a week on a platform formerly known as Twitter? 
 
Why do we need to know some rude guy on social media drinks one or two glasses of muscatel every night? 
 
The muscatel he drinks because at first it made him feel close to Silvana in her absence. Now he drinks it cause he got used to the smell and the taste of it. And because special people consume special drinks. 
 
And Gary feels special. 
 
Secretly. 
 
Gary is almost certain he’s brilliant. 
 
He thinks he should have gone to MIT and not some unknown college. 
 
He blames his parents for not getting into MIT. 
 
That’s a pattern with Gary. 
 
When something doesn’t go like he likes it to go he blames someone else than himself. Always. 
 
If Israel burning children in tents doesn’t fit with what Gary think Israel stands for, then someone else is responsible for burning those children. 
 
Since Gary knows he is brilliant and it’s only the dumb world that has failed to reward his brilliance he feels a glimmer of that brilliance when he can call other people idiots. Anonymously of course. 
 
Gary is hypersensitive to being shamed. 
 
His mum was a mean drunk and at times would make fun of Gary’s father. She would praise sophisticated men, local men and celebrities alike and then laugh haughtily and tell Gary: ‘Your farm raised father is a slob who never takes me anywhere.’ 
 
That’s just one wound that made Gary avoid any situation where someone could shame him. Especially women. 
 
Another factor in Gary labeling people who empathize with Palestinian little girls trapped in cars with dead relatives and being shot at by big ass Israeli tanks is this: 
 
Gary suffers, it’s often the same pain, his brilliance is never recognized. Not in school, not at home, not at his job. Not even by his three poker friends. Since Covid they don’t even meet anymore. 
 
His children treat him like this somewhat adorable chubby block of grumpiness trying to hard to matter. They love him, but don’t respect him. His advice is always made fun of. His son has even said: ‘The only thing I trust you on is if you design a bridge. But now chatgpt can do that faster.’ 
 
Gary knew his son wasn’t even try to hurt him and exactly that hurt the most. 
 
Gary sometimes wondered if when is never fully loved in childhood, love always eludes you. 
 
His dad’s way of showing love to Gary was to build a bird’s house together. Dad would get upset at some point, start yelling and send Gary inside claiming he could focus better alone. Dad would finish the bird’s house and call Gary and his mum to come look at it. Which made Gary feel useless. Worse was when mum said: ‘He makes me live in a dump, but he will build a mansion for the birdies.’ 
 
The closest Gary’s dad ever got was on his death bed. 
 
When he said Gary’s watch looked really good on him. That it showed a bit of class. 
 
Gary beamed and said: ‘It’s a smartwatch.’ 
 
And dad said: ‘Today watches are smart and people are dumb.’ 
 
Gary with the smartwatch feels the irrepressible need to call people dumb online. 
 
Since nobody has ever really empathized with Gary, he experiences it as a personal affront to have to empathize with injured children in Gaza. He hates that everyone now cares about those, but nobody ever cared about little Gary who had to witness the cold war between his parents, was never excellent at anything, except mathematics at times and one science project in school when he was 15 (which went largely unnoticed). 
 
You know how you can tell Gary’s been vitally damaged? 
 
He’s given up on effort. 
 
No effort in Gary ever got him more than a fairly decent job, a respectable wife, a better home than his parents could afford and two kids who are ok, but always feel very far away, especially when they are in the same room as Gary. 
 
So no, Gary is not going to read ten pro-Palestine books and ten pro-Israeli books, examine his own bias, contact people on both sides, try as hard as possible to reach some kind of fair verdict. 
 
But he also can’t resist commenting anyway. 
 
Since effort is suspect in Gary’s life he doesn’t want to spend too much energy on his comments. 
 
He will share some graph he found somewhere showing how there are more Palestinians today than 20 years ago, so Israel can’t have any genocidal intent. 
 
If anyone counters with graphs of their own he types ‘idiot.’ 
 
Gary doesn’t want to know. Gary already knows what counts: 
 
Associating himself with Israel makes him feel connected to the most succesful people in the US. And success is what Gary respects. Palestinians he associates with the same loud people who want everything for free, like cancelling student debt. 
 
Gary’s proof that he is brilliant is that he calls others idiots. 
 
Accepting dead children also makes him feel supremely rational. 
 
What could be more rational than accepting that sometimes to create a better world some children have to be separated from their arms and their legs, and their parents, and their homes. 
 
It’s all for the greater good and it’s not Israel doing it. Hamas members sit in the cockpit of the Israeli F-35s and force the pilot’s hand. Well, you know, symbolically. I mean, they are terrorists after all. 
 
In Gary’s world some guys with guns are terrorists and some guy, and especially pretty girls who look like Gary’s fantasy girls, can never be terrorists. 
 
Gary’s aspirations in life have been defeated, but they are not dead and supporting Israel feels like some of Israel’s dominance, power, cunning intelligence will rub off on Gary. 
 
In Gary’s fantasies he is exactly the kind of guy who could have engineered the pager attack on Hezbollah. 
 
He is the one who could create an Iron Dome. 
 
He is unrecognized success and brilliant goodness, just like, in Gary’s mind, Israel is unrecognized success and brilliant goodness. 
 
In supporting Israel Gary supports little denied Gary. 
 
And so almost every day Gary dumps some comment on a stranger. Sometimes the stranger foolishly takes the bait and reacts. As if anyone could ever change Gary’s mind. 
 
Gary feels good. Finally someone is hit by something Gary did and said, though negatively. Gary has penetrated. And that is enough. He’s no longer interested now, so his off ramp is yelling ‘idiot’. Like dumping the used condom in the bin after the high has been had. 
 
Gary only wants to make people who still love life bad. 
 
Gary has kinda given up on life. 
 
He’s still here. There is some hope left, not much. 
 
And if you ask him why he is angry or annoyed he will say something like all those crazy lefties are turning the whole country upside down and are falling for Hamas propaganda. 
 
He will not mention the 6,5 years dry spell. 
 
Or the school reunions he dreads because he doesn’t shine there. 
 
He will not say how every time the 25 year old colleague, a mesmerizing mix of Syrian-Korean roots and the most dazzling black curls Gary has ever seen walks past at work Gary feels as worthy as a small piece of cheap pizza stuck on the floor of a subway car. 
 
And so Gary throws some cherry picked information online, calls whoever responds a retard and never realizes that this works exactly like the muscatel. 
 
It gives him a vague hint of what he really needs: 
 
intimacy so warm, so real, so safe, so sensual, so embracing of true Gary, his pain would finally go away. 
 
And so the Palestinians come to stand for everything Gary loathes in himself and about the world and Israelis come to stand for everything what Gary knows he could have been, had the world not thwarted him and spit him out. 
 
That Gary can mumble something about the Balfour declaration or can make the sweeping claim that Palestinians have been offered a state many times, but always choose war, doesn’t change any of that. 
 
He doesn’t actually care about this issue. 
 
Gary cares about soothing Gary’s pain. 
 
And for that the pain of Palestinian children needs to be shrugged off, so Gary can piss off some folks Gary loathes and Gary gets to feel for a fleeting second that anything Gary says can have some kind of effect too. 
 
Once you know Gary’s story, and there are so many Garys, you know you don’t owe Gary a senseless discussion because Gary got infinitely less from life than Gary did deserve when he was born. 
 
Now, through his own actions, he deserves those good things less and less. 
 
I dream of all pro-Palestinians holding hands and forming a circle round Gary and reminding him of every good thing Gary did. 
 
Ubuntu. 
 
Strangely that would be the first time Gary would feel the least bit of an opening to modify his opinions on Palestine-Israel. 
 
A person is a person through other people. 
 
Gary just ran into too few people who could have made Gary see bleeding Palestinian children on a cold hospital floor and feel called to do something to stop the ones throwing the bombs on them.

text:
The GAO put it plainly: U.S. federal agencies do not have an adequate, coordinated response to foreign governments harassing and coercing people on American soil. That report, titled "Human Rights: Agency Actions Needed to Address Harassment of Dissidents and Other Tactics of Transnational Repression in the U.S. " didn't bury the lede. Current frameworks are insufficient. Agencies lack basic shared understanding of the scale and tactics involved. Recommended fixes went to both agencies and Congress.

This is transnational repression. Authoritarian governments extending their domestic repression apparatus into other countries, including this one. It's been documented by the GAO, Freedom House, the Human Rights Foundation, and the DOJ's National Security Division. Victim testimony has been collected at Johns Hopkins University's Washington D.C. campus. The picture is consistent across all of them.

Freedom House called it "possibly the biggest challenge in terms of transnational repression for the United States and other democratic countries that are home to dissidents." Their report, "Unsafe in America: Transnational Repression in the United States," is specific about what that looks like in practice. Physical surveillance at diaspora community events. Cyberattacks targeting activists' devices. Covert monitoring of social media. Harassment of family members who stayed behind in the origin country, used as leverage against people who got out. And what Freedom House calls "secret police stations," which are unofficial consular operations running without diplomatic transparency, set up specifically to monitor and pressure diaspora communities from inside the country that's supposed to be sheltering them.

The DOJ's National Security Division has prosecuted cases involving operatives from China, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, and Ethiopia conducting repression on U.S. soil. That's not a short list. But prosecutors face real, persistent problems: attribution is hard, victims often won't cooperate because they're afraid of what happens to their families back home, and jurisdiction gets complicated fast. The DOJ framework covers the legal violations involved, including unregistered foreign government agency, stalking, harassment, identity theft, computer fraud. The law isn't the gap. The coordinated response is.

The Human Rights Foundation added something important: Interpol reinstated Syria into its network after a decade-long ban. That decision handed the Assad regime the ability to issue Red Notices against Syrian dissidents living in democratic countries. An international law enforcement tool, now available to a government that was banned from it for exactly this kind of abuse. That's not a bureaucratic footnote. Red Notices travel. They complicate residency, travel, banking, employment. Weaponizing Interpol against the people it's supposed to protect is a force multiplier for transnational repression, and it happened quietly.

The Johns Hopkins victim testimony put a face on the abstract. One person described was a former NBA player and activist who said he had a bounty on his head in Turkey after criticizing that country's governance, while living in the United States. His international public profile didn't protect him. That's worth sitting with. If you're prominent enough that a lot of people would recognize your name and your face, that visibility offers you less cover than you'd think against a state actor that has decided to come after you.

On the diplomatic side, U.S. Ambassador Michèle Taylor delivered a joint statement at the U.S. Mission to International Organizations in Geneva on behalf of more than 45 countries. It's the largest multilateral statement on transnational repression assembled so far. That's a real development. Democratic governments are increasingly treating this as something requiring coordinated international response rather than each country handling it alone inside their own borders.

But there's a gap between diplomatic statements and operational capacity, and the GAO findings sit right in the middle of it. Forty-five countries signing onto a Geneva statement is meaningful. Agencies still not having a coherent whole-of-government framework for protecting diaspora communities on U.S. soil is also real, and those two things are happening simultaneously.

The core tension Freedom House identified is accurate and unresolved. The United States positions itself as a sanctuary for political refugees and dissidents. Authoritarian governments treat American territory as an extension of their domestic repression. Both things are true right now, in the same country, affecting the same people. The GAO's findings confirm that the institutional response to that tension hasn't caught up to the operational reality of what's being run against diaspora communities here.

text:
A GUIDE TO GODLY DISPUTATION
by John Newton

Dear Sir,
As you are likely to be engaged in controversy, and your love of truth is joined with natural warmth of temper, my friendship makes me solicitous on your behalf. You are of the strongest side; for truth is great, and must prevail; so that a person of abilities inferior to yours might take the field with a confidence of victory. I am not therefore anxious for the outcome of the battle; but I would have you more than a conqueror, and to triumph, not only over your adversary, but also over yourself. If you cannot be vanquished, you may be wounded. To preserve you from such wounds as might give you cause of weeping over your conquests, I would present you with some considerations, which, if duly attended to, will do you the service of a great coat of armor; such armor, that you need not complain, as David did of Saul’s, that it will be more cumbersome than useful; for you will easily perceive that it is taken from that great armory provided for the Christian soldier—the Word of God. I take it for granted that you will not expect any apology for my freedom, and therefore I shall not offer one. For methods sake, I may reduce my advice to three heads, respecting your opponent, the public, and yourself.
1. As to your opponent, I wish that before you set pen to paper against him, and during the whole time you are preparing your answer, you may commend him by earnest prayer to the Lord’s teaching and blessing. This practice will have a direct tendency to conciliate your heart to love and pity him; and such a disposition will have a good influence upon every page you write.
If you account him as a BELIEVER, though greatly mistaken in the subject of debate between you, the words of David to Joab concerning Absalom, are very applicable: "Deal gently with him for my sake." The Lord loves him and bears with him; therefore you must not despise him, or treat him harshly! The Lord bears with you likewise, and expects that you should show tenderness to others—from a sense of the much forgiveness you need yourself. In a little while you will meet in heaven—he will then be dearer to you than the nearest friend you have upon earth is to you now! Anticipate that period in your thoughts, and though you may find it necessary to oppose his errors, view him personally as a kindred soul, with whom you are to be happy in Christ forever.

But if you look upon him as an UNCONVERTED person, in a state of enmity against God and his grace (a supposition which, without good evidence, you should be very unwilling to admit), he is a more proper object of your compassion than of your anger! Alas! "He knows not what he does!" But you know who has made you to differ from him. If God, in his sovereign pleasure, had so appointed, you might have been as he is now; and he, instead of you, might have been set for the defense of the gospel! You were both equally blind by nature. If you attend to this, you will not reproach or hate him, because the Lord has been pleased to open your eyes—and not his!

Of all people who engage in controversy, we, who are called Calvinists, are most expressly bound by our own principles, to the exercise of gentleness and compassion. If, indeed, those who differ from us have a power of changing themselves, if they can open their own eyes, and soften their own hearts—then we might with less inconsistency be offended at their obstinacy! But if we believe the very contrary to this, our part is not to argue, but in meekness to "gently teach those who oppose the truth—if perhaps God will grant them repentance leading them to a knowledge of the truth."

If you write with a desire of being an instrument of correcting mistakes, you will of course be cautious of laying stumbling blocks in the way of the blind, or of using any expressions which may exasperate their passions, or confirm them in their false principles, (humanly speaking).

2. By PRINTING your article, you will appeal to the PUBLIC—where your readers may be ranged under three divisions:
First, such as differ from you in principle. Concerning these I may refer you to what I have already said. Though you have your eye upon one person chiefly—there are many like-minded with him; and the same reasoning will hold, whether as to one or to a million.

There will be likewise many who pay too little regard to true religion, who have no settled system of their own, and yet are biased in favor of those sentiments which are at least repugnant to the good opinion they naturally have of themselves. These are very incompetent judges of doctrine; but they can form a tolerable judgment of a writer's spirit. They know that meekness, humility and love are the characteristics of a Christian temper. And though they treat the doctrines of grace as mere notions and speculations, which, supposing they adopted them, would have no beneficial influence upon their conduct; yet from us, who profess these principles, they always expect such attitudes and dispositions as correspond with the precepts of the gospel. They are quick-sighted to discern when we deviate from such a spirit, and avail themselves of it to justify their contempt of our arguments.

The Scriptural maxim that "man's anger does not bring about the righteous life that God desires," is verified by daily observation. If our zeal is embittered by expressions of anger, invective, or scorn—we may think we are doing service of the cause of truth, when in reality we shall only bring it into discredit! The weapons of our warfare, and which alone are powerful to break down the strongholds of error, are not carnal, but spiritual. They are arguments fairly drawn from Scripture and experience, and enforced by such a mild address, as may persuade our readers, that, whether we can convince them or not—we wish well to their souls, and contend only for the truth's sake. If we can satisfy them that we act upon these motives, our point is half gained; they will be more disposed to consider calmly what we offer; and if they should still dissent from our opinions, they will be constrained to approve our intentions.

You will have a third class of readers, who being of your own sentiments, will readily approve of what you advance, and may be further established and confirmed in their views of the Scripture doctrines, by a clear and masterly elucidation of your subject. You may be instrumental to their edification, if the law of kindness as well as of truth regulates your pen; otherwise you may do them harm.

There is a principle of SELF, which disposes us to despise those who differ from us; and we are often under its influence, when we think we are only showing a fitting zeal in the cause of God.

I readily believe that the leading points of Arminianism spring from and are nourished by the pride of the human heart! But I would be glad if the reverse were always true; and that to embrace what are called the Calvinistic doctrines was an infallible token of a humble mind! I think I have known some Arminians, that is, people who for lack of a clearer light, have been afraid of receiving the doctrines of free grace, who yet have given evidence that their hearts were in a degree humbled before the Lord. And I am afraid there are Calvinists, who, while they account it a proof of their humility, that they are willing in words to debase the creature and to give all the glory of salvation to the Lord—yet are of a prideful, harsh and bitter spirit. Whatever it is that makes us trust in ourselves, that we are comparatively wise or good, so as to treat those with contempt who do not subscribe to our doctrines, or follow our party—is a proof and fruit of a self-righteous spirit!

Self-righteousness can feed upon doctrines—as well as upon works! A man may have the heart of a Pharisee, while his head is stored with orthodox notions of the unworthiness of the creature, and the riches of free grace!

Yes, I would add—the best of men are not wholly free from this leaven; and therefore are too apt to be pleased with such caricatures as hold up our adversaries to ridicule—and by consequence flatter our own superior judgments. Controversies, for the most part, are so managed as to indulge—rather than to repress this sinful disposition; and therefore, generally speaking, they are productive of little good. They provoke those whom they should convince—and puff up those whom they should edify!

I hope your article will savor of a spirit of true humility, and be a means of promoting it in others.

3. This leads me, in the last place, to consider your own concern in your present undertaking. It seems a laudable service to defend the faith once delivered to the saints; we are commanded to contend earnestly for it, and to convince gainsayers. If ever such defenses were seasonable and expedient, they appear to be so in our own day, when errors abound on all sides—and every truth of the gospel is either directly denied or grossly misrepresented.

And yet we find but very few writers of controversy who have not been manifestly hurt by it. Either they grow in a sense of their own importance; or imbibe an angry, contentious spirit; or they insensibly withdraw their attention from those spiritual truths which are the food and immediate support of the life of faith—and spend their time and strength upon matters that are at most but of a secondary value! This shows, that if the service is honorable, it is also dangerous. What will it profit a man if he gains his cause and silences his adversary—if at the same time he loses that humble, tender frame of spirit in which the Lord delights, and to which the promise of his presence is made?

Your aim, I doubt not, is good, but you have need to watch and pray—for you will find Satan at your right hand to entice you. He will try to pollute your piety; and though you set out in defense of the cause of God, if you are not continually looking to the Lord to keep you—it may become your own cause, and awaken in you those tempers which are inconsistent with true peace of mind, and will surely obstruct your communion with God! Be upon your guard against admitting anything personal into the debate. If you think you have been ill treated—this will give you an opportunity of showing that you are a disciple of Jesus, who "when reviled—He did not revile in return; when suffering—He did not threaten, but committed Himself to the One who judges justly." This is our pattern, thus we are to speak and write for God, and "not paying back evil for evil or insult for insult—but, on the contrary, giving a blessing, since you were called for this."

The wisdom that is from above, is not only pure, but also peaceable and gentle; and the lack of these qualifications, like the dead fly in the jar of ointment, will spoil the fragrance and efficacy of our labors. If we act in a wrong spirit—we shall bring little glory to God; do little good to our fellow creatures; and procure neither honor nor comfort to ourselves! If you can be content with showing your wit, and gaining the laugh on your side—you have an easy task!

But I hope you have a far nobler aim; and that, sensible of the solemn importance of gospel truths, and the compassion due to the souls of men, you would rather be a means of removing prejudices in a single instance, than obtain the empty applause of thousands! 

Go forth, therefore, in the name and strength of the Lord Almighty, speaking the truth in love; and may he give you a witness in many hearts that you are taught of God, and favored with the unction of his Holy Spirit!

Russian documents Set out 'tectonic weapon' research
Carl Levitin

Moscow. The first official details have emerged in Moscow of ambitious research into 'tectonic warfare' carried out by the former Soviet Union and subsequently by the government of Russia, and involving atte mpts to stimulate 'artificial' earthquakes as weapons of destruction. According to documents obtained by the newspaper Moscow News, two research programmes, the first known as ' Mercury ' and the second as ' Volcano', were aimed at creating new earthquake epicentres by using underground nuclear explosions . Geophysicists are aware that impending earthquakes may be triggered by underground nuclear explosions . But Western geophysicists remain sceptical about tectonic warfare and have all but abandoned research after two unsuccessful phases of activity in the 1960s and 1980s, says Roger Clark, a lecturer in geophysics at the University of Leeds. Clark is not at all surprised that th e Russians tried to create earthquakes and control their location electromagnetically, however. "This sort of science is very much part of their heritage. We don't think it is impossible, or wrong , but past experience suggests it is very, very unlikely. "

The programme , which was secretly launched by the Communist rulers of the former Soviet Union in 1987, and has been unofficially known to Western geophysicists for several years, is now believed to have been abandoned. It would certainly contravene the terms of the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty, which Russia signe d at the United Nations in Geneva last month . The Mercury project was launched in the former Soviet republic of Azerbaijan, but came to a halt when the republic became independent. It was superseded by the Volcano project. Three underground nuclear tests are believed to have taken place at sites in Kyrgyzstan.

According to the documents, the Mercury project was launched by a secret decree of the Central Committee of the Communist Party and the Council of Ministers of the Soviet Union. The objective was to "develop a methodology for remote operation on an earthquake epicentre by using weak seismic fields and research possibilities of transferring the seismic energy of an explosion ".

The documents say that the Mercury project involved 22 scientific and industrial organizations, including the Geological Institute of the Azerbaijan Academy of Sciences in Baku. The remit extended to developing the electronic equipment to be installed aboard space satellites that would control the tectonic weapon. The scientists were given three years to complete research, with testing planned for 1990.

During the research phase, Azerbaijani scientists grew increasingly confident and, according to the documents, were sure that " after [a] nuclear explosion, subterranean energy may accumulate at huge distances from the epicentre and reach massive capacity, after which the next directed explosion can release it all ".

Underground testing began at the town of Batken in Kyrgyzstan, and was directed by lkram Ke rimov , of the Azerbaijan Academy of Sciences. The documents say that scientists detonated an underground nuclear charge and tried to control the direction of seismic energy release d using British-built equipment known as 'system 9690 ' .

A report prepared by the Mozhaisky Military Engineering Institute concluded that the test had been a success. But progress slowed considerably following Azerbaijan's independence from the Soviet Union. At about this time , Russia embarked on a more comprehensive tectonic warfare programme known as the Volcano project. The Earth Physics Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences (RAS) became the project headquarters .

Research was scheduled to be completed in 1992, with underground testing beginning the following year. The final test was carried out at a place code-named S36NZ-0Kh; Moscow News believes the letters 'NZ' refer to Novaya Zemlya, where Soviet nuclear testing began in the 1950s."

Harry R. Truman (October 30, 1896 – May 18, 1980) was an American businessman, bootlegger, and prospector. After Mount St. Helens awoke from dormancy in March 1980, Truman became a folk hero in the weeks leading to the volcano's May eruption, refusing to evacuate his home despite repeated orders from authorities. On May 18, 1980, Truman was killed in the cataclysmic eruption of Mount St. Helens by a pyroclastic flow that overtook his lodge and buried the site under 150 ft (46 m) of volcanic debris.

text:
October 19, 202 BC. Zama, in North Africa. Hannibal finally loses.

For sixteen years Hannibal had haunted Rome. He crossed the Alps with elephants, crushed army after army, and won at Cannae the most perfect victory of the ancient world. But Rome refused to give up. So a young general named Publius Cornelius Scipio took the war to Africa, straight at Carthage itself. Hannibal was called home to save his city.

Before the battle, the two commanders reportedly met face to face between the armies. Hannibal offered peace. Scipio turned him down.

Hannibal opened with 80 war elephants. Scipio had prepared for them. He lined up his legions with open lanes between the units. When the elephants charged, Roman trumpets blared, the animals panicked, and many either stampeded harmlessly down the lanes or turned back into the Carthaginian ranks.

Then the infantry met in a brutal grinding fight. Hannibal held his best men, the veterans who had followed him through Italy, in reserve for the end. It was nearly enough.

But Scipio's cavalry, led by the Numidian king Masinissa, who had switched sides to Rome, had chased the Carthaginian horsemen off the field. They came back just in time and slammed into Hannibal's veterans from behind.

Carthage surrendered. It gave up its fleet, paid a fortune in silver, and could never again wage war without Rome's permission. Scipio earned a new name: Africanus.

text:
The population did not retreat. On August 8, 1988, a nationwide strike brought students, monks, civil servants, workers and other citizens into demonstrations demanding democracy and an end to military domination. The date gave the movement its enduring name: the 8888 Uprising. Large crowds appeared in Rangoon and other cities, presenting the government with a challenge far beyond the student protests that had begun months earlier. Army units and security forces fired on demonstrators. Contemporary reports and later investigations describe large-scale killings, although the exact number of people who died remains disputed. The violence did not simply restore confidence in the government; it deepened the political crisis and expanded opposition to military rule.

Ne Win's departure from the party leadership had therefore failed to resolve the central issue. The country was demanding a political system in which the armed forces no longer determined who could govern. Figures associated with the old order remained influential, and the military establishment retained the power to intervene. On September 18, a group of officers headed by General Saw Maung seized direct control and established the State Law and Order Restoration Council. A new wave of repression followed. Human rights organizations have documented thousands of deaths across the months of demonstrations and military crackdowns, while many activists were arrested or forced into exile.

The July speech remains chilling because it expressed the coercive logic of the regime so openly. Ne Win offered the possibility of political reform while warning that the army would answer unrest with lethal force. The government eventually changed its name and leadership, but the military retained control through another ruling council. The democratic opening sought by the demonstrators did not follow the 1988 uprising. Instead, the warning that soldiers would shoot became inseparable from the repression that followed it.

Ukraine’s government will partially compensate civilian vessels damaged by Russian strikes in the Black Sea as Kyiv and foreign partners discuss stabilizing shipping routes amid Russian attacks on both foreign and Ukrainian ships.

Under a mechanism developed by Ukraine’s Infrastructure Ministry, Kyiv will compensate shipowners, operators, and charterers whose vessels fly under the Ukrainian or a foreign flag for up to 80% of the assessed damage if insurers don’t cover the risks.

The mechanism will cover damage to or destruction of ships, loss of or damage to cargo, and emergency and rescue operation costs.

"This decision is intended to reduce financial risks for participants in maritime shipping and to support the continuity of Ukraine’s export and import logistics," the Infrastructure Ministry wrote in a public statement.

"Despite the constant threats, Ukraine’s maritime logistics keeps operating. Our task is to ensure its stability and to create additional guarantees for shipowners carrying cargo to Ukrainian ports."

With the hostilities in the Black Sea threatening global food supplies, Turkey, India, and Egypt offered to transport food from both Ukrainian and Russian ports under their respective flags, but Moscow declined to guarantee them safe passage, President Volodymyr Zelensky told Bloomberg on Oct. 19.

Some in the logistics sector are skeptical that talks between foreign partners and Russia will yield results anytime soon.

Russia stepped up attacks on cargo ships in the Black Sea over the summer, hitting 52 vessels in just six weeks in July and August. While ships are now largely avoiding Ukrainian ports, Russia hasn’t stopped its attacks, with Romania accusing Moscow of hitting four merchant ships in 24 hours on Oct. 15, killing eight people.

As a result, insurance rates in the Black Sea are through the roof, with London’s marine insurance market expanding its high-risk zone beyond the coastal waters of Ukraine and Russia on Sept. 18, Reuters reported.

Russia's attacks on vessels, as well as port facilities, have effectively halted Ukraine’s agricultural exports, putting around 32 million metric tons of agricultural products worth approximately $10 billion at risk, Ukraine’s Agriculture Ministry said last week. Alternative routes, such as the Danube River ports and railways, cannot handle enough cargo.

Washington State 

2026 MIDTERM ELECTION 

Ballots found tossed on a Burien (King County) roadside days after Washington mailed them; what to do if yours is missing

Oct. 19, 2026

General election ballots were found scattered along a Burien roadside with other discarded mail Saturday, according to photos sent to The Jason Rantz Show on Seattle Red, and Washington voters who suspect theirs went missing have until 8 p.m. on November 3 to get a replacement that counts.

A Seattle Red reader shared the photos, which a family member took at about 1:10 p.m. on the side of South 128th Street between 12th Avenue South and 14th Avenue South. He was driving at the time.

“He didn’t have time to stop and pick them up. He just took a quick picture and sent them to me. He said its likely someone just went through peoples mail and tossed them to the ground. It’s an absolute shame,” the reader wrote in an email to Seattle Red.

It is not clear whose ballots they were or how they ended up on the roadside. Seattle Red previously reported Jim Walsh’s claim that hundreds of undelivered King County ballots turned up near a Renton strip mall dumpster. Residents who think their mail was taken can report it to the U.S. Postal Inspection Service.

Voters who think their ballot was in the pile don’t need to wait for answers. Replacing it takes minutes, and state rules keep a stolen ballot from becoming a second vote.

How to replace a missing or damaged ballot

Counties mailed ballots by October 16, according to the state voters’ pamphlet. If yours never showed up, or got torn or stained, start at https://t.co/2TxIVkmVoi, the Secretary of State’s voter portal. Confirm your registration and mailing address, then print a replacement ballot. Mark it and sign the declaration on the return envelope; county election workers compare that signature with the one on your registration record before the ballot is counted.

No envelope? Counties offer a printable return envelope that voters assemble with tape or glue, and King County Elections posts its replacement packet online. A return envelope sealed too early can usually still be used if you carefully open it and reseal it with a small piece of tape.

No printer? Call or visit your county elections office, or go to a vote center. In King County, the number is 206-296-VOTE (8683), and the elections office is at 919 Southwest Grady Way in Renton. Under state election rules, a voter, a family member or a registered domestic partner can request a replacement in person, in writing, by phone or electronically, as long as the request comes in before 8 p.m. on Election Day.

What happens to a stolen or lost ballot

Once a replacement is issued, it becomes your current ballot and the original is suspended. If the original reaches the elections office first, that one gets processed, but only after it passes the same signature check. After one ballot is accepted, any others from the same voter are set aside and not counted.

After you return a ballot, VoteWA shows when your county received it. If it never shows as received, request a replacement.

Mailed ballots must be postmarked by Election Day, and the U.S. Postal Service recommends mailing at least a week early. A ballot in an official drop box by 8 p.m. on November 3 is guaranteed on time, which is why Secretary of State Steve Hobbs is urging voters to skip the mail and use a drop box. Washington’s problem with late ballots predates the Trump-era postal changes Democrats now blame.

Not registered yet? Online and mail registrations must be received by October 26. After that, you can still register in person at your county elections office until 8 p.m. on Election Day.

text:
Republican Pat Proctor is actively trying to undermine trust in Kansas elections while people are already casting their votes and just days before Election Night.

And he’s doing it while running for Secretary of State, the very office responsible for overseeing those elections.

Proctor has repeatedly made alarming claims about illegal voting, election conspiracies, voting-rights organizations and the integrity of Kansas elections.

But what happens when we compare his rhetoric with the actual law and evidence?

🔴 NONCITIZEN VOTING: Proctor suggests Topeka and Lawrence might allow noncitizens to vote.

FACT: Kansas laws and constitution already prohibit noncitizens from voting at any election. Neither city has an identified proposal to allow it.

🔴 FEDERAL COURT RULING: Proctor points to a federal judge’s ruling as evidence that Kansas needs his constitutional amendment.

FACT: The Florida ruling involved a very specific federal criminal case. It cannot invalidate Kansas election law or authorize noncitizens to vote here.

🔴 LEAGUE OF WOMEN VOTERS: Proctor has portrayed the League as part of an organized effort to undermine elections.

FACT: The League is a nonpartisan civic organization. The dispute concerns $5 Starbucks gift cards offered at student voter-registration events, not votes for any candidate. No broader election conspiracy has been established.

🔴 VOTER ROLLS: Proctor has highlighted claims that Kansas has more elderly registered voters than elderly residents.

FACT: The comparison included inactive registrations and older Census estimates. It does not establish that deceased individuals voted or fraudulent ballots were cast.

🔴 ELECTION CONSPIRACIES: Proctor repeatedly warns about noncitizen voting, yet recently acknowledged:

“There’s not a vast conspiracy for noncitizen votes in the state of Kansas.”

🔴 WOMEN VOTING: During the 2022 abortion amendment election, Proctor described young women turning out to vote as:

“They’re stealing it fair and square.”

FACT: Those women were exercising their constitutional rights. Kansas voters rejected the amendment 59% to 41%.

⸻

There is a difference between protecting election integrity and undermining public confidence in elections.

Proctor has every right to advocate for changes to election laws and campaign for his constitutional amendment.

But Kansans also deserve to know when his claims are unsupported, misleading or missing important legal context.

The consequences extend beyond one campaign or one amendment.

When a candidate seeking to oversee elections repeatedly suggests that lawful voting, voter-registration efforts, court challenges and unproven allegations are evidence of a compromised system, it raises serious questions about the public’s confidence in election administration.

Kansas voters are already making decisions. Election Day is November 3.

This is precisely when accuracy, transparency and responsible public statements matter most.

Our elections belong to the voters, not the candidates.

🇺🇸 Kansas deserves facts, not fear.

DES MOINES, Iowa — More than 400 cold cases remain under investigation in Iowa, and new funding could help investigators uncover answers in cases that have gone unsolved for years.

Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird announced Monday that the Attorney General’s Office Cold Case Unit has received a $15,000 Community Betterment Grant from the Prairie Meadows Board of Directors.

The funding will support advanced DNA testing as investigators work alongside local law enforcement agencies to revisit unresolved cases across the state.

Bird said the additional resources could help investigators pursue new leads and potentially bring long-awaited answers to families and communities.

The Cold Case Unit works with law enforcement agencies throughout Iowa to give unsolved investigations renewed attention.

For families who have spent years waiting for answers, advances in DNA technology could offer another opportunity for progress.

text:
THE YOUNG MAN WHO FELL THREE STORIES — AND WAS CARRIED HOME ALIVE

The Extraordinary Account of Eutychus and the Apostle Paul — Troas, First Century AD

A young man falls from a third-story window during a Christian gathering. Those who reach him find him apparently lifeless. Grief threatens to overwhelm the congregation.

Then the apostle Paul descends, embraces the young man, and announces something astonishing.

The young man is alive.

Recorded in Acts 20:7–12, this remarkable event offers more than an account of extraordinary recovery. It directs our attention toward Jesus Christ, the Lord of life, whose resurrection transformed the early Church's understanding of death itself.

A NIGHT OF FELLOWSHIP IN TROAS

The setting was Troas, an important port city in northwestern Asia Minor, present-day Turkey, during Paul's missionary travels, probably in the AD 50s.

Paul was preparing to leave the following morning. On the first day of the week, believers assembled upstairs to break bread and hear his teaching.

This glimpse of early Christian worship reveals a community devoted to fellowship, instruction, and shared meals.

Paul continued speaking until midnight.

Among those listening was Eutychus, a young man sitting in a window. As the evening progressed, he fell into a deep sleep.

Then disaster struck.

THE FALL THAT CHANGED EVERYTHING

Acts 20:9 (NIV) records that Eutychus fell from the third story and "was picked up dead."

Imagine the congregation rushing downstairs, the gathering suddenly transformed from worship into alarm.

Paul immediately went down, bent over the young man, and embraced him.

"Don't be alarmed," he said. "He's alive!" (Acts 20:10, NIV).

Luke then records a remarkable conclusion:

"The people took the young man home alive and were greatly comforted." (Acts 20:12, NIV).

There is no elaborate celebration described, no lengthy explanation of what happened, and no attempt by Paul to glorify himself.

The account emphasizes restored life, comfort, and the continuation of Christian fellowship.

RESURRECTION OR EXTRAORDINARY RECOVERY?

Historical integrity requires an important distinction.

Acts explicitly describes Eutychus as having been picked up dead, and its narrative presents his restoration as extraordinary.

However, no independent medical records, examination findings, or modern clinical confirmation survive.

Some interpreters understand the event as an actual raising from the dead. Others consider whether the young man might have been unconscious or mistakenly presumed dead.

Neither interpretation can be established through modern medical testing.

Our evidence is the biblical testimony preserved in Acts, not a contemporary medical investigation.

The passage also belongs to one of Acts' first-person travel sections, traditionally associated with Luke's participation in Paul's journeys. This strengthens its character as a travel narrative, although it does not provide independent medical verification.

Christian faith need not exaggerate the evidence to appreciate the extraordinary event Scripture describes.

THE GREATER POWER BEHIND THE SIGN

Paul's actions recall the prophets Elijah and Elisha, who were associated with restorations to life in 1 Kings 17:17–24 and 2 Kings 4:32–37.

They also direct our attention toward Jesus.

In Luke 7:11–17, Christ encounters a funeral procession at Nain and restores a widow's only son to life.

In John 11, Jesus calls Lazarus from the tomb.

These accounts reveal a profound biblical truth: death does not possess authority greater than God.

Jesus declared:

"I am the resurrection and the life." (John 11:25, NIV).

Yet there is a crucial distinction.

Those restored to earthly life would eventually face death again. Jesus Christ rose from the dead into resurrection life, never to die again (Romans 6:9).

His victory is the foundation of Christian hope.

A MIRACLE WITH A QUIET MESSAGE

One easily overlooked detail is the congregation's response.

They were "greatly comforted."

The Greek wording emphasizes substantial encouragement and consolation.

The miracle was not presented as entertainment or an opportunity for religious fame.

It brought comfort to ordinary believers.

Through the risen Son, God the Father gives hope beyond the grave, while the Holy Spirit strengthens the Church to bear witness to Christ.

The same Gospel that sustained those early Christians continues to offer hope to believers today.

Yet faith does not guarantee that every sickness will be healed or every earthly life prolonged.

Our ultimate promise is greater: resurrection through Jesus Christ.

THE VICTORY THAT DEATH CANNOT DEFEAT

Eutychus went home alive. Paul continued his journey. The Church continued proclaiming the Gospel.

But the greatest resurrection had already occurred.

Jesus Christ had conquered the grave.

As 1 Corinthians 15:54 declares, "Death has been swallowed up in victory."

For Christians, death is a terrible enemy, but not the final authority.

Our confidence rests not in extraordinary stories alone, but in the crucified and risen Savior.

REFLECTION QUESTIONS

Does my confidence rest primarily in miracles, or in Jesus Christ Himself?

How can I bring Christ's comfort to someone facing grief or uncertainty?

Am I living with the eternal hope made possible by His resurrection?

CLOSING PRAYER

Heavenly Father, thank You for revealing Your power and compassion through Jesus Christ. Lord Jesus, strengthen our faith in Your victory over sin and death. Holy Spirit, comfort grieving hearts, give us wisdom to discern truth, and fill us with resurrection hope. Teach us to treasure every life, serve others humbly, and trust Your promises even in suffering. May our lives glorify the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, now and forever. In Jesus' mighty name, Amen.

Scriptural source: Acts 20:7–12 (NIV); supporting passages: Luke 7:11–17; John 11:25–26; Romans 6:9; 1 Corinthians 15:20–26, 54–57.

Historical classification: Biblical resurrection narrative; no surviving independent medical confirmation.

text:
Biped bot uses your old, dusty phone for brains | Omar Kardoudi, New Atlas

That old phone gathering dust in a drawer could have a second life far more entertaining than being a paperweight. UCLA researchers have created PhoneBot, a little humanoid that puts your smartphone to work as the brains of a walking robot companion.

The little walker comes from the Robotics and Mechanisms Laboratory (RoMeLa) at the University of California, Los Angeles. In a preprint posted to arXiv, the team describes a bipedal robot that uses a smartphone as its torso, eyes, and brain.

The idea is to skip the costly extras. Small research humanoids usually need separate sensors, a vision computer, and a lot of wiring. PhoneBot borrows all of that from the handset. The camera handles sight, and the phone's inertial measurement unit (IMU), a chip that senses tilt and motion, works like an inner ear for balance. The processor runs the neural network that drives the joints, and the touchscreen shows status and controls.

The body stands 48.3 cm (19 in) tall and weighs 1.8 kg (4 lb), phone and battery included. It has 13 low-cost servo motors, six per leg, plus one that swivels the torso. That swivel lets the camera turn to follow a person without the whole robot pivoting.

The phone isn't wired to the body. It talks to a small onboard computer over Wi-Fi, which relays commands to the motors. The researchers say this makes it easier to swap in different phone models.

Before taking its first real steps, PhoneBot practiced in a virtual world using reinforcement learning – essentially trial and error with a scorecard. It earned points for keeping pace, alternating its steps, and staying upright, and lost them for bad habits like dragging its feet. The simulation accounted for the real motors’ limited strength and speed, as well as the play in their gears, so the robot learned moves its body could actually pull off in real life. On the real robot, the team demonstrated walking, following a person with the camera and standing up from lying face down.

Conversation isn't fully self-contained yet. Speech recognition and the language model run on a nearby laptop, which the phone reaches over Wi-Fi. Walking and vision run on the phone itself.

The researchers tested PhoneBot on four Android phones: a 2017 Honor 9 and three prepaid models bought for about $50 to $80. All ran the core functions, including motion sensing, walking control, on-device vision, and interaction.

One gap is that camera-based mapping and localization (SLAM) didn't run on the Honor 9, which the researchers attribute to Google services being unavailable on that device in the US. Still, the paper does not establish that PhoneBot will work with every Android phone.

For now, PhoneBot has no arms, and its walking was trained only on flat ground. Its small motors also limit how much weight it can carry and which moves it can pull off. The team plans to explore uneven terrain, lightweight arms and language-model-based planning that turns spoken instructions and visual information into robot actions. The researchers also suggest running suitable language models directly on the smartphone to reduce reliance on the laptop currently handling conversation.

The hardware and software are open source and aimed at education, research, and tinkering. The paper presents PhoneBot as a platform others can build and experiment with, rather than a finished household companion. Or at least not just yet.

The team estimates PhoneBot’s cost at roughly US$400, excluding the smartphone. Other small research humanoids listed in the paper range from about $3,500 to $13,800. Those platforms offer different capabilities, so this is not a direct comparison, but PhoneBot would make bipedal robotics accessible on a considerably smaller budget.

He calls Glendale “where I grew up basically in this league.” He faced adversity there in his first couple of seasons, met lifelong friends, and still has staff members there who mean a lot to him.

He credits Vance Joseph for his whole career: “I really don’t think I’d be in this position without him.” 

J.J. Watt shaped him. Allen says Watt “was really generous with his time” during his farewell run, teaching him both how to be a pro and actual technique.

His first year in Denver is when he realized he could be an All-Pro, because it was the first time he played without J.J. Watt on the other side.

Free agency was “a little bit of a leap of faith.” He wanted a storied franchise and a fan base that was all in: “You feel like you have this responsibility to the fans to perform at a high level.”

Denver was on his list before any offers came in. He and his wife made a wish list for fun, Denver was on it, and when it worked out, “it was almost kind of like a sign.” He also talked to Justin Simmons, a fellow Boston College alum, about the team, the city and the fans.

text:
Quenton Nelson needs to be a Seattle Seahawk before the trade deadline.

John Schneider needs to get on the phone with Ed Dodds, beat Kansas City to the punch, and explore what could become the offensive equivalent of the Leonard Williams trade.

I genuinely believe this could be one of the most impactful moves Seattle makes during its championship window.

And the circumstances are almost eerily similar to 2023.

THE LEONARD WILLIAMS BLUEPRINT

In 2023, Schneider identified an opportunity to acquire an elite interior defensive lineman from a struggling Giants organization.

Williams was 29, approaching free agency, and available at a point when New York had to start thinking about its future.

Seattle surrendered a second-round pick and a future fifth, with New York absorbing much of the remaining salary.

Schneider wasn’t simply buying a few months of production. He was acquiring a proven player he believed could become a foundational piece.

Williams eventually signed an extension, became an indispensable part of Seattle’s defensive front, and helped anchor a Super Bowl championship defense.

Now imagine applying that exact philosophy to the other side of the line of scrimmage.

WHY INDIANAPOLIS SHOULD LISTEN

Chris Ballard is gone. The Colts are 2-4. The organization is facing a potential change in direction, and Quenton Nelson is 30 years old, playing on an expiring contract.

Nelson is still an exceptional football player, but Indianapolis has to consider the opportunity cost of retaining an expensive veteran if the next regime wants to rebuild.

A trade could accomplish three things:

1. Recover premium draft capital before Nelson reaches free agency.
2. Create additional financial flexibility.
3. Give the next GM another valuable asset to accelerate the construction of a younger roster.

This doesn’t mean Indianapolis HAS to trade him. It means Seattle should present an offer compelling enough to make them seriously consider it.

And there’s another connection here that cannot be overlooked.

ED DODDS AND JOHN SCHNEIDER

Dodds spent a decade in Seattle’s personnel department, including years working alongside Schneider during the construction of the Seahawks’ original championship roster.

He understands Schneider’s evaluation philosophy, how Seattle approaches roster construction, and what the organization values.

Now Dodds is overseeing Indianapolis’s personnel decisions.

That doesn’t guarantee a trade or a discount, but established relationships matter when negotiating complicated deals.

If there’s an opportunity, Schneider should be among the first people making that call.

WHY THIS COULD TRANSFORM SEATTLE’S OFFENSE

Seattle already has the foundation of a very good offensive line.

Charles Cross at LT.
Grey Zabel at LG.
Abe Lucas at RT.

But the interior remains an area where Seattle could meaningfully raise its ceiling.

Here’s what makes Nelson particularly intriguing.

Nelson steps in at left guard, while Zabel’s positional versatility potentially allows Seattle to move him to right guard.

Suddenly, you’re not simply replacing one starter with another. You’re potentially improving TWO positions through ONE acquisition.

Cross, Nelson, Sundell, Zabel, Lucas.

Think about what that could mean for this offense.

Better interior pass protection gives Sam Darnold cleaner pockets and more opportunities to work through progressions without immediate pressure up the middle.

Better interior run blocking creates more consistent movement at the point of attack, giving Seattle a chance to establish the physical rushing identity it has struggled to maintain.

And perhaps most importantly, it gives Brian Fleury greater flexibility in how he attacks defenses.

When you can consistently win inside, defenses have to respect your ability to run between the tackles. That creates opportunities for play-action, deeper developing routes, and more favorable situations on early downs.

It isn’t just about making the offensive line better.

It’s about removing limitations from the entire offense.

THE CHAMPIONSHIP WINDOW

Seattle is coming off a Super Bowl championship.

This isn’t a team hoping to become competitive three years from now. This is an organization trying to maximize a roster that has already demonstrated it can win at the highest level.

And we just saw how valuable Leonard Williams became when Seattle invested in a proven difference-maker instead of waiting for an uncertain draft pick to develop.

The same principle applies here.

If the acquisition cost is reasonable, and Seattle can establish a path toward an extension, a second-round pick for an established All-Pro could be an outstanding investment.

Especially if that player helps stabilize multiple positions and improves the efficiency of the entire offense.

The risk is real. Nelson is 30, the extension would be expensive, and moving Zabel would require an adjustment.

But championship teams have to recognize when the potential return justifies taking that risk.

THE BOTTOM LINE

Indianapolis gets valuable draft capital and flexibility for its next chapter.

Seattle gets an established All-Pro who could immediately change the complexion of its offensive line and help extend its championship window.

Schneider already proved this strategy can work with Leonard Williams.

Now he has an opportunity to explore doing it again, this time on offense.

The front-office connection. The expiring contract. The organizational uncertainty. The positional opportunity. The championship window.

It all makes too much sense not to investigate aggressively.

Make the call, John.

Utah Mammoth vs Pittsburgh Penguins — Utah's strong start meets a Penguins road trip going wrong

Preview · NHL · Regular season · Monday 19 October 2026

Pittsburgh finished last season slightly ahead of Utah, and the two teams won one game each against each other. This season has gone very differently. Utah are 6-3-0 and fourth in the Western Conference. The Penguins are 3-5-1, arrive from defeats in Denver and Las Vegas on Friday and Saturday, and are 1-4-1 on the road. Utah at medium confidence.

THE MATCHUP

Pittsburgh ended 2025-26 on 98 points at 41-25-16, second in the Metropolitan, and lost their first-round series 2-4 to Philadelphia. Utah finished on 92 points at 43-33-6, fourth in the Central, and went out 2-4 to Vegas in the first round.

Clayton Keller had 88 points for Utah last season and Dylan Guenther 40 goals. This season Nick Schmaltz has six goals and 11 points in nine games, Keller 11 points and Mikhail Sergachev ten. For Pittsburgh, Sidney Crosby had 74 points last season. This season Erik Karlsson leads them with nine points, all assists, and Evgeni Malkin has five goals.

FORM & CONTEXT

Utah are 6-3-0, with 33 goals for and 27 against, and 4-2-0 on the road and 2-1-0 at home. They beat Chicago 6-0 at home, won in Columbus, New Jersey, Buffalo and Edmonton, and beat Toronto 5-4 at home. On Saturday Edmonton beat them 6-2 in Salt Lake City. Karel Vejmelka is 5-2-0 with a .879 save percentage over seven starts.

Pittsburgh are 3-5-1, with 29 goals for and 33 against. They opened with a 7-0 win in Philadelphia and a 6-5 overtime win at home over Montréal. Since then they have beaten only Dallas, 2-1 in a shootout. The latest defeats were 3-5 in Chicago, 2-5 in Colorado on Friday and 2-6 in Vegas on Saturday. Arturs Silovs is at .875 over five starts and Sergei Murashov is 0-3-1 at .883.

The end of last season was close: Utah went 6-4-0 in their last ten and Pittsburgh 5-5-0. Both teams played on Saturday, so neither is on a back-to-back or has a rest advantage.

THE DECIDING FACTOR

The direction of the two seasons so far. Utah are 6-3-0, and 4-2-0 away from home. Pittsburgh are on a road trip that has gone badly, with 2-5 and 2-6 defeats this weekend, and their two goalies are at .875 and .883.

The head-to-head offers no lean. Utah won 5-4 in overtime in Pittsburgh on 14 December, and Pittsburgh won 4-3 in Salt Lake City on 14 March.

THE CALL

The final table is too close to count, and the series was split. Utah's start to this season and Pittsburgh's form on the road decide it, at medium.

Utah Mammoth to win, medium confidence.

text:
"Human in the Loop" -> Human on the Hook -> ???

Say an agent tries to finance GPUs. The bank needs a beneficial owner.

FinCEN's due-diligence rule: the bank must identify "a single individual with significant responsibility to control" the company.

Consider this shift from AI / cybernetic systems focused on "human in the loop" to "human on the hook." Interesting discussion.

Who makes the decision? Who is accountable when it's wrong? Whose assets cover the loss?

Software can make the decisions. Wyoming, Utah, Tennessee, and the Marshall Islands already let smart contracts manage a company. This was progress for Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAOs), which (usually) had little to do with AI at the time - but may be a useful framework in this next context.

Accountability - right now, buck stops with people and companies. Wyoming and the Marshall Islands can dissolve a DAO "no longer under the control of at least one natural person." 

California bars the defense that the AI acted on its own. The Ninth Circuit called an AI shopping agent "a tool, not a person." (Attorneys feel free to jump in, here. I'm no Saul Goodman).

Bermuda is working on this too. Draft guidance says using someone else's AI "does not transfer or diminish" a firm's accountability.

Liability is evolving. A DAO without a legal entity exposes its members: a federal court let claims proceed that Lido DAO is a general partnership, which can make active members personally liable. 

Bermuda's incorporated segregated accounts, Wyoming's DUNA and Utah's DAO law each create a separate legal entity and limit members' liability. The AI itself is not the defendant.

Agents can already pay. Stripe's Link wallet asks a human to approve each purchase. x402 lets an agent pay per request from a prefunded USDC wallet.

Agents can also borrow without KYC, through flash loans repaid within the same transaction and over-collateralized money markets like Aave and Morpho. Any wallet can borrow there, whether a bot, a DAO, or an agent.

Loans with recourse still require a named borrower. 3Jane offers uncollateralized credit lines to AI agents, underwritten on Plaid and Credit Karma data, with recourse against the borrower.

@USDai_Official  lends on-chain, but its recent $54.4M GPU loan went to a named company, Hydra Host, with the funds held in Wilmington Trust escrow until the GPUs were deployed and verified.

Lenders: underwrite the entity, its books and capital, and the signing officer.
Insurers: the policyholder is the company.
If you own an agent-run company: incorporate and keep company funds separate now. Commingled funds leave you personally liable despite whatever the charter says.
If you advise: confirm the bank's control person and that the contracts are with the entity.
If you build: build the documentation lenders and insurers accept.

text:
Outlier of the Day (2026-10-19): 

Arunachalam Muruganantham, The Village "Madman" Who Gave Millions of Women Their Dignity

Field: Social Entrepreneurship / Grassroots Innovation

In 1998, a newlywed welder in Tamil Nadu caught his wife Shanthi hiding something behind her back: dirty rags she used during her period. Store-bought pads, she told him, would mean less money for the family's food. Arunachalam Muruganantham could not let it go. That moment would cost him his marriage, his mother's trust, and his reputation before it made him world famous.

Born in Coimbatore in 1961 to handloom weavers, he grew up poor after his father died in a road accident. At 14 he left school and took whatever work came: delivering food to factory workers, farm labor, operating machine tools, welding. He had no degree and no laboratory.

He began making cotton pads for Shanthi. They failed. Women were too embarrassed to test them, so he tested them himself, wearing a pad connected to a football filled with animal blood. Neighbors called him a pervert and whispered he was diseased. In 2000 his wife left. His mother left too. He kept going.

His turning point was discovering that commercial pads used processed pine cellulose, and that the machines to make them cost hundreds of thousands of dollars. After roughly four and a half years of tinkering, he built a simple machine that grinds cellulose, presses, wraps and sterilizes pads, priced at a tiny fraction of imported equipment and runnable with minimal training.

It won a national innovation award in 2009, the year he patented it. Corporations offered to buy it. He refused, choosing instead to sell to rural women's self help groups through his company, Jayaashree Industries, so women could produce, sell and earn. TIME named him among its 100 Most Influential People in 2014, India awarded him the Padma Shri in 2016, and Bollywood immortalized him in the 2018 film Pad Man. Shanthi came back after seeing him on television.

Dos: Solve a problem you can see with your own eyes. Build for the people who need it most.
 Don'ts: Don't let ridicule decide your direction. Don't sell your mission to the highest bidder.

Competitive edge: Radical empathy plus a welder's hands. He turned a taboo into an engineering problem.

Perspective: Success is not what you earn; it is how many lives you change.

#PadMan #OutlierOfTheDay 
#SocialImpact #NeverGiveUp

text:
@Decibel_CC $DBCCF $DB.V 

Ewing Morris Proposes $5 Million Buyout for Decibel Cannabis Company

SEDAR FILING
https://t.co/kTu6a5fY8s
 
ANALYSIS
Ewing Morris & Co. Investment Partners has launched a limited all-cash offer for up to ~2.62 million shares of Decibel Cannabis Company Inc. (TSXV: DB / OTCQB: DBCCF) at $1.91 per share (total ~$5 million), a roughly 16.4% premium to the prior 20-day volume-weighted average price on the TSXV.

This is not a full buyout or formal takeover bid under Canadian securities laws. It is a partial tender structured to stay below the 20% threshold (capped at a maximum of 19.99% of outstanding shares, with pro-rata purchases if oversubscribed). The offer runs until November 6, 2026 (unless extended, varied, or withdrawn) and provides liquidity in an illiquid stock without commissions.

### Key Offer Details
- **Size**: Up to 2,617,801 shares (~6.8% of the ~38.47 million shares outstanding after the September 1, 2026, 15-for-1 consolidation).
- **Premium and liquidity rationale**: Ewing Morris highlights the stock’s long-term underperformance (roughly 52% decline over five years ending mid-October 2026; more than 97% below the adjusted January 2019 high of $60) and low average daily volume (~44,700 shares recently). The offer equates to roughly 59 days of liquidity at a premium.
- **Ewing Morris’s stated view**: The cannabis sector has suffered from excess capacity and lagged broader markets for years, making it hard for smaller companies to attract institutional interest. As a potential institutional holder, they aim to add stability to the shareholder base.
- **Company response**: CEO Benjamin Sze said the company was surprised but welcomed the interest as a positive sign for Decibel and the broader Canadian cannabis sector, while emphasizing continued focus on executing its plan and long-term shareholder value.

### Decibel’s Position and Fundamentals
Decibel operates cultivation, processing, and manufacturing facilities in Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Ontario (including an EU-GMP licensed site). It sells branded products (notably Qwest and General Admission) across Canada and exports dried flower, vapes, oils, and other formats to markets including Australia, Germany, the UK, Israel, and others. It recently entered a brand licensing deal for the UK medical market and has been consolidating operations (e.g., efforts around a BC facility sale for efficiency).

Recent results show improvement:
- Q2 FY2026 (ended June 30, 2026): Net revenue $35.6 million (+19% YoY), gross profit $18.1 million (+29%), net income $4.2 million (+154%). International sales $10.6 million (+72% YoY).
- Broader context: 2025 revenue ~$113 million (+22%); guidance for 2026 in the $130–135 million range. Adjusted EBITDA has grown, and the company refinanced with a $61 million facility (maturities to 2030). It has flagged a potential normal course issuer bid (share buyback).

The stock has traded in a depressed range long-term due to sector-wide issues (oversupply, price pressure, capital destruction post-2018/2019 boom). Near-term, it was around $1.60 prior to the announcement and rose on the news (trading toward the offer price in higher volume). Market cap is in the roughly $60–67 million CAD range, with the stock near book value and trading at a low price-to-sales multiple. Debt remains elevated relative to equity/cash.

### Analysis and Implications
This is an opportunistic minority stake and liquidity facility rather than a control transaction or endorsement of a transformative premium valuation. Ewing Morris (a Canadian boutique value-oriented firm focused on small/mid-cap inefficiencies, established 2011) is positioning for a stake in a company that has shown operational progress and international traction amid a still-challenged domestic market. Canadian cannabis continues to face excess capacity and competitive pressure domestically, with exports serving as a key growth and margin outlet for better-positioned players.

**For shareholders**:
- Positive for those seeking an exit at a premium in a low-liquidity name (especially long-term holders who have endured deep drawdowns).
- Neutral-to-mildly positive for remaining holders: Potential institutional ownership can support the base; the company continues executing on brands, international sales, cost discipline, and possible buybacks. The offer validates some level of external interest after years of sector neglect.
- Risks include oversubscription/proration, offer conditions, ongoing sector volatility, execution on international growth and debt service, and the fact that $1.91 is not a transformative re-rating relative to historical peaks or peak multiples.

The announcement has drawn modest attention (including from cannabis-focused market observers), with the stock reacting positively on the day. Overall, it reflects selective capital returning to relatively stronger Canadian operators focused on brands, efficiency, and exports rather than a broad sector revival or full privatization signal. Shareholders should review the formal offer documents (available via SEDAR+) for conditions, procedures, and details before deciding.

OCTOBER 19, 2026

USA POLITICS WATCH ALERT

DOJ CHARGES 28 GREEN CARD HOLDERS:
PERMANENT RESIDENCE IS NOT CITIZENSHIP

SUMMARY

The Department of Justice announced charges against 28 lawful permanent residents in California for alleged election offenses. Eleven were arrested October 19 under Operation Protect the Vote.

The cases raise questions about individual responsibility, registration safeguards and enforcement of federal election law.

A green card grants permanent residence, not U.S. citizenship or the right to vote in federal elections.

1. THE RESPONSIBILITY OF PERMANENT RESIDENTS

Lawful permanent residents have substantial rights and legal obligations.

One fundamental obligation is not to vote in federal elections before becoming U.S. citizens.

Under 18 U.S.C. §611, noncitizen voting in federal elections is generally prohibited, subject to narrow exceptions.

Permanent residents must know their citizenship status and answer registration questions truthfully.

Receiving registration forms, being offered registration or appearing on voter rolls does not establish eligibility.

The individual remains responsible for complying with the law.

2. WHAT PROSECUTORS ALLEGE

According to DOJ, all 28 defendants hold green cards.

Prosecutors allege false claims of citizenship on registration documents. Many allegedly voted in previous elections.

Some allegedly concealed registration or voting histories during naturalization proceedings.

Charges include unlawful voting, fraudulent registration and false statements.

Certain felony charges carry maximum penalties of five years in prison.

These are allegations, not convictions. All defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

3. CITIZENSHIP MUST BE EARNED LAWFULLY

Naturalization is the legal process through which eligible permanent residents become American citizens.

Years of residence, employment, tax payments or family relationships do not independently confer federal voting rights.

False citizenship claims and unlawful voting may also carry immigration consequences.

Applicants for citizenship must provide truthful information throughout naturalization.

4. HOW DID REGISTRATION SUCCEED?

DOJ alleges fraudulent registration applications were approved.

What verification procedures were used? Why did allegedly false citizenship declarations pass?

Prosecutors say the defendants appeared on a larger list of more than 20,000 people identified as likely noncitizens.

That number does not establish 20,000 illegal voters.

California disputes federal demands concerning the list, and litigation continues.

Verification must also protect naturalized citizens against erroneous data matches and wrongful exclusion.

5. ACCOUNTABILITY ON BOTH SIDES

Individuals must obey election laws. Government agencies must administer them accurately.

Proven violations warrant appropriate legal consequences. Allegations require proof in court.

Citizenship checks must also protect eligible American voters.

These 28 cases deserve transparent investigation and judicial resolution. They do not establish the nationwide prevalence of noncitizen voting.

The principle is straightforward:

Permanent residence is not citizenship.

A green card does not authorize voting in federal elections.

SOURCES

U.S. Department of Justice — October 19, 2026

18 U.S.C. §611 — Voting by Aliens
