U.S. Treasury Expands Whistleblower Program: Up to 30% of Recovered Funds for Reporting Fraud 

The U.S. Department of the Treasury, through its Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) Office of the Whistleblower, has formalized and publicized an expanded program encouraging Americans to report fraud, money laundering, sanctions violations, and related misconduct. 

Tips that lead to successful enforcement actions can result in awards of 10% to 30% of the monetary penalties collected by Treasury or the Department of Justice. 

The initiative aligns with the Trump administration’s broader push against waste, fraud, and abuse of taxpayer dollars, including efforts tied to the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) and the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud led by Vice President JD Vance. Treasury’s central hub at https://t.co/jLvn7R96It consolidates reporting options across FinCEN, the IRS, and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. 

Background and Scope
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has repeatedly emphasized following the money trail. In statements linked to high-profile fraud cases (including schemes in Minnesota involving government benefits programs), he noted that the department has historically pursued organized crime and cartels and is now applying similar scrutiny to large-scale benefits fraud.

The program focuses on:
•  Bank Secrecy Act violations and money laundering often connected to fraud schemes.
•  U.S. sanctions violations.
•  Tax-related violations (via the IRS Whistleblower Office, which has long offered awards in a similar 15–30% range of collected proceeds).
•  Misuse of federal funding, including through tax-exempt entities.

FinCEN launched a dedicated tip webpage in February 2026. In March 2026, it issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking to fully implement award procedures, eligibility criteria, and protections under existing statutes (the Anti-Money Laundering Act of 2020 and related laws). 

Awards generally apply when tips lead to enforcement actions producing monetary penalties above certain thresholds (reported as exceeding $1 million in some descriptions). Payments come from collected penalties, not general taxpayer funds. 

How to Report
Individuals with specific, actionable information—ideally supported by documentation—can submit tips through official channels:
•  FinCEN: https://t.co/Kpwc5tvXVa (or the linked whistleblower program page).
•  IRS Whistleblower Office for tax matters.
•  Other Treasury components as listed on the unified page.

Tips are treated confidentially to the extent possible, and the program includes protections against retaliation. Officials stress providing detailed, specific information rather than vague allegations.

Context and Expected Impact
The program is part of ongoing Treasury actions that also include enhanced scrutiny of money services businesses, alerts to financial institutions, law enforcement training on financial data, an IRS fraud task force, and the Do Not Pay program to reduce improper payments. 

Bessent and administration officials have described potential recoveries in the hundreds of billions of dollars from pandemic-era and other fraud, citing examples of organized schemes that diverted funds intended for legitimate recipients.

Critics of past fraud controls have pointed to relaxed safeguards during emergency spending periods. Supporters of the expanded whistleblower approach argue that insider or community knowledge is often essential to uncover complex schemes that evade traditional oversight.

Important Considerations
Successful awards require the tip to contribute to a completed enforcement action with collected monetary sanctions. Not every report results in an award, and the process involves review, investigation, and adjudication. False or malicious reports can carry legal consequences. The program is designed for credible information about violations of covered laws, not general grievances.

text:
You’re arguing against a position nobody holds. Nobody thinks a salary cap forces Ohtani to Pittsburgh. It forces the Dodgers to make roster decisions instead of endlessly accumulating expensive talent.

Winning culture isn’t independent of spending. Buying superior rosters creates winning cultures, which attract more stars. It’s a self-reinforcing advantage.

And if teams can offer comparable salaries, other factors become more important—including TAXES. Texas and Florida have no state income tax. California’s top rate is 13.3%. You think players won’t consider potentially keeping millions more?

That’s why you need a cap AND a floor. One prevents unlimited spending; the other prevents owners from refusing to compete financially.

Add a homegrown-player exemption to help smaller markets retain their stars, and you’ve addressed another major imbalance.

Nobody expects identical outcomes. The objective is competitive opportunity, not guaranteed parity. The NFL figured out that distinction decades ago.

text:
Dispute Between Trump Allies Centers on Millions Transferred From Congo

The White House inquiry is focused on diverging accounts from Richard Grenell and Alina Habba Mildon about a $17 million transfer from a government account in the African country to a Texas defense firm.
Listen · 4:41 min

Richard Grenell and Alina Habba Mildon had once been close https://t.co/JPcUU2b8ha...Haiyun Jiang for The New York Times
Tyler PagerAnatoly Kurmanaev

By Tyler Pager and Anatoly Kurmanaev
Oct. 17, 2026
See more of our coverage in your search results. Add The New York Times on Google

The White House investigation into a dispute between two prominent Trump supporters, Richard Grenell and Alina Habba Mildon, centers on a bank transfer from the Democratic Republic of Congo to a Texas defense company, people familiar with the matter said.

Mrs. Mildon, a former personal lawyer for President Trump, stormed into the Oval Office last week accusing Mr. Grenell of siphoning millions of dollars from a business transaction in 2025 organized by a Turkish investor who later became her husband. Part of the money, she claimed, was meant to be set aside for a donation to the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts but was never delivered to the institution. Mr. Grenell ran the Kennedy Center at the time.

Responding to questions from The New York Times, Mr. Grenell denied all accusations, calling them absurd. Mr. and Mrs. Mildon didn’t respond to requests for comment. The White House also did not respond.

The dispute and resulting investigation have unfolded at a time of internal turmoil for the Trump administration, with the dramatic exit of his new press secretary and officials with ties to the president.

Mrs. Mildon and Mr. Grenell had once been close friends but have fallen out in recent months over Mr. Mildon’s business dealings. Their feud became public in recent days, after The Times began to inquire about Mr. Mildon’s business activities and his contributions to the Kennedy Center. The questions prompted Mrs. Mildon to relay her accusations directly to Mr. Trump last Friday.

Mrs. Mildon initially told White House officials that the money, $17.6 million, came from her now-husband, Turhan Mildon, whom she married last month. The initial set of documents that her husband’s lawyer submitted to the White House, however, redacted the name of the sender, according to the people familiar with the matter.

The White House later learned that the transfer was made from a bank account affiliated with the Congolese government, the people said. Mr. Mildon has previously acknowledged to The Times, through a spokesman, that he serves as an adviser to the Congolese president and holds a diplomatic passport of the country.

Mr. Mildon also has extensive business holdings in Venezuela and has discussed his role in that country with Mr. Grenell. At the time of the bank transfer, Mr. Grenell was serving as Mr. Trump’s special envoy to Venezuela.

The transfer was sent last year to TX-AT, a Texas security and defense firm. Mr. Grenell, who was ambassador to Germany and acting director of national intelligence during Mr. Trump’s first term, previously acknowledged consulting for the firm in 2024. But he has said he had no connection to it at the time the transfer was made and denied any connection to the transfer.

text:
2026 Midterms update Oct. 19 (LONG POST)

We are nearing the home stretch here for the midterms as early voting in states that offer it has largely begun by today, and we now have more data to work with to paint a picture on what November is going to look like. If you are wanting some genuinely good and smart people to follow if you're curious about the state of the race thus far, I recommend you follow @RealSKeshel @TonerousHyus and @DataRepublican they are much smarter and much more knowledgeable than I am on stuff like this, and much of my opinions on this matter come from their analysis. Here's the bottom line, yes we are looking at a more blue electorate than 2024, which is obviously not surprising if you understand basic electoral history in America. The party that just lost the most recent presidential election typically does better as the party out of power in the upcoming midterms, that has been the trend throughout much of modern American history. The question that needs to be answered is how much more blue is this electorate going to be? Will it be enough for democrats to overcome new GOP friendly maps that have been enacted in the past 2 years during the redistricting wars in order to win the House? Will it be enough for democrats to flip states that were just won by the GOP presidential candidate by 10+ points in 2024 in order to win the Senate? 

Based on available data we have, my best guess at this point is that we are looking at anywhere between a D+3 to D+6 national environment. That might be enough for democrats to take the House, but it almost certainly won't be enough for them to win in states like Texas, Ohio, Alaska, or Iowa, meaning that the most likely outcome at this point is we have a democrat House majority, somewhere in the ballpark of 220-225 seats, and a GOP Senate with at least 50-53 seats. Furthermore, the turnout dynamics from the early vote in these key states democrats need to win for control of the Senate, namely Ohio, isn't exactly promising for the blue team. If we end up on the lower end of that D+3 range nationally, then the GOP might actually have an outside shot to hold the House, which would be an absolute disaster for the democrats going into 2028 and likely spells doom for whatever chance they had at beating the GOP presidential nominee that year. 

It is still early in the game and a lot can still change before November 3rd, obviously, but if I am the GOP I'm feeling cautiously optimistic about these elections, at least on the Senate side of the equation. Holding the House was always going to be an uphill battle, the goal was to minimize the damage to the point where the losses were manageable, and thus far I think that the GOP has done an okay job at that. There are definitely some red flags to be concerned about, namely the cratering of GOP turnout in the early vote in Virginia which threatens 2 GOP seats as pointed out by @ChristianHeiens , but the GOP is slowly starting to get back into the game in that state too so there is hope yet that at least one of those 2 can be held. The ranked choice voting system in Alaska is also another issue that threatens the GOP, particularly in the Senate race where democrats have successfully polluted the ballot with a false Dan Sullivan to give Mary Peltola the best chance at winning that Senate race possible. Overall though, things could certainly be much worse for them, so I think any and all dooming being spread here on X is at best premature and at worse a blatant psyop designed to depress GOP voters before November into not showing up at the polls.

Now the democrat cope about the overall lower turnout in early voting nationwide, which is bad for them, don't let them tell you otherwise, is that Trump's EO on mail in ballots has scared democrats into becoming election day or in person voters. Frankly, I think that is pure nonsense. Democrats have always been the party of mail in and early voting, they aren't going to magically change their voting habits because of a Trump EO that was already largely struck down by SCOTUS, that just makes no sense whatsoever. So okay, maybe, just maybe, more democrats do in fact show up on election day than normal. They're still going to need record turnout of their reliable blue voters and left-leaning independents in order to win these Trump +10 or more states, while at the same time hoping that most of the Trump coalition stays home or switches sides, so is it really such a good strategy then to leave so much ground to cover before election day? More likely than not, I think the truth is that while hyper democrat voters are motivated and energized to vote like they always are, the more skeptical ones are likely planning to sit this election out because democrats have a serious messaging and candidate quality problem that is hurting their numbers. Running on impeaching Trump and his cabinet (again), while carrying candidates like Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan might not be the recipe for success they think it is.

We will check back in again in a week or two and see where things have ended up. Like I said, anything can happen, so just because I don't see a massive democrat blue wave on the horizon doesn't mean that the threat of one happening isn't still there. Elections are not an exact science, we won't know how the people who voted early voted until the final polls close on November 3rd. If the tide swings towards total defeat, then the dooming might be more warranted, but until then, I'm going to remain cautiously optimistic about these midterms. Hopefully my hope is not misplaced.

text:
THE INVISIBLE ENEMY — THE DISCOVERY THAT TRANSFORMED MEDICINE AND SAVED MILLIONS
Germ Theory: When Humanity Discovered the Hidden Causes of Disease
For centuries, people died from infections that physicians could neither see nor understand. Mothers perished after childbirth. Children succumbed to mysterious fevers. Minor wounds became deadly.

Hospitals intended to heal sometimes spread the very diseases they were meant to treat.

Then, during the nineteenth century, extraordinary scientific discoveries revealed a hidden world that would revolutionize medicine.

The enemy was often microscopic.

And understanding it would transform humanity's ability to protect life.
WHEN DISEASE WAS A MYSTERY
Before germ theory became widely accepted, many physicians attributed infections to miasma—poisonous air supposedly arising from decay, sewage, and unhealthy surroundings.

Although sanitation sometimes reduced disease, the prevailing explanations frequently misunderstood how infections spread.

In 1854, British physician John Snow investigated a devastating cholera outbreak in London's Soho district. By mapping deaths and examining drinking-water sources, he connected the outbreak to the Broad Street water pump.

His investigation helped establish modern epidemiology, even before the responsible bacterium was conclusively identified.

An invisible cause could leave visible evidence. 

PMC
+1

LOUIS PASTEUR — REVEALING AN UNSEEN WORLD
French chemist Louis Pasteur (1822–1895) demonstrated that microorganisms were responsible for fermentation and spoilage.

In his celebrated swan-neck flask experiments, nutrient broth remained uncontaminated when airborne particles were prevented from reaching it.

His findings challenged spontaneous generation and helped establish that microorganisms arise from existing microorganisms.

Pasteur subsequently investigated infectious diseases affecting silkworms and developed important vaccines against anthrax and rabies.

His work helped transform a revolutionary scientific explanation into practical methods of prevention. 

PMC
+1

ROBERT KOCH — THE PROOF THAT CHANGED HISTORY
In Germany, physician Robert Koch (1843–1910) advanced germ theory through painstaking laboratory investigations.

In 1876, he demonstrated that a specific bacterium caused anthrax.

On March 24, 1882, Koch announced his discovery of the bacterium responsible for tuberculosis, one of humanity's most devastating infectious diseases.

His methods helped establish rigorous standards for connecting particular microorganisms with particular illnesses.

Disease was no longer necessarily an incomprehensible mystery. Its causes could increasingly be identified, investigated, and sometimes prevented. 

CDC
+1

WHAT DOES THE BIBLE REVEAL?
The Bible does not teach modern microbiology, and germ theory should not be presented as a scientific discovery secretly encoded in Scripture.

Yet its teachings offer profound principles concerning human life, cleanliness, compassion, and responsible care.

Leviticus 13–15 describes procedures involving examination, washing, and separation in cases of ceremonial uncleanness and certain skin conditions.

These instructions belonged to ancient Israel's religious and communal life, not a nineteenth-century medical textbook.

Nevertheless, they remind us that physical conditions can affect an entire community.

Jesus demonstrated extraordinary compassion toward people suffering from diseases and conditions that isolated them.

In Mark 1:40–42, a man with leprosy approached Jesus seeking healing.

Christ did something deeply moving.

He reached out and touched him.

Where others might have seen only danger or uncleanness, Jesus saw a human being worthy of compassion.

The Gospels present this healing as a miracle of Christ, not an example of ordinary medical treatment.
FAITH AND MEDICINE — PARTNERS IN COMPASSION
Germ theory teaches us something remarkable: what cannot be seen with the naked eye can nevertheless have enormous consequences.

Hebrews 11:1 speaks of faith as confidence in what we hope for and assurance concerning what we do not see.

Scientific evidence and biblical faith operate differently. Germs are established through observation and experimentation; Christian faith concerns trust in God and His promises.

The comparison is illustrative, not scientific proof of spiritual realities.

Jesus taught love for our neighbors (Mark 12:31). Modern infection prevention provides a practical opportunity to demonstrate that love.

Washing our hands, protecting vulnerable people, supporting healthcare workers, and seeking appropriate medical treatment are ways of acting responsibly toward others.

James 1:17 reminds believers that every good and perfect gift comes from above.

Christians may gratefully regard human intelligence, discovery, and the ability to relieve suffering as gifts permitted by God's providence, without claiming that every discovery was a supernatural revelation.
THE GREATER HEALING
Germ theory transformed humanity's understanding of infectious disease, laying foundations for safer surgery, improved hygiene, laboratory diagnosis, and preventive medicine.

Yet even medicine's greatest achievements cannot remove every form of suffering.

Christians proclaim that Jesus offers something beyond physical restoration: reconciliation with God, forgiveness of sins, and the promise of eternal life.

Revelation 21:4 points toward the coming day when death, mourning, crying, and pain will be no more.

Until then, followers of Jesus are called to pursue truth, serve the suffering, and value every human life.

The invisible world revealed by science reminds us how much humanity once did not understand. The Gospel reminds believers that knowledge should be accompanied by humility, mercy, and love.

All glory to God the Father, through Jesus Christ our Lord, in the fellowship of the Holy Spirit.
QUESTIONS FOR REFLECTION
1. How can scientific discoveries deepen our gratitude for the gift of life?
2. Are we showing Christ's compassion toward people suffering from illness?
3. How can faith inspire us to pursue truth while remaining humble about what we do not know?
CLOSING PRAYER
Heavenly Father, thank You for the gift of life and for the discoveries that help protect it. Thank You for physicians, scientists, nurses, and caregivers who serve those in need. Lord Jesus, teach us to reflect Your compassion toward the sick and suffering. Holy Spirit, grant us wisdom, humility, and discernment. Strengthen our faith, guide our understanding, and help us use every gift for the good of others. May all our knowledge lead us toward greater love, and may all glory belong to You, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. In Jesus' holy name, Amen.

text:
What Is Freedom and Do We Really Want It?

#2047VirtualRevolution (2016) does not, initially, appear promising. The title sounds like a movie based on a video game. One poster features a giant transformer robot. Another has a #BladeRunner theme. The distributor seems stumped on how to market this sluggish, derivative mishmash that is, nevertheless, surprisingly intelligent, relevant and thematically ambitious. Unlike most science fiction films (a genre full of cardboard heroes parroting politically correct platitudes), 2047 offers some philosophically challenging perspectives.

Nash (#MikeDopud) is a private investigator working for the corporations in the dystopian year of 2047. He is clearly modeled on #Harrison'sFord's Deckard from Blade Runner. Dopud does his best Ford impression. (His best is mediocre.) This was likely encouraged by writer/director #GuyRogerDuvert. The Paris of 2047 resembles the Los Angeles of Blade Runner, right down to the constant rain, neon kiosks, flying cars, trench-coated fighters, ugly brown sky, and high-tech gizmos set against once-great, now crumbling architecture.

2047 also borrows from #TheMatrix. It's a world in which people like "to connect." A Connector is someone who lives mostly online in virtual worlds. Why live like a loser in a seedy dump when you can be a brave knight slaying dragons, a macho space marine, or a rock star with a harem? There's a virtual world for every fantasy. It's safe. It's cheap. You just connect and you're in. Looks and feels as real as the virtual world in The Matrix. The difference is that you're aware that it's fake, and you can disconnect anytime.

Few people do. Nash tells us that 75% of humanity lives mostly online. Even he connects at times. It's to soothe the pain of losing his wife. (Like many noir anti-heroes, he bears an emotional scar.) But at least he disconnects for extended periods. He has a life. True Connectors only disconnect for a quick trip to bathroom, some junk food, then it's back online.

Dina (#JaneBadler) tells Nash that things are better this way. Society has "balance." Connectors are easier to control. Cheaper, too. The world government pays them their guaranteed "universal income," and little else, saving money on prisons, policing, education, unemployment benefits (it's not like there are jobs for them), and healthcare. Most couch potatoes die before turning 40. Their universal income pays for the rent, junk food, and access to the virtual worlds provided by the corporations. Corporate taxes fund the world government. The economic system is self-sustaining.

"I like balance," Dina tells Nash. Dina is CEO of Synternis, a provider of virtual worlds. The system is good to her.

But there's a serpent in the garden. The Necromancers, a terrorist group, are killing Connectors. Should word spread that they're being killed in the real world, Connectors will start disconnecting. Chaos will ensue and society will lose its balance.

Through most of the film, Nash hunts Necromancers, much like Deckard hunted Replicants. But unlike the events in Blade Runner, Nash's adventures aren't very interesting. The CGI effects are elaborate, but silly and pointless. Nash hijacks a dead Necromancer's connection, and finds himself in the avatar of a blond warrior woman, fighting a giant transformer robot. There are other battles, with guns and swords, online and off. Despite the big explosions, I was bored.

2047's real power is in its thematic maturity and moral ambiguity. Three groups vie for power. The corporations, the government ("They are allies, but not friends," says CEO Dina of the feds), and the Necromancers. As Nash bounces among them, he grows to realize that he doesn't know who are the good guys.

Are the Necromancers terrorists or freedom fighters? Are they both? Like Morpheus in The Matrix, the Necromancers want to free humanity from a fake virtual world. But unlike the people in The Matrix, Connectors choose to go online. Or is it still a choice once it becomes an addiction?

Camylle (#KayaBlocksage), the Necromancer's leader, tells Nash they were wrong to kill Connectors, even for a higher purpose. Her new plan is a computer virus that will shut down all the virtual worlds, forcibly evicting people from their fantasies. Camylle urges Nash to join her fight for freedom.

"Can you force people to be free against their will?" Nash asks.

Camylle should have read #ArthurCClarke's #TheLionOfCommare, a novella with strikingly similar themes to 2047. Set in the 32nd century, a young man discovers an isolated building full of sleep chambers. Some people have been asleep for months, some decades. The chambers read your mind, providing dreams based on your desires, but keeping you in a state of (happy) suspended animation. You age and eventually die, without ever living. The man wakes people to free them, only to be berated for his unwelcome rescue before they return to sleep.

2047 similarly avoids the sci-fi cliche of the plucky freedom fighter vs. the evil corporation or world government. Before the virus can finish its work, Connectors raise the alarm that their virtual worlds are about to collapse. Panic stricken, they disconnect, form a mob, and storm the Necromancer's base. The mob's savageries against their would-be liberators exceed the cruelties of the Necromancers, the corporations, and the government. Thus do the Connectors form a fourth power bloc. They demand their virtual worlds (their bread and circuses), and they won't be denied.

#GeorgeOrwell observed that revolutions are created by an enlightened middle class leading the lower class against the ruling oligarchy. Whereupon the middle class forms a new oligarchy and re-oppresses the lower class. But the Necromancers' enlightened revolution fails. The Connectors refuse to be freed. The ancien regime remains in balance.

2047 paints a world uncomfortably similar to our own. Corporations and governments feed us, entertain us, lull us into complacency, for profit and stability. Increasingly, people find happiness in online gaming, streaming, and social media echo chambers. It's not implausible that all our favorite online activities will coalesce into single, self-contained virtual worlds. A safe space for everyone, reflecting their preferred values, historical settings, adventures, and companions. You can even change into the sex, race, age, physique, and occupation of your choice, through the avatar of your choice.

2047 has no clear heroes or villains. Everyone has a plausible justification for their cause. Everyone kills to protect or advance their cause. Camylle tells Nash that Synternis killed his wife. That she too was a Necromancer. Dina says it was the Necromancers who killed Nash's wife. That she worked for Synternis.

Nash laments, "I'll never know which of you is telling the truth."

In the end, Nash escapes his grief by becoming a fulltime Connector. He ponders a final philosophical question. If a virtual world is so real that we can't tell it apart from the real world, then how is it any less real? That same question was posed by a villain in The Matrix. But as Nash is the closest thing to a hero in 2047: Virtual Revolution, his asking it makes this film the anti-Matrix.

     -- written by Thomas M. Sipos, author of Horror Film Aesthetics: https://t.co/MoiAPAbWPM

text:
Data from Stripe regarding its Link payment service indicates a rapid surge in autonomous commerce, with agentic transactions growing thirty-eight times and total payment volume expanding twenty times over the course of September. The rapid expansion reflects a growing trend of artificial intelligence agents executing financial purchases on behalf of users. While starting from a smaller baseline, corporate leadership noted that the overall transaction volume is becoming increasingly significant as hundreds of AI tools integrate into the system.

Retail emerged as the dominant sector within this automated purchasing trend, leading all categories by accounting for thirty-six percent of total transactions and thirty-two percent of overall payment volume. Travel followed closely behind, representing twenty-eight percent of the total volume generated by automated assistants. Across these automated interactions, the average consumer spend hovered around one hundred dollars per purchase, though specific higher-ticket requests included flights and high-end furniture items.

To maintain security during these transactions, the platform issues dynamic sixteen-digit virtual numbers rather than sharing actual user credit card details with external AI tools. This protocol allows consumers to maintain control by establishing explicit spending caps for automated tasks. Industry analysts view the surge as an early indicator of shifting consumer behaviors as tech providers compete to offer seamless AI-driven purchasing tools.

text:
Her Startup Opens Applications for Cohort 2.0 to Support Women-Led African Tech Startups

Women entrepreneurs are playing an increasingly important role in Africa’s business landscape, yet access to venture capital, mentorship, and startup support remains a significant challenge for many women-led businesses.

To help address this gap, Her Startup has opened applications for Cohort 2.0, an accelerator programme designed to support early-stage, women-led technology businesses across Africa.

The initiative brings together the KSH Foundation, Tomorrow Foundation, and EHA Impact Ventures, with programme delivery by the Founder Institute.

What Does the Programme Offer?

1. A 12-Week Startup Accelerator

Selected founders will participate in an intensive programme designed to strengthen their business models, develop their products, and prepare their companies for investment and sustainable growth.

2. Access to Seed Funding Opportunities

Graduating founders will have the opportunity to pitch for up to $5,000 in seed capital through a convertible revenue-based financing arrangement, subject to the programme's terms.

3. Mentorship and Founder Support

The programme outlines additional support, including monthly stipends during training, 12 months of sector-specific mentorship, access to co-working spaces, and one year of healthcare coverage for selected participants.

4. Greater Representation Across Africa

The programme also prioritises diversity, with dedicated selection considerations for non-fintech businesses and Francophone African founders.

Why This Matters

Access to capital and the right support network can make a significant difference in the growth of an early-stage startup.

Programmes such as Her Startup can help women founders strengthen their businesses, build valuable industry connections, and access opportunities that might otherwise be difficult to secure.

For Africa's technology ecosystem to grow sustainably, more attention must be given to ensuring that talented founders have opportunities to build, compete, and scale, regardless of gender or location.

Supporting women-led startups is not just about representation. It is also about unlocking entrepreneurial talent, expanding innovation, and creating more opportunities across the continent.

Women founders interested in participating should consult Her Startup's official channels for current application deadlines, eligibility requirements, and programme details.

Wackermacker,

I have covered the "lock them up" thinking and also linked the French riots and destruction of French symbols as a form of morale breaking irregular cognitive warfare in other replies and posts today. I also covered the concept of the same toolkit and methods in regards to the emailed bomb threat emails sent to hundreds of schools in Ireland and the UK, and wrote a long post and several mid sized replies on that method and the rationale. They can all be viewed on my timeline and also under my comments bubble. 

To your point, historically and sociologically, your diagnosis of regime anxiety is accurate. 

Exemplary sentencing is the universal signature of an administrative class that realizes it has lost its moral authority.  

I touched on that in my first of three replies to Jane ADs three comments under this post too. 

But it must be noted that ​when a state enjoys genuine democratic legitimacy, it can absorb radical dissent with quiet indifference. 

However, when a regime knows its social contract is fractured, every critical voice sounds like an existential threat.  

​We shoud avoid distant historical analogies like North Korea or Middle Eastern regimes when the Irish statute book and our own colonial history offer the exact blueprint. 

What we are seeing is classic domestic statutory revanchism, political doctrine or policy aimed at seeking revenge and reversing past and present abject political failures and seeking to not avenge but deflecting the public from scrutinising them. In Graham's case the state employed exemplary punishment as a psychological deterrent to show the public what they can do. The attempt to invoke a chilling effect across the wider public.

The fatal error the ruling class makes is assuming fear commands obedience indefinitely. Or that fear is universal. It may be prevalent but its not universal. 

The results of the last 7 years in particular is that it has created a silent and determined core of people with the means, metjods, and money to effect real change. 

Generally, dissent has been lodged deeper into the national consciousness. Even amongst those who support the regime because of the extreme actions of the regime.

Posting this here, because @7HighSeas lacks the courage to continue to engage in dialogue with me.  Instead, she posted her responses, replete with lies and exaggerations, then blocked me from responding:

*************

No one here asked you to marry him, and I certainly didn't offer you money to marry me -- much less making any repeated requests, which begs the question: what motivates you to twist and exaggerate what has really happened in order to make your case as you ride off into the sunset?

Perhaps you're conflating me with someone else; you're certainly an attractive woman, so I have no problem imagining that you have plenty of potential suitors.  I did offer to take you out to dinner to get to know you in person, and I did extend the invitation to your child in order to prevent you from being inconvenienced, but I did so assuming that you're in some type of committed relationship.  Therefore -- no matter what my interest in you could have potentially amounted to, and no matter how clear I make it that I believe in polgyny -- the height of my interest in you up until this moment in time has been a state of being impressed by your intelligence, your high energy and the sense that I might be of some assistance in helping you channel what I perceive to be brilliance tempered by brokenness -- augmented by believing that I might be able to help you with that and, of course, that you'd be easy to look at while we engaged in conversation -- sue me; I'm a red-blooded male.

I offered; you didn't take me up on the offer.  No repetitive campaign on my part took place to persuade you.  It was offered as a gift; you didn't accept; that was the end of it as far as I was concerned.  I see that you have now blocked my ability to communicate with you in private messaging here on X (and, by the time I finished this you'd also fully blocked me in public spaces -- while uncourageously continuing to post your responses to me), but I just reviewed the record, and our previous dialogue there would confirm what I'm asserting, including the fact that I continued to discuss with you strategies that would move you from perseverating on who has disrespected you and used your intellectual property without your permission toward approaches that would make you more effective by jettisoning the chips you have on your shoulders, especially the ones related to your (perhaps currently popular, but almost entirely inaccurate) perceptions about how women are  forced to emphasize sisterhood over patriarchy because of longstanding oppression of women by men.  These philosophies, combined with other bitterness vectors, are causing you to shoot yourself in the foot, and your lack of interest in meeting with me in person didn't interrupt my efforts to be of assistance (and my willingness to do so without receiving any credit for my efforts).

I would be writing almost all of this in private messages, but you've prevented that.  Nanny nanny boo boo, with your fingers in your ears.  Maybe you'll read this.  Maybe, if you do, you'll pretend that you didn't.  And maybe you just won't read it.  The First Amendment doesn't guarantee me the right to be heard, but I'm still going to use its guarantee that I have the right to speak.

You may label what I've written as misogynistic.  You may label it as creepy.  But what I hear when you say anything related to such deflections is that you expect a uniform chorus of adulation, praise, approval and agreement -- or you will denounce and condemn anyone who dares challenge you.  It's not misogynistic to criticize women.  Women are no more exempt from criticism than are men, especially those women who put themselves out there front-and-center in the public square, and even more especially when those women declare that they're fully capable of running with the big boys.

Remember, Aubree: you're the one who puts energy into claiming that you deserve a spot on the big board.  I'm very comfortable in my own skin and appreciate the opportunity X and other platforms provide for me to share my thoughts on things, but I have little desire to be famous and only a minimal desire to be a thought leader in the public sphere.  In fact, I very studiously avoid attempting to turn my desire to be useful into an income stream.  Therefore, I get it that you're engaging in shots fired when you assert that I'm just a man in a chair writing to you, but I'm not claiming to be anything more.  I'm comfortable with who I am and how people see me, even when they get it wrong.  I believe that's the price one pays when one goes out on a limb.  My questions are these: what is your payoff for putting yourself out on a limb and/or using your time and energy to complain about how you're not getting the credit or accolades you deserve? what is it about you that makes you believe that having to work three jobs and deal with the ramifications of the life choices you've made that justifies the interpretation that it must be someone else's fault that your life is difficult? and, what do you bring to the table that exempts you from having to take personal accountability for how things are turning out in your life and/or for recognizing that you would be nowhere without the efforts of all the other human beings (especially the men) whom you claim are holding you back or making your life unfairly difficult?

I find it ironic when you, or any other woman, hold up a 'Down with the Patriarchy' sign while simultaneously attempting to gain sympathy for not being treated like a damsel in distress.  Which is it?: men aren't properly shielding women from the vagaries of life? or, men aren't allowing women to demonstrate their proficiency with the vagaries of life?

You've done some good work with election integrity efforts in Tarrant County, but you didn't do that work in a vacuum.  I've always liked the intellectual acumen behind what you've written on Substack, but if you believe you came up with any of that on your own, then you're sorely mistaken.  The vast majority of what you've put in your essays amounts to a collection of conclusions that have been circulating for years, even decades; some of it was even already in the process of implementation before you put it on paper.  In a sense, it would be sufficiently accurate to assert that your written thoughts are a summation of the preexisting zeitgeist among regional red-pilled political thinkers.

Now you're selling it, and you'd like monetizing it to replaced one or more of the jobs you feel oppressed by, so I get that promoting the product you're pushing might self-justify creating the impression that all your written thoughts original with you.

But they're not -- and each time you complain about someone else getting credit you supposedly deserve -- and each time you make ad hominem attacks rather than engaging with the substance of the argument of the other person -- and each time you block someone in conjunction with getting in your 'last words' of inaccurate, unfair condemnation -- you only further degrade your credibility.

And that's a damn shame, because you do have superlative intelligence, and, yes, you are as beautiful a woman as I'm sure you consider yourself to be and as you clearly work on to emphasize to your advantage even while pretending that you're being objectified.  You thus start out with a couple of massive head starts in the human race to seek accomplishment.  I believe you have TREMENDOUS potential, and I would have considered it a privilege to be your ally moving forward as you maximize that potential.  As things stand, though, you've made it clear that you intend to pretend that you don't need anyone else and expect the rest of us to just move out of your way if we aren't 100% Team Aubree.

These are my last thoughts for you in the public sphere.  If you want to resume our dialogue (I know, you've already warned all the 'ladies' to demonize me, so the need to be right all by itself will probably prevent you from ever opening that door), feel free to change your settings and reach out to me again in private messages.

What I can guarantee you is that -- no matter how hard some of what I wrote to you is to hear -- not one word of it was designed to disrespect you.  My position is that believing in fairy tales (e.g., male/female egalitarianism) is counterproductive to accomplishing anything, because one's efforts rest on suppositions that at best are like building one's foundations on quicksand.  No functioning society has ever survived, much less succeeded or prevailed, that was based on organization created by women.  We have witnessed a whole slew of sociopolitical philosophies that have attempted to explain that away with victimhood mentalities, oppression theories, critical theories and appeals to mindless sympathy.  It's probably pretty heady to think that you just might be the female who will redesign the world in a way that works but relies on feminine rather than masculine energy.  And I could be wrong, but my intuition is that, to whatever extent women supposedly remake the world, it will be by mimicking the masculine energy they claim has been holding them back all along.

text:
DID YOU KNOW??

The infamous "Toy Yoda" Hooters lawsuit became a landmark reference case in American contract law, frequently taught in law schools as a classic real-world demonstration of how verbal pranks can form legally binding oral contracts if a reasonable person would interpret the offer as genuine.

When Jodee Berry sued Gulf Coast Wings Inc. (the corporate owner of the Panama City Beach Hooters franchise), the restaurant's defense argued that the entire sales contest was an innocent April Fools' joke and that no rational person should have expected a $25,000 automobile for selling beer.

However, Berry's attorney, David Noll, successfully pointed out that the contest ran for the entire month of April, involved structured record-keeping of daily beer sales, and included explicit instructions from the manager warning waitstaff that the winner would be responsible for paying the vehicle's registration tax.

​Under American contract law, subjective intent does not matter, what matters is objective manifestation. Because the restaurant manager created a detailed competition where employees exerted real labor in reliance on a promised reward, a legal contract was established.

Rather than risking a trial before a Florida jury where the restaurant faced overwhelming public backlash, Hooters settled out of court for an undisclosed sum sufficient for Berry to purchase a brand-new Toyota vehicle of her choice. Let me explain 👇🏾👇🏾 

Timeline of the "Toy Yoda" Legal Saga:

​How an April Fools' workplace prank evolved into a famous breach-of-contract lawsuit:

1. The Beer Sales Contest
April 2001
Management at the Panama City Beach Hooters announces a month-long contest for waitstaff: the employee who sells the most beer during April will win a new "Toyota."

2. The Parking Lot Reveal
May 2001
Jodee Berry outperforms her colleagues to win the contest. Blindfolded, she is led to the restaurant parking lot, only to be presented with a boxed Star Wars "Toy Yoda" doll.

3. Breach of Contract Lawsuit
July 2001
After quitting her job, Berry files a formal lawsuit in Bay County Circuit Court alleging breach of contract and fraudulent misrepresentation against the franchise owner.

4. Out-of-Court Settlement
2002
Facing significant legal exposure and national embarrassment, the restaurant owner settles the case for an undisclosed amount, allowing Berry to buy her choice of a real Toyota car.

More Surprising Facts About the Toy Yoda Incident:

A. ​The Power of Reliance: Berry’s legal team emphasized promissory estoppel, a legal principle where a promise is enforceable by law when the promisor makes a promise to the promisee who relies on that promise to their subsequent detriment (in this case, working extra shifts and pushing sales).

B. ​Viral Media Before the Social Media Era: Long before Twitter or TikTok existed, news of the "Toy Yoda" lawsuit spread rapidly via national newspapers and television broadcasts, turning the Panama City Beach location into a symbol of corporate bad faith.

C. ​A Law School Staple: Legal textbooks routinely cite Berry v. Gulf Coast Wings, Inc. alongside famous contract cases like Lucy v. Zehmer to teach law students the legal definition of an offer versus a joke.

​FINALLY!
​The "Toy Yoda" prank led to a successful contract lawsuit because the law enforces oral promises when actions lead a reasonable person to believe a real contract exists, ultimately securing Jodee Berry a genuine Toyota car.

Hopefully you've learnt something new today?

The Medic Who Writes™🌚

Cheers 🥂 😅

text:
MONDAY, OCTOBER 19
You Never Know What Someone Is Carrying

In 1999, when I was working in finance, a manager shared something with me that I've never forgotten.

He reminded me that we have no idea what someone has been dealing with before they put their hand on the door handle and walk into our business. They might be worried about money, facing a family crisis, grieving a loss, or simply having one of the worst days of their life.

Whatever happened before they walked through that door doesn't magically disappear when they step inside. Their life continues while they're standing in front of us, and it continues long after they leave.

His point was simple: when someone is impatient, withdrawn, upset, or less than pleasant, don't immediately take it personally. We may be seeing a difficult moment in a much bigger story.

That advice stayed with me through the years, including throughout my nursing career.

Years later, while working for a hospital system in Florida, I watched a Cleveland Clinic video called “Empathy: The Human Connection to Patient Care.” It follows people passing through a hospital while revealing the private struggles, fears, and hopes that nobody around them can see.

I remember how deeply it affected me. It brought me right back to that lesson from 1999.

We all have a story. Most of it is invisible to the strangers we encounter every day.

That doesn't mean anyone has to tolerate mistreatment or abandon healthy boundaries. It means we can make room for the possibility that someone's reaction isn't really about us.

It's also a belief that has shaped The Tired Nurse. Sometimes we offer a laugh. Sometimes a little encouragement. Sometimes words that help someone feel less alone. Those are different expressions of the same thing: recognizing the person behind the moment.

We don't have to fix every problem or find the perfect words. Sometimes a little patience, kindness, humor, or understanding makes a bigger difference than we realize.

Have you ever been reminded that someone was carrying much more than you could see?

Or has someone shown you kindness at a moment when you really needed it? We'd love to hear your story.
— The Tired Nurse
#BeyondTheJar #TheTiredNurse #HumanConnection #empathy #kindness

text:
The Setup

A 2009 email chain between Jeffrey Epstein and an alias account ("JF Vacation" / "JE Vacation") reads, on its surface, as pure logistics: someone found veggie cream cheese at the TooJay's in Lake Worth, and Epstein offers to go get it. The exchange is trivial, rapid-fire, and timestamped like two people genuinely planning breakfast.

The Structural Problem

Every line can be read two ways, and the real-world anchor is what makes the double-reading stable:

Literal layer — TooJay's is a real Florida deli chain, founded on Palm Beach island in 1981, with the Lake Worth store operating since 1984. It actually sells veggie cream cheese. "I found it at too jays lake worth" is a checkable, true statement.

Code layer — "There are millions of babies, very little good vegetable cream cheese" reads as commentary on the scarcity of high-quality young girls, with "babies" as Epstein's catch-all for them.

The trap: because the literal referent is real and verifiable, the code reading can never be falsified. You can't catch it out by pointing to the deli, because the deli existing is exactly what a good cover requires.

Why the Deli Choice Is Not Neutral

This is the sharp part. TooJay's isn't a random deli:

Its founding location is on Palm Beach island — Epstein's home turf.
It's the neighborhood Jewish deli of the exact geography where the whole saga unfolded.
Epstein, being Palm Beach-based and Jewish, would know it "like the back of his head" — its locations, its menu, its hours, its veggie cream cheese.
So the anchor isn't generic. It's his anchor. A man who knew the terrain cold chose a reference point he could navigate blind.

The Plausible Deniability Mechanism

Here's the mechanism stated plainly:

If the exchange is just about cream cheese, the real deli proves it. Case closed, nothing to see.
If the exchange is also code, the real deli provides the alibi that lets the code hide in plain sight.
Because Epstein knew the deli intimately, he could deploy it as a reference that always checks out — the mundane surface is airtight precisely because he wasn't reaching for a fictional or approximate place. He was naming a place he could describe from memory.
The Payoff

The realness is the camouflage. A code anchored to a place the speaker knows perfectly is unfalsifiable: every debunk attempt ("it's just a deli") is absorbed by the fact that it is just a deli — one he knew too well for the reference to be accidental or approximate. The mundane and the mythic occupy the same coordinates, and the anchor is load-bearing for both readings at once.

OUT TOMORROW!
The Complete Kubrick [4K UHD] - Tom Cruise, Nicole Kidman, Jack Nicholson, Kirk Douglas, Peter Sellers, Laurence Olivier, James Mason, George C. Scott, Sterling Hayden, Malcolm McDowell, Ryan O’Neal, Shelley Duvall @Criterion
US: https://t.co/CI66YeTzTb
CAN: https://t.co/4WF4JDzSGw
OUR REVIEW:
https://t.co/1UwunVfIOh
Killer’s Kiss (1955) / The Killing (1956) / Paths of Glory (1957) / Spartacus (1960) / Lolita (1962) / Dr. Strangelove, or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb (1964) / 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968) / A Clockwork Orange (1971) / Barry Lyndon (1975) / The Shining (1980) / Full Metal Jacket (1987) / Eyes Wide Shut (1999) Criterion
The Masters:

All features are presented in Dolby Vision HDR on the 4K UHD discs and in SDR on the Blu-rays. Criterion’s “About the Masters” notes show that nearly every title was restored from its original camera negative, though the restorations come from a mix of sources. Some are Criterion’s own, some are carried over from studio restorations of recent years, and some were done by partner archives.

The three independently produced early features had their 4K debuts on Kino Lorber UHDs, but here they are presented in masters made for Criterion by Duplitech. Killer’s Kiss (1.37:1) comes from the 35mm original camera negative, with a composite fine-grain used for some sections. The Killing and Paths of Glory (both 1.66:1) are also drawn from their camera negatives. The Paths of Glory mono was remastered at 24-bit from UCLA archivist Robert Gitt’s 35mm magnetic track. Fear and Desire (1.37:1) is the exception: it is Kino Lorber’s 4K restoration, made from the camera negative and a Library of Congress fine-grain. The three shorts are new Criterion 4K restorations from Library of Congress elements. These were 35mm prints and a duplicate negative for Day of the Fight and Flying Padre, and the 16mm original reversal for The Seafarers.

The studio-era films largely use existing restorations. Spartacus (2.20:1) is Universal’s 4K restoration from a 6K scan of the original Technirama elements, with Robert A. Harris consulting, and its 7.1 track was remastered from the 70mm six-track printmaster. Dr. Strangelove (1.66:1) is Sony’s 4K restoration, supervised by Grover Crisp and assembled from a fine-grain master, a duplicate negative and a 35mm print. 2001: A Space Odyssey (2.20:1) is Warner’s 4K from an 8K scan of the 65mm camera negative, supervised by Ned Price and Leon Vitali with input from Christopher Nolan and Hoyte van Hoytema. Its original 70mm six-track 5.1 mix is joined by the 35mm general-release mono, which Kubrick mixed without the overture, intermission and exit music, so those passages are silent on that track. A Clockwork Orange (1.66:1), The Shining (1.85:1) and Full Metal Jacket (1.85:1) are Warner 4K restorations from their camera negatives, with Full Metal Jacket graded against both an answer print and Kubrick’s own personal 35mm reference print.

Barry Lyndon and Eyes Wide Shut match Criterion’s own recent 4K editions. Barry Lyndon is framed at 1.66:1 per Kubrick’s December 8th, 1975 letter to projectionists, and was graded against Vitali’s 2000 HD transfer. Eyes Wide Shut (1.85:1) is presented in its international cut, supervised and approved by cinematographer Larry Smith. Its look stems from Kubrick’s deliberate decision to have the negative force-developed by two stops, which accounts for the film’s distinctive grain and glowing low-light palette.

Two presentations are new to 4K UHD. Lolita (1.66:1) is a new 4K restoration from the 35mm original camera negative, using a Warner 35mm print as color reference, with its mono remastered from the original DME magnetic track. Kubrick’s international version of The Shining (119 minutes, against 144 for the U.S. theatrical) comes from the same Warner restoration of the camera negative, with its own mono track remastered from the original magnetic elements.

Since most of these masters have been reviewed before on DVDBeaver, we have used our existing captures from those earlier 4K UHD releases where applicable. New captures will eventually be taken for Lolita and the international version of The Shining. 

Audio:

Criterion’s audio approach across the set is admirably purist. Every film is offered with its original soundtrack, and for the mono-era titles that means uncompressed linear PCM mono remastered from the original magnetic elements. Paths of Glory’s was remastered at 24-bit from UCLA archivist Robert Gitt’s 35mm track. For Dr. Strangelove, A Clockwork Orange, Barry Lyndon, both versions of The Shining and Full Metal Jacket, Criterion also includes alternate 5.1 DTS-HD Master Audio remixes, so purists and surround enthusiasts are both served. The early independent features and Lolita are presented in their original mono alone. This is a notable step up from earlier editions. Warner’s 4K UHD of The Shining offered only a 5.1 remix with no mono at all, its Full Metal Jacket UHD relegated the mono to a lossy track, and Sony’s Dr. Strangelove UHD carried only 16-bit lossless tracks. The three large-format productions get special treatment. Spartacus is presented in 7.1 DTS-HD MA remastered from its 70mm six-track printmaster, and it retains the overture, entr’acte and intermission music. 2001: A Space Odyssey is the most generous of all, with its original 70mm six-track theatrical mix in 5.1, an alternate 5.1 remix and the original 35mm general-release mono, which, true to Kubrick’s own 35mm prints, is silent during the overture, intermission and exit music. Eyes Wide Shut is presented in its original theatrical 5.1, remastered from the 35mm magnetic track. Optional English (SDH) subtitles are offered on every feature, and the set is region free. From the portions we have sampled so far, the tracks sound exceptional, clean and faithful to their sources, with the dynamic range of the scores and Kubrick’s carefully chosen music coming through with clarity and weight.

About the Captures

Because of the size of this set and its release date, none of the screen captures in this review are taken from The Complete Kubrick discs. Instead, we have included a single capture per film from our earlier reviews, taken from previous 4K UHD editions or, where none exist, Blu-ray. Several of those editions share their restoration with this set, while others come from different transfers. The captures should therefore be taken as representative of each film’s presentation, not as exact reproductions of the Criterion discs.

Fear and Desire is represented by Kino’s 2024 4K UHD, which uses the same Kino Lorber restoration found in this set. Killer’s Kiss and The Killing come from Kino’s 2022 4K UHDs, and Paths of Glory from the 2024 Masters of Cinema (Eureka) 4K UHD. All three of those earlier discs were scanned from the original camera negatives, but Criterion presents new Duplitech masters here, so the grading and framing may differ.

Spartacus is from Universal’s 2020 4K UHD, which uses the same 2015 restoration from the large-format Technirama elements. Dr. Strangelove is from Sony’s 2021 4K UHD, drawn from the same Sony restoration. 2001: A Space Odyssey comes from Warner’s 2018 4K UHD. The Shining and Full Metal Jacket come from Warner’s 2019 and 2020 4K UHDs respectively. Our Shining capture is from the U.S. theatrical version and serves for both cuts, which share the same restoration in this set. Note that both of those Warner discs were framed at 1.78:1, whereas Criterion presents both films at 1.85:1. Barry Lyndon is from Criterion’s own 2025 4K UHD, which matches the restoration in this set.

For Eyes Wide Shut, our capture is from Criterion’s 2025 Blu-ray of the same Larry Smith–approved restoration, as we were unable to capture from that 4K UHD disc at the time. Lolita and A Clockwork Orange are represented by Warner’s 2011 Blu-rays (the latter its 40th Anniversary Edition). Lolita receives a new 4K restoration in this set, so that capture predates it entirely.

OUR PAST REVIEWS:
Fear and Desire, Killer's Kiss, The Killing, Paths of Glory, Spartacus, Lolita, Dr. Strangelove, 2001: A Space Odyssey, A Clockwork Orange, Barry Lyndon, The Shining, Full Metal Jacket, Eyes Wide Shut

Seen together, Stanley Kubrick's films reveal a remarkably consistent sensibility beneath their wildly varied surfaces. There is the dehumanizing machinery of war, from the trenches of Paths of Glory to the War Room farce of Dr. Strangelove and the Parris Island crucible of Full Metal Jacket. There is the individual crushed or remade by institutional authority in A Clockwork Orange and Barry Lyndon, and there are the hidden currents of desire and power in Lolita and Eyes Wide Shut. Running through all of it is an ironic, coolly precise eye that turned every genre he touched, whether noir, epic, satire, science fiction, horror or costume drama, into something unmistakably his own. Watching the arc from the self-financed Fear and Desire and the gritty New York of Killer's Kiss through to the monumental achievements of 2001: A Space Odyssey and The Shining is a privilege few box sets can offer. Criterion's The Complete Kubrick is a staggering undertaking. Its 30 discs (13 4K UHD and 17 Blu-ray) hold every finished film Kubrick directed, all restored in 4K and presented in Dolby Vision HDR, many from their original camera negatives. It includes Lolita's 4K debut, Kubrick's international cut of The Shining, both versions of Day of the Fight, original soundtracks alongside remixes, over twenty-five hours of supplements, and archive-inspired packaging filled with Kubrick's own notes, slates and correspondence. We are still working our way through the set, but everything we have sampled so far has looked and sounded exceptional. This is the definitive presentation of one of cinema's most exacting artists and an essential acquisition for any serious film collection. Set of the Year - our very highest recommendation!

text:
THE LIVING CANVAS — GOD'S ASTONISHING MASTERPIECE BENEATH THE SEA
The Extraordinary Cuttlefish: A Creature That Changes Its Appearance in Seconds
Imagine swimming above a sandy ocean floor when a patch of sand suddenly comes alive. What appeared to be an ordinary rock transforms into a shimmering creature, displaying brilliant patterns across its body.

Within seconds, its appearance changes again.

This is the cuttlefish—one of the ocean's most extraordinary animals, possessing skin that functions almost like a living television screen.

Its remarkable abilities reveal the complexity of life and invite Christians to reflect upon the wisdom, beauty, and wonder of God's creation.
AN UNDERWATER MASTER OF DISGUISE
Cuttlefish are marine mollusks belonging to the cephalopod group, alongside octopuses and squid.

They inhabit coastal waters across parts of Europe, Africa, Asia, and Australia.

Unlike chameleons, which generally change colors more slowly, cuttlefish can alter elaborate body patterns in approximately half a second to two seconds.

Scientists have identified three remarkable skin structures:

Chromatophores: Tiny pigment-filled organs that expand and contract under nervous-system control, producing changing patterns.

Iridophores: Reflective structures that manipulate light, creating shimmering, iridescent effects.

Leucophores: Structures that scatter surrounding light, helping produce brightness and pale coloration.

Together, these systems generate astonishing visual displays. The animal can even alter its skin texture, producing bumps and ridges that resemble surrounding surfaces. 

PMC
+2

THE MYSTERY OF SEEING WITHOUT COLOR
One of the most surprising discoveries is that cuttlefish appear to lack conventional color vision.

A 2006 study published in Vision Research provided compelling behavioral evidence that the common cuttlefish, Sepia officinalis, is colorblind.

Yet it can blend remarkably well into colorful underwater environments!

Research published in 2011 demonstrated that cuttlefish camouflage can closely match backgrounds as perceived by potential fish predators.

Scientists continue investigating how these animals achieve such impressive results through brightness, contrast, visual patterns, and sophisticated neural processing. 

PubMed
+1

The cuttlefish reminds us how much remains undiscovered even among creatures living on our own planet.
WHEN THE SKIN BECOMES A LANGUAGE
Camouflage is only part of the story.

Cuttlefish also display striking patterns during courtship, rivalry, and other social encounters.

Researchers have investigated how polarized light reflected from their bodies may provide an additional channel of communication.

Their skin is not merely protective covering. It is part of an extraordinary communication system. 

PubMed
+1

What appears silent to human observers may contain information we are only beginning to understand.
WHAT SCRIPTURE REVEALS ABOUT CREATION
Thousands of years before modern marine biology, the psalmist celebrated the astonishing diversity of living creatures.

Psalm 104:24 (NIV) declares:

"How many are your works, LORD! In wisdom you made them all; the earth is full of your creatures."

The cuttlefish is not specifically mentioned in Scripture, and its abilities are natural biological processes rather than documented supernatural miracles.

Nevertheless, Christians may recognize in its extraordinary complexity another reason to praise the Creator.

John 1:3 teaches that all things were made through the eternal Word, whom John's Gospel identifies with Jesus Christ.

Colossians 1:16 likewise presents Christ as central to the creation of all things.

The natural world becomes an invitation to worship—not because every biological mystery proves a theological claim, but because faith recognizes creation as belonging to God.
THE SPIRITUAL LESSON — MORE THAN APPEARANCES
The cuttlefish survives partly by changing its outward appearance.

Human beings can also become remarkably skilled at presenting different appearances to the world.

Yet Scripture calls us beyond appearances.

In 1 Samuel 16:7, God teaches Samuel that human beings judge outward appearances, while the Lord looks at the heart.

Jesus repeatedly challenged outward religious performance that concealed inward spiritual neglect.

The Christian calling is not simply to appear righteous, but to experience genuine transformation through God's grace.

Romans 12:2 calls believers to be transformed through the renewing of their minds.

The Holy Spirit works within believers, cultivating the character described in Galatians 5:22–23: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.
A CREATION THAT POINTS BEYOND ITSELF
The cuttlefish can change its appearance almost instantly.

But the transformation Jesus offers reaches far deeper than skin.

Through His death and resurrection, Christ offers forgiveness, reconciliation with the Father, and new life through the Holy Spirit.

The greatest wonder is not merely an animal's ability to change its colors, but God's gracious power to change the human heart.

REFLECTION QUESTIONS
1. When you encounter extraordinary beauty in nature, does it lead you toward gratitude and worship?
2. Are you more concerned with how others see you or with the condition of your heart before God?
3. Where might the Holy Spirit be inviting you toward genuine inward transformation?
CLOSING PRAYER
Heavenly Father, thank You for the breathtaking wonders of Your creation. Lord Jesus, teach us to look beyond outward appearances and seek the beauty of holiness. Holy Spirit, renew our minds, purify our hearts, and transform our lives through Your grace. May every discovery deepen our gratitude, strengthen our faith, and draw us closer to You. To the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit be glory forever. In Jesus' mighty name, Amen.

Old Flame (Gambler's Folly Book 4) by Mellie Miller is a heartfelt second-chance paranormal shifter romance that blends emotional healing, mature love, and the magic of fate. Billionaire and bear shifter Kort Behrens has been lucky in business but unlucky in love—after two failed marriages and a string of gold diggers, he’s given up hope of finding a real connection. Elizabeth Murphy, a widow for four years, has rebuilt her life through her Reiki practice and the quiet companionship of her cat, Puzzle, still carrying the quiet ache of a long marriage that never fully satisfied her deeper desires. When these old college friends (who never dated) unexpectedly reunite on the way to the enchanted world of Gambler’s Folly, sparks fly and a full-blown romance blooms. Will they seize this second chance at a happily-ever-after, or will doubts and fears snatch it away? On Gambler’s Folly, every love story is a gamble—and Fate always deals the final hand. A slow-burn friends-to-lovers tale full of heart, sensuality, and the series’ signature fantasy charm.

About the author
Mellie Miller first fell in love with writing in a high school creative writing class. Married to her one and only, Steve, they began their journey through life in 1976 and, after two children and many moves, she finally has the time to devote to this love. She mainly writes fantasy romance, often with a paranormal twist, though she also has a short book sharing her struggle with breast cancer. Mellie feels her background in music, martial arts (2nd-degree black belt), and Reiki gives her a broad palette to draw on for her character development. Many of her stories incorporate one or more of these talents. As a lover of fantasy, Mellie hopes the worlds and stories she creates will give others a bit of escape from the hectic world around us and offer hope for a happy outcome. She and her husband live in rural Georgia and share their lives with cats, dogs, and a flock of chickens. She also writes under the pen name Sultonna Nadine.

text:
After 9/11 Putin was among the first leaders to call Bush, offering overflight rights, intelligence, and logistical support for Afghanistan. He later gifted a monument to the victims and visited Bush at his Crawford ranch in 2001 to discuss a post Cold War partnership.

Russia sought a place in the European security architecture. Yeltsin in 1991 called NATO membership a long term aim. In 2000 Putin told the BBC “Why not?” if treated as an equal and raised the idea with Clinton and NATO Secretary General George Robertson, who said countries must apply rather than receive special invitations. 

The West instead offered partnership bodies, Founding Act 1997, NATO-Russia Council 2002, that gave Russia a seat but no veto, while expanding the alliance eastward. Full equal membership was never offered.

In 2002, during this détente, Putin said Ukraine was a sovereign state free to choose its security path and that deeper NATO ties need not harm Russia Ukraine relations. Russia’s general opposition to NATO expansion remained, but the focus was practical cooperation.

That window closed. Planned U.S. missile defense interceptors in Poland and radar in the Czech Republic were seen in Moscow as a potential threat to its strategic deterrent and first strike stability. 

In 2008 the Bucharest Summit promised Ukraine and Georgia eventual NATO membership. U.S. Ambassador William Burns cabled that this was the “brightest of all red lines” for the Russian elite and risked civil war plus forced Russian intervention. 

Earlier warnings from Kennan 1997 “most fateful error”, Matlock, Perry and others had made the same point.

Western political support during the 2014 Maidan events, which removed a pro-Russian elected government, further hardened Russian perceptions of encirclement and regime change on its border.

text:
WOGBTC EVENING ORDER
October 19, 2026 • TSE Commander Training
MISSION: REST IN HIS PROTECTION — THEN BECOME A REFUGE FOR OTHERS
1SG 🫡 Tonight we build directly upon this morning's AWP promise from Psalm 91:4.
The morning order declared: “I am sheltered in Christ.”
Tonight's training asks a deeper question:
If I know that Christ is my refuge, how should that change the way I respond to someone who is frightened, overwhelmed, or hurting?
1 — THE ORDER
Receive God's protection. Reflect His compassion.
“God is our refuge and strength, A very present help in trouble.”
— Psalm 46:1, NKJV
Warrior Doctrine: A warrior secure in the Lord does not need to approach every difficulty defensively. He can stand firm in truth while extending mercy to others.
Our Commander Jesus Christ is not only our example of strength; He is our example of compassionate strength.
Battle Line: Because Christ is my refuge, I will bring His compassion into the struggles of others.
2 — THE TRAINING
TSE Doctrine: Security in Christ produces courage to serve.
A. Identify the source of your security.
Psalm 91:4 describes God's protection using the picture of shelter beneath His wings. The image communicates care, nearness, and faithfulness.
It does not promise that believers will never suffer. It teaches us where to place our trust when suffering comes.
Training: When uncertainty rises, remember whose authority governs your life.
B. Recognize the wounded without assuming they are the enemy.
“Rejoice with those who rejoice, and weep with those who weep.”
— Romans 12:15, NKJV
Not everyone who responds harshly is attacking you. Sometimes the person standing before you is carrying pain you cannot see.
Your mission is not to surrender discernment. It is to exercise discernment with compassion.
Training: Before responding to a difficult person, ask: What burden might this person be carrying?
C. Put compassion into action.
“Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.”
— Galatians 6:2, NKJV
Jesus demonstrated strength through service. He listened, healed, corrected, forgave, and spoke truth.
Compassion is not weakness. It is strength placed under Christ's command for another person's good.
Training: Practice listening without interrupting, offering practical help, and speaking truth without unnecessary harshness.
3 — THE EXECUTION
Tonight's field mission: Be a steady presence in someone's difficult moment.
Your mission is not to fix everyone. It is to faithfully care for the people Christ places in your path.
Observe: Notice someone who seems troubled, withdrawn, impatient, or discouraged.
Approach: Respond with patience rather than judgment.
Listen: Give the person room to speak without immediately offering solutions.
Serve: Offer encouragement, practical assistance, or prayer when welcome.
Release: Entrust the outcome to Christ. You are responsible for obedience, not controlling another person's response.
Commander's Orders
1SG, your military experience taught you that leadership involves protecting, preparing, and caring for those entrusted to you.
Tonight, apply that same discipline under the authority of Jesus Christ.
Do not mistake every difficult encounter for a battle. Some are opportunities to bring comfort.
Prayer of Deployment
Heavenly Father,
Thank You for covering me with Your faithfulness and providing refuge through Your Son, Jesus Christ.
Teach me to rest in Your protection rather than react from fear. Give me eyes to recognize suffering, ears to listen with patience, and courage to serve without seeking recognition.
Lord Jesus, govern my strength. Let my words bring truth, my actions demonstrate compassion, and my presence reflect Your love.
I belong to You, and I will care for the people You place in my path.
In the mighty name of Jesus Christ, Amen.
TONIGHT'S BATTLE LINE
I am sheltered in Christ, and I will serve others through His love.
TRAIN • STAND • EXECUTE

▫️🚀 Pentagon and BAE Systems Reach Agreement to Produce Up to 35,000 Precision Rocket Guidance Kits Annually▫️

🔹 Major Defense Production Agreement: The U.S. Department of War and BAE Systems have signed a framework agreement covering production of up to 25,000 Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS) guidance kits annually, with potential expansion to 35,000 units depending on demand from allied nations.

🔹 🎯 Counter Drone Warfare: APKWS provides U.S. military aircraft with a relatively inexpensive precision weapon for intercepting unmanned aerial systems (UAS). The technology converts conventional 70mm unguided rockets into laser guided weapons capable of engaging aerial threats.

🔹 💰 Lower Cost Interceptions: One of APKWS's biggest advantages is its comparatively low cost. Traditional air defense missiles can cost hundreds of thousands or even millions of dollars per interception, while APKWS guidance kits offer a significantly less expensive alternative against certain drones.

🔹 🏭 Expanding American Weapons Manufacturing: The agreement establishes a framework for increasing domestic production capacity, helping the Pentagon replenish precision weapons inventories while responding to growing military demand for counter drone capabilities.

🔹 🌍 Allied Demand Could Drive Expansion: Production could increase by another 10,000 guidance kits annually if international demand supports additional manufacturing investments. NATO members and other U.S. defense partners could benefit from expanded access to the technology.

🔹 ✈️ Aircraft Gain Greater Defensive Flexibility: APKWS can be integrated with compatible military aircraft and rocket systems, allowing pilots to engage certain drones without relying exclusively on more expensive air to air missiles. Its effectiveness depends on targeting conditions, integration and the type of threat.

🔹 ⚔️ Changing Economics of Modern Warfare: The agreement reflects a broader military priority to counter inexpensive drones with affordable, scalable weapons. Increasing APKWS production could help reduce the economic imbalance created when militaries use costly interceptor missiles against comparatively cheap unmanned aircraft.

text:
< Be John Marshall
< Born 1755, log cabin, Virginia frontier
< Eldest of fifteen children
< Your father surveys land with George Washington
< Formal schooling: less than two years total
< The Revolution comes. You enlist at nineteen.
< Valley Forge, winter of 1778. You survive.
< After the war, six weeks of law lectures at William & Mary
< That is your entire legal education
< You hang a shingle in Richmond
< Clients come. You win.
< 1788: Virginia ratifying convention for the Constitution
< Patrick Henry opposes. You speak in favor.
< The Constitution passes by ten votes
< President Adams offers you Attorney General. You decline.
< He offers France. You accept.
< The XYZ Affair: French diplomats demand bribes
< You refuse. Return home a national hero.
< Adams offers Secretary of State. This time you take it.
< January 1801: Adams nominates you Chief Justice
< Confirmed by the Senate in one day
< You are forty-five years old
< The Supreme Court has no building. No prestige. Little power.
< Marbury v. Madison, 1803
< You rule against your own party to establish judicial review
< The Court can now void acts of Congress
< You invented that. It is not in the Constitution.
< Thirty-four years on the bench. Over 1,000 opinions.
< You write 519 of them yourself
< McCulloch v. Maryland. Gibbons v. Ogden. Dartmouth College.
< The entire architecture of federal power, built by your pen
< Presidents come and go. You remain.
< Jefferson despises you. Can do nothing about it.
< You die in 1835, still serving
< The Liberty Bell cracks ringing at your funeral

Every law student learns Marbury. Few learn you had six weeks of training.

You took a court that met in a basement and made it co-equal to Congress.

The judicial branch you built has outlasted every president who tried to diminish it.
