text:
The rink manager told the soldier in uniform to come back on Wednesday.

Harold Moss had reached Fort Lewis in 1950 with a combat engineer outfit out of Detroit, and on a day off he wanted to skate. The manager was apologetic about it. There was a day of the week set aside for Black skaters, and this was not that day. Moss was twenty, wearing the uniform of a country that had sent him to train for Korea, and he could not get onto a rink floor in Tacoma. Looking back on it in 1994 he said it galled him, and that "I wanted to push for a change in the racial climate."

He already knew what the inside of that sentence sounded like. He had learned it three years earlier and two thousand miles east.

Moss was a senior in high school in Detroit, one of the strongest students in his class, and he applied for a place in an apprenticeship program run by the automobile industry. The application came back to him marked with two words. Unacceptable entry.

He went to his teachers about it. They already knew the thing he was only then finding out, which was that the program did not take Black students and would not have taken him.

He wrote long afterward that he understood they had done the best they could for him.

The family had come north from Gilmer, Texas, where Moss was born on October 1, 1929, the oldest of the three children of John Harris Moss and Ida Bell Wright. His father had gone looking for steady work and thought the north might be a more hospitable place to look.

For a while in Detroit the four of them lived in the detached garage of a friend's house.

His father learned to bump and paint cars at a place called Sam's Body Shop and opened a shop of his own ten years later, and he worked in it for the rest of his life. There was a college for Black students back in Texas that the older man had not been able to attend, and it was years before Moss worked out that his own schooling was being paid for out of that.

The plan was that Harold would come into the body shop and eventually take it over. He had the hands for it and not the appetite, so his father found him a place in a dental laboratory instead.

That was the work that fit. Fine mechanical work, close tolerances, a trade where a tenth of a millimeter shows. It held him on and off for the rest of his working life.

He took it into the service with him. Moss started as a field medic and was moved across to the post dental laboratory at Fort Lewis once somebody read his file, and when his discharge came through the laboratory hired him straight back as a civilian.

He married Williebelle Stringer in Detroit in 1951 and she joined him in Tacoma that December. Everyone called her Bil.

They bought a plot of land and meant to build on it. No bank would write Moss a mortgage and no contractor would take the job.

So they went looking for a house that already stood.

On the telephone he used what he called "your white voice." He said that sounding Black on a call to a realtor got you nowhere at all.

The voice got them as far as the doorstep. Agents who reached a house first and saw who was waiting would leave, so the couple learned to park down the street, sit until the agent walked up, and then drive in and catch him between his car and the front door where he could not step past them.

That was the routine. It did not get them a house.

A developer with a vacant lot met Moss face to face and then would not sell, on the grounds that his other buyers would not want to live beside him.

An owner in a hurry to move would not sell either. He was a minister, and he told Moss his neighbors would never forgive him for it.

The minister offered to walk them round and introduce them, which is how the Mosses came to be standing on a porch on an older street in Tacoma in the early 1950s, ringing a doorbell.

Nobody answered it. Bil could see the woman through the glass, standing inside, close enough to have reached the handle.

Moss rang it a second time. The woman looked back at him and did not move.

They went down the hill to another house. The couple who opened that door were about their own age, and they asked the Mosses in and sat them down on the couch.

Then the back door of that house started opening and closing.

By the time it stopped there were six, seven, eight neighbors in the room, and the questions came in a row.

Who had sent them. Whether they were fronting for an organization. Whether they were the kind of buyers people were calling blockbusters.

They said they wanted to buy a house.

One of the women in the room said she worked at a bank and knew what happened to property values when people like them moved in. She told them to go and live where they were wanted, with their own people, back up on K Street, where she said they had already driven out most of the Norwegians.

Bil started crying.

Moss joined the Tacoma branch of the NAACP and was its president in 1957 and 1958.

From 1957 to 1961 he co-chaired the branch's employment committee with Johnny Epps and Jimmy Paterson, leaning on the downtown stores to hire Black staff. Their main target was Sears and Roebuck, which the committee said had no Black employees at all, and they put out a flyer telling Tacoma shoppers not to buy where they could not work.

In 1960 a woman named Ella Capers was hired as a stenographer in the credit department of the downtown Sears. She was the first Black employee that store had ever had, and Moss put it down to the campaign.

He had heard Martin Luther King Jr. speak at the NAACP's national convention in 1957, held that year in Detroit. Moss came away from it certain that the road out was in his own hands and that it would take longer than anybody wanted.

In 1965 he opened his own dental laboratory south of Tacoma. Three years later he was one of the founders of the Tacoma Urban League.

On May 11, 1969, an attempted arrest on the Hilltop turned into a night of confrontation and property damage across the neighborhood, and a Tacoma police officer was wounded. Moss was one of a small number of Black leaders in the city whose presence on those streets held it to the single night.

In the days that followed, Black spokesmen in Tacoma demanded representation in the police and fire departments and better services for the Hilltop, and they got both. The group that came together that week called itself the Concerned Black Citizens, and it later took the name the Black Collective.

That autumn Moss ran for a seat on the Tacoma City Council.

His friend Thomas Dixon raised the money for a full modern campaign. When another civil rights worker went out in the September primary, that campaign's volunteers came across, and between them they doorbelled and then leafleted every precinct on the priority list. There were advertisements in the News Tribune and direct mail out to the likeliest voters.

Moss finished first in that primary out of a field of ten, more than a thousand votes clear of the man in second place.

Friends of his, Black and white both, had been coaching him on how he came across. He said so out loud in testimony at council meetings, that they had worked with him on "lowering the hostility level in my comments."

He spent that autumn in front of white Tacoma. Lions Clubs, Rotary, Kiwanis, room after room of people who were going to decide whether the city got new equal rights laws.

On November 4, 1969, he lost. The man who had finished second in the primary, a well known local sportscaster named John Jarstad, took the seat 23,440 to 19,893.

Tacoma's politics came apart the following year on their own. Five council members were removed by a recall in September 1970, after a campaign driven by residents and by business figures who had watched the council's conservative bloc fight the federal money aimed at the Hilltop.

On October 13, 1970, the council appointed Moss to one of the empty chairs.

He was the first African American to hold public office in Tacoma or in Pierce County, and he got there because an argument among white politicians had emptied five chairs at once. In 1971 he won the seat outright, 17,947 votes to Jack Gamble's 14,073.

From 1970 to 1981 Moss also ran the Urban League's apprenticeship training program, working the unions and the contractors to get young people of color into the building trades. The man whose own apprenticeship application had come back refused was now the one deciding who got in.

With a fellow council member named Jack Warnick he wrote much of the ordinance that created the city's Human Rights Commission, and the two of them were behind Tacoma's first affirmative action plans.

In 1975 he gave up the seat. The Urban League employed him, the possibility of a conflict of interest was raised, and rather than sit under it he resigned.

In 1981 the Reagan administration cut off the federal program that paid for his Urban League work, and Moss went back to making dentures. He also pushed the state to let people outside dentistry fit them, which Washington eventually legalized.

He lost a council race in 1983. The council appointed him to another vacancy in 1987 and he held it in the election that followed. On November 5, 1991 he won it again, 19,561 votes to Jerry Thorpe's 16,226.

Jack Hyde was elected mayor of Tacoma in November 1993 and asked Moss, a friend of long standing, to be his deputy. On January 17, 1994, less than three weeks into the term, Hyde died of a heart attack.

Eight days later the council voted unanimously to make Moss the mayor of Tacoma. He was the city's thirty-fourth mayor and its first Black one.

He kept his day job through it, as the state transportation department's civil rights manager for construction projects, getting minority-owned and women-owned firms onto state contracts while he ran a city.

Then the arithmetic in the city's own rules caught up with him. The mayor sat as part of the council, and Tacoma's term limits counted every year Moss had already spent in a council chair, so the city's first Black mayor was not eligible to stand in the 1995 election to keep the job.

He served the two years and handed it on. When he ran for the office on his own account in 2001, he lost that too, and when he tried for a council seat again in 2007 he lost that.

Harold Moss was the first Black mayor Tacoma ever had, and Tacoma never elected him to it.

The county took him instead. On November 5, 1996 he won a seat on the Pierce County Council, 17,042 votes to Richard Nivens's 8,042, and he served from January 1997 to the end of 2004, the last of it as chairman.

In 2009 the University of Puget Sound gave him an honorary doctorate of laws.

One of the things he counted himself proudest of was getting the lights put on the East 34th Street Bridge, a concrete arch thrown up in 1936 over what later became State Route 7.

On October 1, 2019, his ninetieth birthday, the city renamed it the Harold G. Moss Bridge. The council's resolution said the lights on it should stand as a shining monument to the ways Tacoma was brighter for what he had done. The name went up while he was still alive to drive across it, which is not how that honor is usually handed out.

The first document in this story came back to him with two words on it about entry. The last one is a city resolution with his name in the title.

He died in Tacoma on September 21, 2020, ten days short of his ninety-first birthday.

The Pierce County Council has had one Black member in the whole of its history. Moss took that seat in January 1997, and it was still true the day he died.

The people who worked with him kept repeating a line of his afterward. It was "an honor to be first, but you never want to be the last."

🇺🇲 🇺🇦 Trump suggests Ukraine should replace Zelensky as its chief negotiator, dismissing the Ukrainian president's accusation that Washington is on the wrong side of history.

“Zelensky doesn't know what he's talking about,” Trump told reporters outside the White House on Monday.

The US president argued that Ukraine could have secured a better peace agreement years ago if Zelensky had followed his advice.

“Maybe it's time for Zelensky to get somebody else to negotiate,” he said, adding that he believes the Ukrainian leader is not doing enough to end the war.

The remarks come hours after Zelensky accused Washington of pressuring Ukraine toward capitulation in an interview with Bloomberg. He also alleged that deliveries of Patriot interceptors already paid for by European allies were being delayed and that further American support could be restricted if Kyiv continued striking Russian oil infrastructure.

Trump separately described Russia's conduct regarding Ukraine as “fine,” saying Moscow had not been doing much. His comments follow another night of Russian ballistic missile and drone attacks that damaged energy infrastructure across Ukraine.

The dispute now extends beyond the terms of a possible ceasefire to who should represent Ukraine in negotiations. Trump has offered no evidence that replacing Zelensky as negotiator would secure an agreement acceptable to Kyiv.

🇺🇦 🇺🇲 SCOOP: Zelensky accuses Trump of pressuring Ukraine toward capitulation, threatening further cuts to US support and withholding deliveries of Patriot interceptors already paid for under the PURL program, in a new interview with Bloomberg.

“I believe steps have been taken to convince Ukraine to capitulate,” the Ukrainian president said, while clarifying that he was not claiming capitulation was necessarily Washington's intended objective.

Zelensky also revealed a proposal he made to the Trump administration: Ukraine would stop striking Russian diesel infrastructure if the United States supplied Patriot missiles to defend Ukrainian cities and energy facilities.

“My latest model was: We don't target Russian diesel, you give us missiles for Patriot systems to protect our facilities.”

According to Zelensky, Washington has demanded that Kyiv halt attacks on Russian refineries without agreeing to the proposed exchange. He said Ukrainian officials have been warned that further strikes could result in additional American support being disconnected, although he did not specify which systems or services were threatened.

The dispute extends to weapons already purchased.

“We have paid for the weapons,” Zelensky said, referring to deliveries financed through the NATO-coordinated PURL procurement mechanism. “A part of the supplies has been authorized, while the rest haven't been. And this is not a technical issue.”

⚠️ He said Ukraine is now receiving just 12 Patriot interceptors per month from the United States, approximately one-quarter of the delivery rate under the Biden administration.

The interview follows Trump's statement defending his decision to delay new sanctions against Russia, citing peace negotiations, Moscow's potential assistance to Iran and the impact of Ukrainian refinery strikes on global diesel prices.

Despite the confrontation, Zelensky expressed hope that relations with Washington could improve after the November 3 US midterm elections.

“Politics is very aggressive during election time. I think it is agony now, but after elections, life will continue and I believe it will be calmer.”

Source: Bloomberg News, October 18, 2026. / @alexwickham

text:
🇺🇲 🇷🇺 🇨🇳 Trump says he is willing to meet Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war in Ukraine, even if Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is absent, opening the door to an unprecedented three-way summit that could place Kyiv's future on the negotiating table without its own government present.

“Whatever I can do to end the war,” Trump told reporters when pressed on whether Zelenskyy would need to participate.

His remarks follow a Wall Street Journal report that Putin proposed meeting Trump and Xi on the sidelines of the November 18–19 APEC summit in Shenzhen, China. According to the Journal, the Russian president raised the idea during his October 9 telephone conversation with Trump, seeking to negotiate an end to the war on terms favorable to Moscow.

The Kremlin confirmed Monday that the possibility of a trilateral meeting had been discussed, although no agreement on the summit or its agenda has been reached.

Trump also suggested that nuclear disarmament could be a central subject of the talks, saying he would welcome a meeting with both leaders to discuss nuclear weapons and denuclearization.

“If we can do denuclearization, I will have done the world a big, big favor,” he said.

The proposal arrives amid deteriorating relations between Washington and Kyiv. Trump has criticized Ukraine's renewed attacks on Russian oil refineries, while his administration has eased some economic restrictions on Russian energy exports and faced Ukrainian accusations of disrupting critical military assistance and intelligence sharing.

For Moscow, a summit involving the leaders of the United States, Russia and China, without Ukrainian participation, would offer an opportunity to elevate negotiations over Ukraine to a great-power forum. Whether such discussions could produce an enforceable settlement without Kyiv's consent remains unresolved.

No trilateral summit has been formally announced, and there is no indication that Ukraine has agreed to the proposed format.

Where you see a show matters. Fontainebleau made that obvious.

We saw Logic at BleauLive Theater, and the sound, lighting and stage made it feel like a complete production. The clips I’d watched online hadn’t prepared me for the experience inside that room.

And look at what Vegas has to offer:

🎤 BleauLive: major production capabilities in a theater holding up to 3,800 people.

🔊 Dolby Live: 402 speakers, Atmos capabilities and a farthest seat just 145 feet from the stage.

🎶 Resorts World Theatre: immersive spatial audio, with the farthest seat only 150 feet away.

🌐 Sphere: precision audio and visuals that surround the audience.

🏛️ The Colosseum: upgraded sound, lighting, video and flexible seating built around the performance.

To me, these investments add up to a serious advantage: Las Vegas is making the venue itself a reason to travel.

You can catch the same tour in Arizona or California. But the room changes the experience—and after seeing Logic at Fontainebleau, I’d pay more attention to WHERE I book my next concert.

Which Vegas venue gets it right?

🎨 DEADLINE EXTENDED! Sacred Art Prize 2026 — Call for Entries Now Open Through October 27!

In response to requests from several artists for additional time to prepare their submissions, the Catholic Art Institute is pleased to extend the deadline for the 2026 Sacred Art Prize to Tuesday, October 27, 2026!

Recognizing excellence in contemporary sacred art, the Sacred Art Prize will feature an international juried online exhibition in November 2026, hosted by the Catholic Art Institute, followed by a live exhibition in 2027 at The Sacred Art Gallery in Mesa, Arizona.

The Sacred Art Prize reaches a worldwide audience and has become a valuable resource for architects, liturgical arts firms, clergy, patrons, and collectors seeking exceptional sacred art and artists for commissions and acquisitions.

Works by Sacred Art Prize and Bernini Awards winners have attracted the attention of collectors and patrons, leading to sales and new professional opportunities.

The competition offers artists an opportunity to gain international recognition, exhibit and sell their work, and connect with those actively supporting the renewal of sacred art.

We extend our sincere gratitude to Canning Liturgical Arts and Willet Studios, whose generous sponsorship helps make the Sacred Art Prize possible and supports our shared mission of renewing sacred art and beauty in the life of the Church.

NEW DEADLINE: OCTOBER 27, 2026

We invite artists from around the world to submit their finest work and participate in this growing movement to renew sacred art and culture through beauty.

Enter the 2026 Sacred Art Prize today!

text:
In June 2026, xAI quietly replaced Grok's per-product daily usage limits with a single shared "weekly usage pool."  This did not hit everyone at once. It rolled out over time up until now. It is a change that effectively slashed the total output available to paying subscribers by an estimated 80% or more.  

The FTC complaint record is extensive. A July 2026 Gizmodo investigation documented numerous complaints filed at https://t.co/jyACR2HRB2, including:

"To advertise usage levels, accept a year paid subscription in advance, only to then 3 months later effectively limit the service capacity to a 4th of the promised rate for payment is standard 'bait and switch' fraud."

"I paid $300 for a year of service with the original rate limits and have now had my paid subscription reduced to the degree that the value for service paid is significantly crippled." 

"The product reduced usage by 90% without informing me." 

"I believe that this is extortion."

Under US state consumer protection statutes (California UCL, Texas DTPA, etc.), materially degrading a paid service mid-subscription without meaningful notice or a prorated refund option is a deceptive practice.

What xAI offers in response: Buy "Extra Usage Credits" starting at $5, or upgrade to a higher tier.

What xAI does not offer: A published number for what the weekly pool actually contains, a prorated refund for annual subscribers whose service was materially  reduced.

Subscribers who paid for a year of access at advertised limits are being asked to accept a fraction of that value or pay more. That is not a pricing update. That is a bait-and-switch.

text:
$RBB Q3 2026 earnings: RBB Bancorp's margin widens, but its deposits stop getting cheaper

RBB Bancorp earned more as it repaid costly debt and problem loans shrank, but a building sale flatters the result. The Los Angeles lender serving Asian-American communities lifted profit per share 25% from a year ago. Its net interest margin, the gap between loan income and funding costs, widened to 3.16%. Chief executive Johnny Lee credited strong loan production for the first loan growth since March. By our math a building sale and a lower tax rate supplied about a fifth of the profit.

• Profit per share: $𝟬.𝟳𝟰 ($0.59 a year ago)
• Net interest margin: 𝟯.𝟭𝟲% (3.06% last quarter)
• Loans: $𝟯.𝟰𝟬 𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻 (+10.8% annualized from June)
• Full-year tax rate outlook: 𝗟𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗼 𝟮𝟲.𝟵% (28.0% in July)

⚖️ 𝗩𝗲𝗿𝗱𝗶𝗰𝘁: 🟢 Bullish

The story got better because loans are growing again and the margin resumed widening. The bad news: the growth came almost entirely from home mortgages, and deposit costs stopped falling just as the Federal Reserve raised rates.

The question now is whether the margin can keep widening when deposits no longer get cheaper. Either new loans and the debt repaid in July carry it higher, or repricing deposits and the Fed's rise eat the gain. January's fourth-quarter deposit cost will tell.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝗕𝘂𝗹𝗹 𝗖𝗮𝘀𝗲

🟢🟢 𝗖𝗵𝗲𝗮𝗽𝗲𝗿 𝗗𝗲𝗯𝘁 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗥𝗲𝗰𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗪𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗻𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗠𝗮𝗿𝗴𝗶𝗻
The net interest margin is the gap between what RBB Bancorp earns on loans and what it pays for money. After the second-quarter results, finance chief Lynn Hopkins told analysts to expect a margin near the first quarter's 3.15% and above the second quarter's 3.06%.

The margin reached 3.16%, just above the top of that range. The main reason is that the Los Angeles lender repaid part of its subordinated notes on July 1, which cut its borrowing costs.

• Subordinated notes repaid: $40 million, leaving $80 million at 7.02%
• Interest on long-term debt: $1.4 million, down $684,000 from the second quarter
• Cost of all borrowings: 5.04%, from 5.53%

Not all of the gain will last. The company said the higher asset yield came mostly from "higher nonaccrual interest recoveries on loans" and a $320,000 special dividend from the Federal Home Loan Bank. By our math the dividend alone added 0.03 points, so the underlying margin was about 3.13%, still inside Hopkins's range.

What to watch: the fourth-quarter margin, due in January, the first full period after the Federal Reserve's quarter-point rate rise. A reading at or above 3.13% would show cheaper debt and new loans at 6.30% outweigh dearer deposits.

🟢🟢 𝗥𝗲𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗲𝘀 𝗡𝗼𝘄 𝗖𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝗡𝗼𝗻𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗟𝗼𝗮𝗻𝘀 𝗧𝘄𝗶𝗰𝗲 𝗢𝘃𝗲𝗿
Two years ago RBB Bancorp's main problem was bad construction and property loans. Chief executive Johnny Lee said credit quality continued to improve and the bank was "well positioned to continue these positive trends to finish the year".

Borrowers repaid $5.3 million of nonperforming loans in the quarter, and only $522,000 of new ones joined the list. Write-offs were almost nil for a second quarter, so the $500,000 set aside for losses reflects loan growth, not new problems.

• Nonperforming loans: 0.55% of loans, from 1.38% a year ago
• Reserve as a share of nonperforming loans: 234%, from 184% in June
• Net charge-offs: 0.01% of average loans, annualized

This matters because credit costs held profit down last year: the provision for the first nine months was $9.8 million then, against $300,000 now. With reserves at twice the bad-loan balance, the bank can absorb a new problem loan without a charge to profit. One caution: special mention loans, a watch list one step above substandard, rose $4.1 million as the bank added $7.0 million.

What to watch: the fourth-quarter special mention balance. A second increase would mean new problem loans form faster than borrowers repay the old ones.

🟢 𝗥𝗕𝗕 𝗣𝗮𝗶𝗱 𝗢𝗳𝗳 𝗖𝗼𝘀𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝗡𝗼𝘁𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗞𝗲𝗽𝘁 𝗕𝘂𝘆𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗕𝗮𝗰𝗸 𝗦𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗲𝘀
RBB Bancorp holds far more capital than regulators require. Last year it paused buybacks until it had decided what to do with $120 million of costly subordinated notes.

On July 1 the bank repaid $40 million of those notes at face value. It also spent $4.5 million on buybacks, cutting the share count by about 159,000 by our math, and declared the usual dividend for November.

Capital ratios slipped because subordinated notes count as regulatory capital: total capital fell to 22.05% of risk-weighted assets from 23.44%. Common equity tier 1, the core measure, held at 17.87%, leaving room to redeem the remaining notes and keep buying stock.

What to watch: whether the remaining $80 million of notes, at 7.02%, go before year-end. A second redemption would widen the margin again.

🐻 𝗕𝗲𝗮𝗿 𝗖𝗮𝘀𝗲

🔴🔴 𝗟𝗼𝗮𝗻 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘁𝗵 𝗖𝗮𝗺𝗲 𝗙𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗠𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗴𝗮𝗴𝗲𝘀, 𝗡𝗼𝘁 𝗙𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗕𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘀
Chief executive Johnny Lee said "Strong loan production drove double-digit annualized loan growth in the quarter". The loan book did grow $89.8 million, but the production figures tell a different story.

New lending did not rise. Growth came because borrowers repaid less, the bank stopped selling mortgages, and it bought loans from other lenders.

• Originations: $154.0 million, from $187.8 million a year ago
• Loans sold: $2.7 million, from $50.2 million last quarter; loans bought: $21.9 million
• Single-family mortgages: up $80.7 million, now 51.8% of loans
• Commercial and industrial loans: down $165,000

This matters because the lender opened a Northern California loan production office this year to build commercial lending, and that office has now cost a full quarter of salaries and rent with nothing to show in the business-loan line.

Mortgages also earn less: home loans yielded 5.5% against 7.3% for business loans in the last breakdown it published. Commercial real estate is still 37.7% of loans, and construction lending produced the last wave of bad loans.

What to watch: the split of fourth-quarter originations between mortgages and commercial loans, and whether loan sales resume. A quarter in which business loans grow faster than mortgages would show the Bay Area team is producing, not just costing.

🔴🔴 𝗗𝗲𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁𝘀 𝗦𝘁𝗼𝗽𝗽𝗲𝗱 𝗚𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗖𝗵𝗲𝗮𝗽𝗲𝗿 𝗮𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗙𝗲𝗱 𝗥𝗮𝗶𝘀𝗲𝗱 𝗥𝗮𝘁𝗲𝘀
For five quarters RBB Bancorp's recovery ran on cheaper deposits as maturing certificates renewed at lower rates. That tailwind has stopped: the company said quarter-end deposit rates rose partly because the Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate by a quarter point.

• Cost of interest-bearing deposits: 3.35%, from 3.34% last quarter
• Rate on all deposits at quarter end: 2.82%, from 2.75% in June
• Loans as a share of deposits: 100.1%, from 97.6%

There is good news in the mix: retail deposits grew $63.3 million, so the bank cut wholesale deposits, money bought through brokers, to 1.8% of the total. But the new money came as time deposits and savings, while free checking balances fell $34.7 million.

This matters because loans now exceed deposits, so the lender borrowed $20 million more from the Federal Home Loan Bank. Hopkins said last quarter that about $1.5 billion of certificates mature within a year, mostly below rates rivals now offer, so that money reprices higher as the Fed moves up.

What to watch: the cost of interest-bearing deposits in the fourth quarter, the first full period after the rate rise. A second straight increase would mean dearer deposits are eating the gain from the notes redemption.

🔴 𝗧𝗵𝗲 $𝟮𝟬 𝗠𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗿𝘁𝘆 𝗜𝘀 𝗦𝘁𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗨𝗻𝘀𝗼𝗹𝗱
The largest problem asset is no longer a loan. In the spring RBB Bancorp foreclosed on a partly built construction project and holds it as other real estate owned, property the bank owns after foreclosure, at $19.8 million. Hopkins said last quarter she was looking for a resolution in the second half.

Nothing moved in the third quarter: the September balance matched June's, and the property is now 51% of nonperforming assets by our math. Repossessed property sits outside the loan loss reserve, so a sale below carrying value hits profit directly; a $2 million shortfall would cost about $0.09 a share by our math.

What to watch: the fourth-quarter balance of other real estate owned and any gain or loss on a sale. A sale near carrying value would halve problem assets.

👓 𝗢𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝗧𝗵𝗲𝗺𝗲𝘀

𝗕𝗿𝗼𝗼𝗸𝗹𝘆𝗻 𝗢𝗳𝗳𝗶𝗰𝗲 𝗦𝗮𝗹𝗲 𝗔𝗱𝗱𝗲𝗱 $𝟮.𝟳 𝗠𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻
RBB Bancorp sold the Brooklyn office building that housed its loan operations center and booked a $2.7 million gain. It has leased the building back for four months and will move the team to new leased space in Brooklyn in 2027, so rent rises while the gain does not repeat. The sale flattered the efficiency ratio, costs as a share of revenue; without it, by our math, the ratio was 57.8%, little changed from June.

— • — • —

💲 𝗢𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝗞𝗣𝗜𝘀

𝗧𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗶𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗯𝗼𝗼𝗸 𝘃𝗮𝗹𝘂𝗲 𝗽𝗲𝗿 𝘀𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗲 (𝟮𝟲𝗤𝟯): $𝟮𝟳.𝟰𝟰  ⇘ decelerating
Up 0.8% from June and 6.0% from a year ago, the slowest annual gain in four quarters. Tangible book value is equity minus goodwill, per share. Growth slowed because higher market rates pushed unrealized losses on the bond portfolio to $30.6 million, cutting equity by $6.8 million after tax and offsetting about half of the quarter's profit.

𝗡𝗼𝗻𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗲𝗻𝘀𝗲 (𝟮𝟲𝗤𝟯): $𝟭𝟵.𝟱 𝗺𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻  ⇗ accelerating
Up 2.8% from the second quarter and 4.6% from a year ago. Hopkins has pointed to an $18 million to $19 million quarterly range since last autumn, and costs have now run above it for three straight quarters. Salaries and occupancy drove the rise: the Northern California office ran for a full quarter and the bank now pays rent in Brooklyn.

𝗥𝗲𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗻 𝗼𝗻 𝗮𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝗮𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘁𝘀 (𝟮𝟲𝗤𝟯): 𝟭.𝟭𝟳%  ⇗ accelerating
Return on average assets, profit earned on each dollar of assets, rose to 1.17% from 0.97% last quarter, the highest in the two years we track. The building gain and the lower tax rate explain the whole step: without them, by our math, the return would have been about 0.93%, slightly below the second quarter.

— • — • —

🔮 𝗚𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲

𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲 𝗲𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝘁𝗮𝘅 𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲: 𝟮𝟲.𝟵%  ⇗ accelerating
🠇 cut from 28.0%
Lowered. The company now expects to pay 26.9% of pre-tax profit in tax this year, down from the 28.0% it planned in July, because it bought more federal tax credits. By our math the plan implies a fourth-quarter rate near 27%, well above this quarter's. A lower rate also eases the comparison with last year's 24.2%.

𝗤𝘂𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗹𝘆 𝗱𝗶𝘃𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗻𝗱: $𝟬.𝟭𝟲 𝗽𝗲𝗿 𝘀𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗲  ⇒ stable
🠆 unchanged from $0.16 per share
Unchanged. The board declared $0.16 a share, payable November 12, the same payment the lender has made since at least 2024. The dividend took 21% of this quarter's profit, and with buybacks the bank returned $7.2 million, about 57% of net income. Management said in July it would consider a higher dividend; the release does not mention one.

— • — • —

❓ 𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗤𝘂𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗿𝘁𝘆 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗵, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘄𝗵𝗼 𝘄𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗯𝘂𝘆 𝗶𝘁?
The $19.8 million repossessed project is half of all problem assets and sits outside the loan loss reserve. The as-is appraisal, the cost to finish it and the buyer pool decide whether the promised second-half sale brings a loss.

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗺𝘂𝗰𝗵 𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗴𝗶𝗻 𝗰𝗮𝗺𝗲 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗼𝗻 𝗯𝗮𝗱 𝗹𝗼𝗮𝗻𝘀?
The company said recoveries on formerly nonaccrual loans were the main reason asset yields rose, but gave no figure. Without it, readers cannot tell how much of the 3.16% margin repeats.

text:
"Breaking the Cowboy Curse": Fourteen Years of Frustration... 

October 13th, 2012, Laramie, Wyoming. Air Force 28, Wyoming 27. The final whistle was only the beginning. Wyoming head coach Dave Christensen confronted Troy Calhoun in a profanity-filled exchange that made national headlines. Christensen accused Air Force of manipulating an injury to stop the clock, calling TC "Howdy Doody." Air Force left with a win. Nobody could have imagined that fourteen years later, the Falcons would still be searching for their next victory inside War Memorial Stadium. 

November 17th, 2018. Snow, 19 degrees. I stood there as Air Force led 27-14 in the fourth. It felt perfect for November Falcon Football. Then a critical possession stalled. Wyoming scored 21 unanswered. Final: 35-27. Air Force finished 5 and 7, one win short of a bowl. Another trip to Laramie. Another disappointment. And the Cowboy Curse lived on. Through all of it, one familiar face has remained on the Air Force sideline: Troy Calhoun. Now in his twentieth season, he's built a legacy worthy of comparison with Fisher DeBerry. Christensen is long gone. But Calhoun remains, and perhaps nobody understands the depth and weight of this streak better. Fourteen years later, the coach who last won in Laramie has another chance. Different players. Different circumstances. Same head coach. Unfinished business. 

Friday, October 23rd. Air Force arrives 5 - 1 after a convincing win over UNLV. Wyoming is 4 - 3 and also much improved. What's different? Adversity forced freshmen to play last year, especially on defense. Now sophomores, supported by veterans like Blake Fletcher, Dallas Daley, Jaden Oquendo, Roger Jones Jr., and Corey Johnson, they're growing up under Steve Russ. Alex Perez, Max Mustell, and Cade Paterson took their lumps as freshmen and are now players teammates rely upon. Offensively, when Liam Szarka went down, Sophmore Evan Medders stepped in and surged, including 152 yards and three touchdowns against UNLV. He's joined by reliable Owen Allen, patient weapon Rocco Conti, Matt Long, Kemper Hodges, and Gage LaDue. But none of it happens without Bolt Diesel. Rudy Varela, Jon Ashford, Alec Falk, Luke Vandahar, TJ Tarascio, and a seasoned unit coached by former Falcon lineman Steed "Lobo" Lobotzke. Under his guidance, Air Force captured three straight national rushing titles. This is a run-first, run-second team. Everyone knows it. Against UNLV, that meant four hundred thirty rushing yards. Those yards weren't magic. They were forged in the trenches. And make no mistake: if the Falcons break the "Cowboy Curse", that victory will run through the Bolt Diesel offensive line. Add dependable kicker Carter Cremascoli, and you've got a group that knows how to respond. War Memorial Stadium is beautiful and unforgiving, but curses only live as long as we believe in them. The Red Sox waited eighty-six years. For Falcon fans who remember 2012 and endured 2018, fourteen feels long enough. This group isn't responsible for the past. Wyoming will be ready. Nothing is guaranteed. But this team has shown resilience, maturity, and an ability to respond when challenged. Fourteen years. Five straight losses in Laramie. One head coach who's been there through it all. Friday night offers a fresh chance. Forget the history. Forget the streak. Forget the curse. Because when the ball is kicked off Friday night in Laramie...

Nothing Else Medders‼️
⚡️🏈🇺🇲🚫🤠

Article by Rick Baum @Falcon8fan

text:
Moon Calendar, October 20, 2026, Tuesday.

The waxing gibbous Moon gathers more light with each passing day and remains in the airy sign of Aquarius throughout the day. The fullness of the Moon is drawing nearer, yet we do not need to find a final answer to every question today. One of Aquarius’s finest gifts is curiosity: an openness that dares to ask whether the world can truly be seen in more than one way. Sometimes a single honest question lets in more light than a certainty we have carefully guarded. Today, it is worth leaving room for what is not yet clear, because our thoughts often begin to move in a new direction when we do not rush to close the matter.

When caring for the body, comfort around the lower legs and ankles deserves attention. On chilly autumn days, a tight sock cuff or a hard shoe edge can press against this area; soft-edged garments that fit well can feel more comfortable throughout the day. Good care grows from small, sensible choices, with room for gentleness in everyday life. Freedom sometimes appears in a very simple form: in feeling comfortable within the day we have.

In beauty care, a playful, delicate choice of colour can bring freshness today. Should you feel inspired, draw a fine line of opalescent blue eyeshadow along the roots of your lashes, allowing this small detail to bring a distinctive light to your gaze. A single unexpected shade can express your personality beautifully. Aquarius’s freedom can also be seen in beauty: in choosing according to our own taste and enjoying the subtle details that make a look our own.

In the garden, one question can lead us to the smallest of its inhabitants: where will beneficial insects find shelter when the cold arrives? Gather a few dry, hollow plant stems, tie them loosely together, and place them in a quiet spot protected from rain. Such a little refuge may offer shelter to the garden’s tiny creatures, and life may gather around it again in spring. The autumn garden is both a farewell to colour and a home for unseen guests; here, a few quiet stems can create a place of refuge.

Today, we can allow our souls to ask questions without shame. Curiosity shows that there is still room within us to learn and discover new layers of the world. Today’s affirmation is: “I ask with an open heart and welcome what the world reveals with trust.” The Moon’s message is that inner spaciousness grows from the courage to explore. When we do not hurry past uncertainty, a question can slowly become a direction, and a direction can unfold into a new possibility. A question today may illuminate a path we could not even see yesterday.

If you would like an up-to-date Moon Calendar every morning, subscribe so you won't miss a single day.
Wishing you a blessed day!

Chubbytoro is up $48.7K in a single day, with total PnL at +$32.7K after joining in May 2026.

Profile shows $57.9K positions value, $150.8K biggest win, 110 markets traded, and $7.2M total volume. 
@Polymarket Active positions focus on NFL and NHL spreads

Washington Commanders – San Francisco 49ers
And spreads on Rangers.

How the approach looks
▪️ Focuses on sports spreads (point spreads in NFL/NHL).  
▪️ Holds relatively large share counts in active markets.  
▪️ Contracts pay $1 if the spread covers, $0 if not.  
▪️ High total volume relative to current PnL suggests frequent trading or larger size rather than pure buy-and-hold.  
▪️ Interesting part is the scale: big volume and a large past-day swing alongside a still-modest cumulative PnL.

The numbers
▪️ Past-day gain: +$48.7K (visible on the chart).  
▪️ Cumulative PnL: +$32.7K on $7.2M volume.  
▪️ Rough return on volume is low (~0.45%), which is consistent with high-turnover sports trading where many small edges or hedges net out.  
▪️ Average position size and exact entry prices are not shown; only current values and share counts appear.  
▪️ Biggest single win listed: $150.8K (could be one market or a closed position).

Why this matters
Sports spreads can offer edges if a trader reads injury news, weather, or line movement faster than the market, or provides liquidity on both sides. High volume and a large daily swing fit someone active in liquid NFL/NHL markets.  

Limitations are clear: cumulative PnL is still relatively small versus volume, so one or two big wins (or losses) can dominate. Fees, adverse selection on spreads, and variance in individual games all reduce edge. A single strong day does not prove the process is repeatable.

Is the combination of high volume and a big daily gain a real sports-spread edge, or mostly variance plus active trading that still has to prove itself over more markets?

text:
COMMANDERS ⛑️ @ 49ERS ⛏️ (SF -7.5 | 52.5 Total)

Can the 49ers pay off their massive ownership?

Let's break it down  👇

GAME SETUP

San Francisco carries a 29.75-point implied total against a Washington defense allowing 29.8 points per game.

The 49ers are the clear favorites, but Washington’s 25-point team total gives us a path to a competitive game.

The biggest variables are Mike Evans’ status, Washington’s returning pass catchers, and how much ownership lands on the obvious San Francisco pieces.

SAN FRANCISCO ⛏️

Christian McCaffrey is the best skill-position play in the game. His snap rate remains elite, and his receiving role gives him upside even against a Washington defense that has been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground.

George Kittle becomes especially interesting if Mike Evans sits. Kittle already has a strong matchup and a path to more targets with Deebo Samuel out. 

He’ll be popular, but the role makes that ownership reasonable.

Mike Evans is questionable with rib and Achilles issues. At $9,600, he needs touchdowns to justify the price, and his status affects the entire 49ers passing-game pool.

If Evans sits, Brandin Cooks is my preferred cheap receiver, followed by Christian Kirk, Jordan Watkins, and Jacob Cowing. At least one could matter simply because of the available salary and opportunity.

If Evans plays, the cheap receivers become much less appealing. Kirk’s availability is another variable to monitor.

Kaelon Black is a deep option if San Francisco gets far enough ahead to rest its starters or reduce McCaffrey’s workload.

WASHINGTON ⛑️

Rachaad White is a strong value at $6,600 with Jacory Croskey-Merritt out. White should lead the backfield and offers receiving upside, while Austin Ekeler’s limited role last week makes him harder to trust.

Stefon Diggs is expected back after two limited practices. If active, he gets a slight preference over Terry McLaurin, though both should project similarly.

Antonio Williams is an interesting tournament option. His projections may lag behind his upside, creating a chance to get exposure at lower ownership.

Treylon Burks is the preferred punt over Dyami Brown, with his playing time trending upward while Brown’s has declined.

Chig Okonkwo faces a difficult matchup against a strong 49ers defense against tight ends. I’d rather take a chance on Williams at a similar price.

ROSTER CONSTRUCTION 📊

49ers onslaughts are a natural starting point given the 29.75-point team total and Washington’s defensive struggles.

McCaffrey is the strongest individual play, while Kittle’s value rises if Evans is ruled out.

Washington has enough implied scoring to keep up, so Diggs, McLaurin, and Williams remain viable if you expect a competitive game.

If Evans sits, ownership on Kittle and the cheap 49ers receivers could climb quickly. Pay attention to which value options become the field’s preferred salary savers.

The alternative is to build around a San Francisco blowout. Washington could struggle to keep pace, making 49ers-heavy constructions more attractive.

Stephanie Rice Unfairly Slammed for Posting “God Asked Me to Resign”
by @Rod_Lampard [TESTIMONIES]

Swimming royalty Stephanie Rice is being hammered over a caption stating she resigned from her job after hearing from God.

On Instagram, the former Australian Olympian made a clear argument about how God directed the decision.

Critics weren’t interested and chose to flood her post with mockery instead.

One user ironically accused Rice of being “tone deaf.” That person then added, “To just quit a high-paying job because ‘God told me so’ is so arrogant. You quit your job because you could.”

Another wrote, “This is so silly. Read the Bible because it sounds like you have been deceived.”

Facebook’s Christian-hating trolls were worse.

Someone commented, “It’s not God talking to you. It’s called Schizophrenia.”

In another example, someone left an essay-length comment, lecturing Rice about privilege and being a public figure. The person told Rice to choose her words more wisely because they could encourage people to be reckless.

At least two people wrote “oh, dear,” while others took Rice to task for allegedly making God her business partner. The pile-on included: “clearly lost the plot”, “you’re making it up. You need mental help”, “cooked”, “such crap”, and “Freak”.

Legacy media were just as glib. They appeared to ditch due diligence by skipping Rice’s 6 October video explaining how God had directed her to resign.

The Daily Mail, Nine, and https://t.co/1jijAG84kT ignored that reel. They ran the criticisms and the Instagram carousel image Rice had posted on 13 October.

Titled “A Career Change,” her offending post, in part, read, “I was offered to become CEO, my dream position… but God asked me to resign. I obeyed.”

Of the three, The Daily Mail was the most dishonestly jarring. Their headline read: “Fears for Stephanie Rice as her followers think she has been brainwashed after moving to Dubai and finding God: ‘Poor girl’.”

Ignored by The Daily Mail, Rice said in her two-part 6 October Instagram video explanation, “So how do I know that it was God who asked me to resign from my job and not the voice in my head?”

“1. He spoke through a story I’d already lived. 2. He confirmed it again while journaling. 3. He gave me a vision which I have held onto in this waiting season.”

NICK SABAN REVEALS HOW HE LEFT MICHIGAN STATE FOR LSU AFTER THE SPARTANS OFFERED HIM A RAISE OF MORE THAN $100,000.

And the story is a fascinating look at one of the biggest coaching decisions in college football history.

In footage from a documentary about his legendary coaching career, Saban reflects on the circumstances surrounding his departure from Michigan State following the 1999 season.

At the time, Saban was building a successful program in East Lansing and had attracted attention from other schools looking for their next head coach.

But Michigan State wasn’t ready to let him leave without a fight.

As speculation about his future continued, the Spartans made an effort to keep Saban in East Lansing, including a significant financial commitment.

The documentary revisits the rumors surrounding his potential departure and the decision that eventually brought him to LSU.

And what happened next changed college football forever.

Saban left Michigan State to become LSU’s head coach in 2000, beginning a five-season run that would culminate in a BCS national championship following the 2003 season.

That success helped establish him as one of the nation’s premier coaches.

After a brief stint in the NFL with the Miami Dolphins, Saban eventually took over Alabama in 2007.

The rest is history.

Saban went on to win six national championships with the Crimson Tide, building one of the most dominant dynasties college football has ever seen.

Combined with his championship at LSU, Saban finished his college coaching career with seven national titles.

And it all makes his decision to leave Michigan State even more interesting in hindsight.

For the Spartans, retaining Saban could have dramatically changed the trajectory of their program.

For LSU and Alabama, his eventual arrival helped reshape the history of both schools.

It’s incredible to think about how differently college football might have unfolded if Saban had decided to stay in East Lansing.

One coaching decision helped change the sport for decades.

(Via Saban documentary)

The father, Gleidson Tiago da Cruz was convicted of qualified homicide (homicídio qualificado) and sentenced to 14 years in closed regime (regime)

On June 26, 2024, a popular jury in Blumenau (Santa Catarina) accepted the Santa Catarina Public Prosecutor’s Office (MPSC) thesis in full. He was convicted of homicide qualified by a futile motive (*motivo fútil*) and the use of means that made the victim’s defense impossible. The victim was Giovane Ferreira da Silva de Oliveira, a 29-year-old homeless man who sold peanut candy (paçoca).

Key points from the investigation and trial (as reported by MPSC, G1, and local outlets):
- The argument began when Giovane offered candy to Gleidson’s ~2-year-old daughter outside a supermarket.
- After an initial confrontation (including Gleidson striking the victim with a metal rod, according to the prosecution), Gleidson left, went home, retrieved a knife, and returned roughly 7 minutes later.
- He then stabbed Giovane approximately 19 times (including from behind and while the victim tried to flee); the knife lodged in the victim’s cervical spine. The attack occurred in front of his daughter and witnesses.

Self-defense was rejected by the jury. Earlier custody-hearing decisions had also found insufficient evidence for legitimate defense, citing the sequence of events, the number of wounds, and witness statements. Gleidson has been imprisoned since the day of the crime (November 3, 2023) and was denied the right to appeal in freedom. The defense indicated it would appeal (particularly on a qualifier), but available reporting as of 2026 still treats the 14-year conviction as in effect.

Note that many viral social-media posts (including the one you referenced) presented a simplified narrative of immediate self-defense against an armed aggressor who kicked a stroller. Court findings described a more protracted sequence in which Gleidson left the scene, armed himself, and returned.

text:
Grok Bot just got an update with v0.71.2! 🚀

Smarter notifications and larger file attachments
Also includes v0.71.0 and v0.71.1

Changelog v0.71.2

New:
• Bots can send from a tagged form of their email address, like name+shop@, and a routine on that tag runs only for its mail.
• Forms a Bot asks you to fill in can arrive with known fields filled in, and you can edit them before you submit.
• While a paid account merge is still moving this account's data, Settings shows Your accounts are being merged, with Contact Support if it runs long.
• Team admins can turn off Messaging between Bots under Bot capabilities on the dashboard, so members' Bots can't message or hand work to other Bots. (Teams)
• Enterprise team admins can recreate, terminate, or delete members' Grok Bot computers from Manage Bot Computers on the dashboard or through the Admin API. (Enterprise)
• When a Bot's computer runs low on disk, the Bot tells you once, names the biggest files, and deletes them only if you agree.

Improved:
• While you use Grok Bot on a Mac or Windows PC, Bot replies and questions notify you there instead of your phone. Requires Grok Bot 0.70.2 or later.
• You can attach files up to 250 MB and videos up to 1 GB, and the Bot says when a video is too large to watch. Requires Grok Bot 0.70.2 or later.
• One message can carry up to 20 attachments instead of 6, and a notice says how many weren't added past the 200 MB total.
• Images a Bot creates or captures, and files from cloud agents it started, load in the chat while its computer is asleep.
• If a voice chat's connection drops, the call reconnects and continues the same conversation instead of ending.
• Bots can use up to 200 skills from your installed plugins instead of 24, so skills from plugins you add are no longer left out.
• When a Bot's computer is asleep, clicking the Computer is asleep preview wakes it in place, replacing the separate Wake button.
• Grok Bot opens while the Bot's computer is still starting, instead of waiting behind a full-window Setting up Grok Bot's computer screen.
• Sending while the Bot's computer wakes no longer shows Waiting to send… under your message or Waking your computer… in the message box.
• Bots can archive, move, delete, flag, or mark many Outlook messages as read or unread in one step instead of one at a time.
• At checkout, Bots use card details or photos you send in chat, asking only for missing fields or a verification code in a Secure Form.
• When GitHub can't see a repository, the Bot stops retrying and gives you a link to the GitHub page where you grant access.
• Bot searches on X with date limits, minimum likes or reposts, or filters X doesn't support now return posts instead of being rejected.
• When a Bot asks you to choose with a question card, it no longer repeats the question and options in a message beside it.
• Email drafts from a Bot's own address show attachments as file cards, marked when they can't be sent, changed since attached, are too large, or weren't scanned.
• Merging accounts finishes when both accounts have files on the Bot's computer, keeping both sets and adding (from transferred account) to clashing file names.
• In Team Bot Slack setup, Connect goes straight to Slack, Awaiting admin approval offers Resubmit, and a denied request shows when it was denied. (Teams)
• When a Team Bot asks to use your connected account, the card explains the access covers only your own messages and others can't use it. (Teams)
• Captions in the full-screen image viewer show formatting and clickable links, and images keep their size as you page between them.
• In a Bot's info pane, the name reads as plain text until you hover or click to rename it, and screen readers announce it as editable.
• On approval cards, the rule under labels such as Paused by your Ask first rule shows as plain text, without a box or quotation marks.
• Animated Bot avatars in the sidebar and a chat's activity line move more smoothly.
• When GitHub isn't connected, the Bot offers a single Connect GitHub action instead of listing every GitHub tool.
• A voice call from your phone wakes the Bot's sleeping computer, so the Bot can work with what you said after the call.

Fixed:
• While the Bot's computer is asleep, Grok Bot keeps what it loaded and says Your computer is asleep instead of showing Couldn't refresh or connection errors.
• When the Bot's computer updates, a working Bot reconnects to the new computer and keeps going.
• When the Bot's computer fails to wake, the Bot says it couldn't start instead of retrying as if it were still starting up.
• Images and files a Bot shares from its computer still load in the chat when the app can't fetch them from that computer directly.
• Opening a file right after you send it shows its contents instead of File unavailable.
• When the server fails an attachment upload, Grok Bot says Couldn't upload an attachment and keeps your draft, instead of asking you to check your connection.
• When your computer sleeps, Bots treat it as disconnected within two minutes and say so right away, instead of waiting for commands to time out.
• After a Wi-Fi, VPN, or other network change, Bots can run tasks on your computer right away instead of finding it unreachable.
• Commands a Bot runs on your computer keep going through brief connection stalls and long waits instead of failing as temporarily unreachable.
• If work is meant for one of your computers that's offline, the Bot tells you instead of running it on another computer without asking.
• Background jobs a Bot starts on your Mac, such as a local server, keep running after the command returns.
• Plugin and Auto-review settings changes keep reaching the Bot's computer after Grok Bot reconnects, instead of stalling until a restart.
• When a Bot asks to wait on a command longer than the time limit, it's told the limit right away instead of timing out.
• When a safety check blocks a Bot's reply, the chat shows Blocked by a safety check and Try a different message instead of a generic error.
• Tables in Bot replies stay within the reply's width and scroll sideways when they need more room.
• Attachments in one message that share a file name are numbered, such as report.pdf (2), so you can open or remove the right one.
• On Windows, pasting text copied from a list into the message box keeps it inline instead of splitting it into extra paragraphs.
• On Windows and Linux, text copied from a chat pastes into other apps with non-English characters and curly quotes intact.
• Opening Grok Bot to a restored chat no longer flashes a Couldn't refresh bar above the message box.
• Switching accounts or signing back in shows the app's loading frame instead of a blank white window.
• Switching accounts while a queued message is canceled or refused no longer puts its text and attachments in the other account's message box.
• Accounts without Grok Bot access finish setup and see just the access notice, without setup or load errors.
• When the Bot you had open is deleted on another device, Grok Bot opens another of your Bots instead of an empty pane.
• Deleting several Bots at once still deletes the rest when one fails, and the alert names only the Bot that failed.
• Sidebar section changes that can't be saved stay put with Can't reach your computer and Retry, then save once your computer is reachable.
• In the collapsed sidebar, a Bot list that can't load shows a warning icon with retry instead of text squeezed letter by letter.
• The full-screen computer view no longer shows a cut-off snippet of a subagent's instructions or a Couldn't load subagents line.
• When a Bot's routines fail to load, Couldn't load routines appears inside the Routines section of its details pane.
• With the details pane open and no Bot selected, a failed primary Bot load shows Couldn't load and Try again.
• When a Bot's skills can't be loaded, the @ menu no longer shows a Couldn't load skills row.
• The sidebar's number shortcut badges no longer stay on screen after you change zoom with Cmd or Ctrl.
• In the collapsed sidebar, the More unreads button is a circle with its arrow centered.
• When you drag Bots or sections in the sidebar, screen readers announce their names and where they land.
• Screen readers announce a Bot's reply even when it arrives after the announcement that the Bot stopped.
• When you Tab to a link and its preview card opens, keyboard focus moves into the card.
• When a Bot changes a routine while the app is briefly disconnected, the Routines list updates once it reconnects, without a reload.
• After onboarding creates your primary Bot, the Introducing your primary Bot chooser no longer asks you to pick one again.
• After you answer a request to use your computer, the Bot's sidebar row shows Allowed, Denied, or Expired instead of Permission required.
• When you pause and keep talking in a voice chat, the transcript extends your line instead of repeating it, and leaves out noise tags.
• Connector calls no longer time out after one minute: they wait up to two minutes for a reply, and longer while the connector reports progress.
• Bots see the full parameters of tools on connectors from Grok, so they call those tools correctly instead of guessing.
• Bots hit X's rate limit less often when searching X or reading posts, and a rate-limited call no longer counts toward your X read limit.
• Bots work with a specific Stripe customer, invoice, subscription, or payment on the first try instead of hitting a missing parameter error.
• Stop also ends a Bot's background subagents, so their results no longer wake the Bot afterward, and their pending approval cards expire.
• When you hand the Bot's computer back with I'm done or Skip, the Bot posts its answer in the chat instead of sometimes staying silent.
• Scripts a Bot runs in its browser no longer fail over extra or out-of-range settings, so browser tasks finish more often.
• Secure Form fills fields on more websites, including inside embedded frames from other sites, instead of leaving them empty.
• When a routine needs to sign in to a site, it asks you in chat at that step instead of quietly stopping.
• Bots ask for logins and other multi-field details on one Secure Form instead of a secret request card that holds a single value.
• Screenshot, computer, and browser actions keep working when you haven't connected 1Password, instead of failing on a saved-login check.
• Messaging from another time zone updates the zone the Bot uses for schedules and reminders right away, unless you chose one under Timezone in Settings.
• Bots with any shape the avatar editor offers, such as sparkle or star, can be shared as templates without the Bot changing its look.
• Emails that arrive in a Bot's own inbox keep each link's web address, so the Bot can open verification and sign-in links.
• Email sent to a Bot's own address arrives even when its subject, sender address, or thread references are very long.
• After you choose Disable drafts for a Bot, it sends email from its own address right away, without a draft card.
• After a Bot claims an email address, opening Email or Plugins shows it as Connected instead of still offering Connect.
• When you allow a Team Bot to use one of your plugins, its tools work right away instead of the Bot failing to find them. (Teams)
• Plugins on a Team Bot use the settings your team admin entered, such as a Datadog site, when the Bot has none of its own. (Teams)
• A Team Bot still named New team bot with no description shows Draft, not Published to your team, until you rename it or add a description. (Teams)
• Grok Bot works under your selected team even when another team you're on uses Privacy Mode (Legacy), as long as the selected team doesn't.
• Account merges that move many Bots finish in one go instead of failing and showing Your account merge is taking longer than usual.
• When a downloaded update is withdrawn, Restart to Update goes away and Grok Bot keeps your current version, even when you quit on a Mac.
• An update download that keeps restarting from the beginning waits between tries and then stops with an error instead of retrying nonstop.
• When the update server sends a broken response, Settings says The update server returned an invalid response instead of blaming your connection.
• Restart to Update shows Restarting… and waits up to two minutes for commands a Bot is running on your computer to finish.
• When an update replaces Grok Bot's files while it runs, reloading or crash recovery relaunches the app instead of showing a blank window.
• On Linux deb and rpm installs, Update required links the latest package, leading with it when the package repository doesn't have the update yet.
• On Windows and Linux, opening Grok Bot while it's still quitting reopens it after the quit instead of leaving nothing open.
• GitHub tools stay available after a connection block and work once you reconnect, without starting a new chat.

• A connector that still needs Allow keeps its name, so the Bot asks you to allow it instead of saying it can't find it.

text:
XXII

The Trouble With Staying

Angel woke to find a book open on her stomach.

Again.

She blinked at the dim room, the blanket tangled around her legs, and Liam sitting beside her with a suspiciously amused expression.

“How long was I asleep?”

“Long enough for me to consider decorating you for Halloween.”

“You wouldn’t dare.”

“I had ideas. Maybe a sign saying Do Not Disturb. Currently Deceased Adjacent.”

“I’m throwing this book at you.”

“You’d have to pick it up first.”

She glanced at the book on her stomach.

Liam smiled.

She hated how much she loved that smile.

“Did you wake me?”

“No.”

“Did I drool on you?”

His expression shifted.

“Liam.”

“I’ve decided to take that information to my grave.”

“Your grave?”

“Fine. Wherever ghosts go when they’re being unfairly interrogated.”

She laughed and pushed his shoulder. His hand found hers on the blanket, their fingers intertwining naturally.

Angel looked down at them.

“You stayed.”

“That’s generally what happens when someone falls asleep on you. You become furniture.”

“You could’ve left.”

“I could’ve become a professional ballet dancer. We all have unrealized potential.”

“I’m serious.”

“I know.”

His answer was quieter than she’d expected.

Something about his expression made her pause. He looked thoughtful, almost unsettled, as though he’d discovered something he couldn’t explain.

“What?” she asked.

“Nothing.”

“That’s your second-worst lie.”

“What’s the first?”

“‘I’m fine.’”

“That’s your line.”

“Exactly. I know a professional when I see one.”

He laughed, and the moment passed. Angel leaned back against the sofa, still holding his hand.

She didn’t ask again. She knew what it felt like to need time before putting something into words.

Instead, she reached for her book.

Liam pulled it away.

“Absolutely not.”

“Excuse me?”

“No research tonight. You’ve read enough ominous nonsense to qualify as a minor academic threat.”

“I was going to read something else.”

“Something cheerful, I assume. Perhaps a book about the inevitable collapse of the universe.”

“Give it back.”

“Ask nicely.”

“Give it back, or I’ll read your terrible poetry aloud.”

His eyes widened. “You wouldn’t.”

“Try me.”

He handed it over immediately.

Angel grinned. “Thought so.”

They spent the next hour talking about nothing important. She told him about something ridiculous she’d overheard that day. He offered unnecessary opinions about people he’d never met. She accused him of being judgmental.

He reminded her that he was dead, not deaf.

Eventually, her head found his shoulder again.

Liam rested his cheek against her hair.

He could still remember the feeling of her heartbeat beneath his hand. He didn’t understand it or know what it meant.

For once, he decided not to chase the answer.

Angel shifted closer, her fingers curling around his.

“You’re quiet,” she murmured.

“Enjoy it. It won’t last.”

“I wasn’t complaining.”

“I know.”

Her eyes closed.

A few minutes later, her breathing slowed.

Liam looked down at her.

“You know, for someone who claims to enjoy her own company, you’re remarkably determined to use me as a pillow.”

“You’re comfortable,” she mumbled.

He went still.

Then he looked at the ceiling.

“That’s devastating. I’ve spent years developing a personality.”

She didn’t answer. She was asleep again.

Liam settled beside her, letting the quiet gather around them.

He still didn’t know what was happening to him. He didn’t know what the book would reveal, why the gates had opened, or why he’d been drawn to someone he’d never met while alive.

But he knew this much.

Leaving had once been the easiest part of every night.

Now, staying was becoming the part he couldn’t imagine giving up.

And that frightened him far more than any gate ever could.

text: A farmer does not need a messenger to tell him rain is coming. He feels it in his knees, in the way the dogs go quiet, in a hundred small signs his own years of watching have taught him to read without even trying…. nobody delivers that knowledge to him from outside. It was grown in him, slowly, through attention……..That is closer to what is actually happening with the sense so many people carry now that something large is turning. The instinct is right that a shift is coming. The mistake is in where people point the telescope……..They want a craft, a confirmation, an outside intelligence finally stepping forward to settle the matter…. but the faculty that can actually read a coming age has never lived in the sky. It lives in the advanced soul itself, as a plain property of being further along, the same way a trained ear hears the wrong note before the orchestra does. It is not supernatural. It runs on the ordinary connection between the unseen and the seen that every soul carries, stronger in some than others, the way some farmers simply read weather better than their neighbours…….but that knowing is often deliberately taken back afterwards. A soul far enough along can, in rare moments, hold a stretch of time the way you might hold a whole river in view from a hill, see what is coming whole…. and then wake with most of it gone, left only with a pull, a certainty without content, just enough to steer by and no more. It shows up strongest exactly in danger, in upheaval, in the years before something breaks open, which is a clue . The pull people feel is not a sign sent from elsewhere. It is memory leaking through from a vision their OWN further-along self already had and was not allowed to keep whole…..And the shift itself, when it comes, will not look like arrival. It will look like exhaustion. A world wrings every drop out of cleverness, builds and calculates and solves, and still feels a thinness it cannot name, an ache for something cleverness never had on offer. That ache is moral growth finally catching up with intelligence, and it never arrives tidy. It comes through argument first, through ideas grinding against each other before anything clears, because nothing this size has ever moved through a species without friction……….So, stop scanning the horizon for the visitor. The instrument capable of reading the age correctly is the one you are already carrying, and it sharpens the same way the farmer's did, by years of paying honest attention and living well through them, not by waiting longer at the window.

text:
Interesting question. I asked my Hermes agent, it took it good minute to find the setting it but here it is (with a little tongue-in-cheek at the end... 🤣):
===
Found it. The chime is Hermes Desktop’s **turn-completion sound**, and there’s a persistent mute flag—but the current Settings page only offers different sounds, not an Off option.

**To silence it:**

1. In Hermes, press **⌥⌘I** to open Developer Tools.
2. Select **Console** and run:
   ```js
   localStorage.setItem('hermes.desktop.hapticsMuted', 'true')
   ```
3. Quit and reopen Hermes **after this reply finishes**.

That setting survives restarts. It also mutes the wake-word chime and thinking blips; it isn’t a system-wide audio mute.

I verified the code: `playCompletionSound()` immediately returns when that flag is true. To undo it, run the same command with `'false'` and reopen.

**I haven’t changed anything.** And no, choosing fourteen varieties of ding without offering “no ding” is not a triumph of interface design.

text:
$CRWV  is the most obvious short in the market and that is why i'm not currently shorting it:

For full disclosure, in the short section of Fraxinus Capital’s Q2 letter, I wrote that we were short the neoclouds. We are no longer short any of them. We may have covered a little early, but at the time we felt we'd captured most of the downside and r/r was not as good as it previously was. 

CoreWeave and the other neoclouds, but especially CoreWeave, look to me like the most obvious shorts in the AI market. I see very little foreseeable upside in the underlying business economics. And that is exactly why I'm not shorting them right now.

If you're long Nvidia or other names in the AI ecosystem, it's easy to see why these companies look like the natural short against that exposure. The recent selloff has shown us that the market expects the Neoclouds to take the first to get hit if there's a crack in the AI trade. While this may have been obvious to anyone who has looked at the AI market, until the market sees confirmation, it is slow to react on a trade like this. If you’re a net neutral long/short fund, You could adjust the position sizes for beta and look at the pairing as a potentially attractive hedge.  I think that's part of what the market is looking at and why these companies could have a poor equity reaction over the near term. 

Then there's the debt. CoreWeave has a lot of it. With Corweave’s debt trading between 14-15% Yield to Maturity, and somewhere around a 20% discount to par there's another trade to consider: going long the debt while shorting the equity. In my view, that pairing could offer a favorable skew for R/R, So there are two reasons an investor might be short these shares.

Going back to why we were short in the first place, the assumptions needed to make these businesses economically viable just didn't look tenable to us. Fabio and I looked at CoreWeave, and he did most of the work on this name and other Neoclouds. From my memory, you had to assume GPU rental rates would rise over the next five years, and even then the result was something like a 1% return after debt costs. I don't have the exact calculation in front of me, but that was roughly the outcome. To us, it didn't make much sense.

When you compared those economics with the profitability of companies such as Nvidia  and memory names (we are long both NVDA and SK Hynix) elsewhere in the AI ecosystem, the short made sense to us as a hedge for a portfolio with AI exposure. We liked the economics in other parts of the trade, and we could use these companies to hedge some of that exposure.

Fast forward to today, and these companies have been slammed. Most of the neoclouds are down 50-60% from their recent highs and down 20-30% in the last week.  To me, the bearish argument now seems much more widely understood. Other investors have had time to do the work, look at the economics, and reach the same conclusion.

That's actually a scary setup for me as someone looking to go short. If weak economics are already widely recognized, and the shares have already fallen that much on recognition of this, the next major downside catalyst starts to feel like something closer to bankruptcy risk. I don't personally see these companies going bankrupt in the next couple of years. I could be wrong on that. But given that view, I don't think the risk and reward favor putting the shorts back on here.

At some point, I could see looking at them as a trade in the other direction. If AI sentiment turns upward, you could get a violent rally. For an opportunistic trader, there may be a technical long setup. I don't like them as fundamental longs, but that doesn't stop the shares from having that kind of move. They've been in the headlines a lot lately, and I wanted to explain where I stand.

Because of this though, we are not wanting to take either side of the trade at the moment.  This could change at any time in the near future and all of this is just a thought process and meant for entertainment, but we currently think there are more attractive R/R setups in the market and would rather target those for shorts.

text:
Chad Johnson saved 83 percent of every dollar he made in the National Football League.

For the first two years of his career he lived inside the Cincinnati stadium so he would not have to pay rent.

He is now offering 2 million dollars of that money to a college freshman he has never met.

Here is the whole thing.

The freshman is Jesse Legree, and he plays receiver at Oregon State. Right now he leads the entire country in receiving yards and in touchdown catches, with 14 of those.

Oregon State won seven games total across the previous two seasons. They have already won five this year, under a head coach in his first season there.

Which means when this season ends, every rich program in America is going to come for that kid.

So Chad Johnson went on Nightcap and said this, out loud, to the Oregon State head coach.

"You give him 2 million dollars, I give him 2 million dollars. That's 4 million dollars right there."

Now here is why a man says a thing like that.

He did not qualify academically coming out of high school in Miami. He barely went to class.

He landed at a small school in Oklahoma called Langston, and he got thrown out of there for skipping class and getting in trouble. He never played a single down for them.

So he went to a junior college in Santa Monica.

Then he was ruled ineligible and lost another year completely.

Then back to the same junior college.

And then one school in America offered him a scholarship. Oregon State.

He played there exactly one season. That team went eleven and one and beat Notre Dame in the Fiesta Bowl, and Cincinnati took him in the second round the following spring.

One season. That is the entire relationship.

Now understand what the 2 million dollars actually is.

This is a man who lived in a stadium to avoid paying rent. Here is how he described it on Club Shay Shay.

"Showers, cafeteria, TV, couch, gaming system. What's the point? I was so locked in."

His own head coach is the one who finally made him leave and go get an apartment.

He wore fake jewelry instead of real jewelry. He flew Spirit instead of private.

That is the money he just offered to a teenager he has never spoken to.

Now the honest part. This was one sentence on a podcast, not a signed check, and nobody at Oregon State has said anything about it. Four million dollars for a receiver is not even a surprising number anymore. Legree may walk at the end of the year and he will have every right to. And Chad Johnson says a great many things into a great many microphones.

But nobody asked him for this one.

And of all the people in football who could have spoken up for that school, the one who did is the man it took when nothing else would have him.

A guy who slept in a stadium to save money is offering 2 million dollars of it so a freshman he has never met does not have to leave.

text:
Fed cattle in western Nebraska sold up to $227 live on Friday. The same week, choice boxed beef closed at $372.31, down $1.04.

Higher cattle against lower beef is the wrong direction for a packer. It is what he pays when he needs cattle worse than he needs the spread.

The board said it would not happen. October live cattle fell 22 cents Monday, 12 Tuesday, 72 Wednesday.

Then it turned. Up $2.05 Thursday, $1.60 Friday, closed the week at $227.55.

Corbitt Wall on Friday's Feeder Flash: "They finally got a little bit of grit to them and they asked for a little bit more."

Country trade backed him up. Northern Plains live cattle ran $220 to $223 through Thursday. Friday brought $220 to $225 in Iowa, $222 to $227 in Nebraska, and dressed bids of $350 to $360, steady to $8 higher.

What moved the number was a refusal. The first bid is an opening offer. It only gets raised when the seller has feed in the bunk, room at the bank and enough cattle to say no.

Formula cattle, roughly 70 percent of the kill, are priced off that negotiated print. The 17 percent who can afford to wait are pricing everybody else's contract.
