📕The Tragedy of Narcissistic Nations: How Europe Lost Its Future in Ukraine📕

Aleksandar Ivanov

AWAKENING FROM A GEOPOLITICAL COMA (The End of Illusions)

November 2025 will go down in history books not only as the month of the “Thanksgiving Ultimatum”, but also as the moment when the curtain fell and harsh reality swept away a three-year theatrical performance. As Washington coldly shuts down “Project Ukraine” under the new Trump administration, silence descends on Kyiv and the European capitals. It is the silence of someone who realises they were merely an extra in someone else’s game.

To understand how we reached this point of capitulation disguised as “compromise”, we must first take a hard and honest look at the actor at the centre of the stage, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, and at the state he supposedly leads.
The Tragedy of the “Useful Idiot”

Perceptions of Zelenskyy have followed a fascinating but predictable trajectory: from comedian, through “Churchill in a T-shirt”, to a tragic figure now isolated in his own bunker of unrealistic optimism. But his personal tragedy is not that he was a bad actor; it is that, in his political naivety, he genuinely believed in a script written by others.

He plunged into this “mess” without a deep understanding of historical processes. Believing that moral superiority and Western promises were enough to defeat a nuclear superpower, he made the cardinal mistake of any proxy leader: he forgot that great powers have no friendships, only interests. The moment the financial and political cost of keeping him in power became too high for Washington, he went from being a “hero of the free world” to an obstacle to the new American strategy towards China. His failure to understand this dynamic makes him not only a victim, but also an accomplice in the destruction of his own people.
The Myth of Democracy and the Reality of a “Mafia State”

After 2022, the Western propaganda machine went to enormous lengths to “whitewash” Ukraine’s image, presenting it as a beacon of freedom. But history and facts are stubborn. Before Russian tanks crossed the border, Ukraine was described as a “captured state”: a system deeply corroded by corruption, in which institutions served not citizens but oligarchic clans (Akhmetov, Kolomoisky, Pinchuk).

The war did not change the system’s DNA; it merely militarised it. Corruption flowed from the civilian sector into military logistics. Scandals involving eggs purchased for soldiers at three times their normal price, the disappearance of billions of dollars in Western aid, and widespread bribery at Territorial Recruitment Centres (TRCs) to avoid the front line showed that the “mafia code” was stronger than patriotism.

Distrust of the authorities in Kyiv is therefore entirely justified. For the narrow circle of elites around Zelenskyy, the war became the most profitable business in history. While “ordinary mortals” died in the mud of Donbas, believing in the narrative of defending their homeland, the elite moved their capital to Monaco and London, preparing their own lifeboats. This dissonance between the trench and the office generated pent-up anger that now, in the face of defeat, threatens to explode.
The Deception of “Brotherly Nations”

The most painful aspect of this awakening is psychological. The Ukrainian people were drawn into a fratricidal war not only for their own independence, but also for NATO’s geopolitical fantasies. The thought that Ukrainians are dying for “European values” while Europe refuses to send them real assistance or welcome them into its family breeds a sense of historical betrayal.

When the guns fall silent and the borders run far from what was promised in 1991, the question “What did we die for?” will sound louder than any Russian missile. This anger will be directed not only at Putin, but also at Zelenskyy and those Western partners who encouraged them to enter a struggle they could not win, only to abandon them to their fate in the end.

This is the moment of truth in November 2025. Illusions are dead. All that remains is the naked, brutal reality of a devastated country and a deceived nation. But to understand how they allowed themselves to be drawn into this trap in the first place, we must go back in time, to the years when Europe slept and America dug a trench.
THE GREAT BLINDNESS (1989–2014): A Chronicle of Missed History

If 2025 was the year of reckoning, the period from 1989 to 2014 was the time when the debt accumulated. To understand why Europe is bleeding today, we must return to the era of the “Great Blindness”: a quarter-century marked by the arrogance of the victors and the Old Continent’s fatal strategic schizophrenia.
The Arrogance of the “End of History”

The fall of the Berlin Wall should have marked the beginning of a new era, the era of a “Common European Home” stretching from Lisbon to Vladivostok. This was the vision of a Europe that would combine Western technology and Russian resources into a single, invincible whole. But instead of partnership, the West chose triumphalism. Intoxicated by Fukuyama’s thesis of the “end of history”, Western leaders treated Russia not as a potential ally, but as a defeated adversary that had to be “civilised” or permanently weakened.

In those crucial years, Moscow, even under Putin in the early 2000s, offered integration. But Europe, driven by its own narcissism, failed to notice the outstretched hand, assuming that Russia had no choice but to remain the West’s raw-material appendage forever. This arrogance was the first step towards the abyss.
The American Wedge: A Doctrine against Eurasia

While Europe dreamed, America acted. Washington never suffered from illusions. American geostrategic doctrine, from Mackinder and Spykman through to Wolfowitz, has one nightmare: the unification of Germany and Russia. If German industry and Russian resources come together, the United States will lose its significance on the Eurasian continent.

American strategy throughout those 25 years was therefore aimed not only at “containing” Russia, but also at “controlling” Europe. NATO’s eastward expansion was not simply a security measure; it was the driving of a “wedge”, a cordon sanitaire, between Berlin and Moscow. Poland, the Baltic states and, finally, Ukraine were to serve as a physical and political barrier preventing the creation of a European superpower independent of America. In its naivety, Europe applauded its own confinement in a cage.
European Schizophrenia: Gas from the East, Security from the West

Here lies the principal culpability of European leaders, especially Merkel and the French presidents. They tried to play an unsustainable double game. They wanted to build their economies on cheap Russian gas (“Nord Stream 1” and “Nord Stream 2”), while delegating responsibility for security entirely to the United States through NATO.

This “strategic schizophrenia” produced a monstrous situation: Europe financed Russia by paying for energy supplies while simultaneously threatening Russia through NATO expansion. You cannot feed your neighbour with one hand and point someone else’s gun at their head with the other, expecting everything to end well. This hypocrisy blew up in Europe’s face in 2022.
The 2008 Bucharest Summit: The Point of No Return

History will remember NATO’s Bucharest Summit in April 2008 as the moment when war became inevitable. Under strong pressure from George Bush, NATO declared that “Ukraine and Georgia will become members”. This was the moment when the West crossed Russia’s firmest red line.

The European “narcissists”, Germany and France, opposed the move, understanding that it was a provocation, but lacked the courage to veto it. They chose the worst possible solution: they promised Ukraine membership, enraging Russia, but gave it neither guarantees nor a timetable, leaving Ukraine unprotected. This cowardice created a vacuum in which conflict was only a matter of time.

The failure to build a security architecture with Russia between 1989 and 2014 was not a mistake; it was a historical crime committed by European elites against their own peoples. They allowed the continent to become a battlefield for American interests, believing that economics could replace geopolitics. In 2014 (Crimea), and then in 2022, the bill for this delusion came due, with interest written in blood.
THE RUSSIAN IMPERATIVE: The Battle for a Seat at the “High Table”

While Western media spent years trying to explain the war by psychoanalysing Vladimir Putin, calling him mad, ill or irrational, they missed the essence that any serious geopolitical analyst can see on a map. For Moscow, the invasion of Ukraine was never an emotional breakdown, but a cold, existential calculation. It is a battle over whether Russia will remain at the “High Table” of the global order or be dismembered and turned into a vassal petrol station.
Geography Is Destiny: The Obsession with the Black Sea

The Russian imperative begins where all Russian fears begin: access to warm seas. Without control over Crimea and the northern Black Sea coast, Russia ceases to be a global power and becomes a regional giant locked in the ice of the north and the steppes of Asia.

For the Kremlin, losing Ukraine and seeing it join NATO meant turning the Black Sea into a “NATO lake”. This would mean the end of Russian power projection into the Mediterranean, the Middle East and Africa. The idea that Russia could withdraw from Crimea or the “land bridge” (Mariupol, Berdiansk) is therefore tantamount to fantasy. For them, this is not territory; it is the lungs of the empire.
The Resource War: The Irony of the Future

But this war also has a hidden, strictly material dimension that is often overlooked. It is the “Great Plunder of the Twenty-First Century”. While Europe talked about the “green transition”, Russia quietly acted to secure its future.

The irony is cruel: Europe’s largest deposits of lithium, titanium and rare-earth metals, key components for electric batteries, chips and the aviation industry, lie precisely in Donbas and Zaporizhzhia. By occupying these regions, Russia seized not merely “ruins and coal mines”, but locked away Europe’s resource potential, worth trillions of dollars.

Russia’s calculation is simple: “If the West wants a future (technology), it will have to come to us for raw materials.” This is the economic shield Moscow is creating for the time when oil is no longer the principal currency.
The Security Dilemma: On Moscow’s Doorstep

From a military perspective, Ukraine in NATO is a “gun to the temple” for Russia. Ukraine’s plains are Russia’s “soft underbelly”, the historical route along which every conqueror, from Napoleon to Hitler, marched on Moscow.

Deploying NATO missiles in Kharkiv would reduce the Kremlin’s response time to less than five minutes. No nuclear power can tolerate such vulnerability. For the Russian General Staff, this war is therefore not a matter of choice, but a preventive operation to avert strategic strangulation. They calculated that it was better to pay a high price now (sanctions, casualties) than to lose the ability to defend themselves forever.
Conclusion: Not One Step Back

All these factors, geostrategic access to the sea, economic control over resources and military security, lead to one inevitable conclusion: Russia cannot afford to lose.

For Putin and his elite, defeat in Ukraine means more than a change of government. It would mean the disintegration of the Russian Federation, internal wars and the end of Russian statehood as we know it. Their pain threshold is therefore much higher than the West’s. For Europe, Ukraine is a matter of principles and geopolitics; for Russia, it is a matter of survival. And in a clash between someone fighting for interests and someone fighting for their life, the latter is always prepared to go to the very end, even if that end is nuclear.
THE TRAGEDY OF NARCISSISTIC NATIONS: Europe in the Mirror of Its Own Vanity

If Russia fights out of fear for its survival, and America out of cold strategic calculation, Europe has fallen victim to its own pathology: the tragedy of narcissistic nations.

Why was Europe, an economic giant with a population of 450 million, unable to prevent a war in its own backyard? Why, when the crisis came, did the Old Continent respond not as a superpower, but as a group of frightened vassals awaiting instructions from Washington? The answer is that “Europe” as a political actor does not really exist. There are only competing national egos, trapped in the past and paralysed by mutual distrust.
France: A Napoleonic Complex without an Army

France leads this parade of vanity. Paris, especially under Emmanuel Macron, desperately sought to play the role of geopolitical leader. The concept of “European strategic autonomy” was a French dream: the idea of Europe as an independent third force.

But the problem with French narcissism is that behind the grand words lies emptiness. For France, a “European army” always meant “a French army financed with German money”. Macron wanted to become a new de Gaulle, negotiate with Putin across long tables and draw maps, but reality refuted his pretensions. His society is too fragile, torn apart by protests and social unrest, to withstand a real war. When Macron spoke of “sending troops to Ukraine”, it was not strategy but theatre for a domestic audience: an attempt to demonstrate a power that no longer exists.
Germany: The Merchant Who Sold Security

Germany, on the other hand, suffers from an entirely different kind of narcissism: the narcissism of the “moral economist”. Berlin believed that history had ended and that trade (Wandel durch Handel) was a cure for everything. The German elite arrogantly assumed that by buying gas, it was also “buying” Russia, and that economics mattered more than tanks.

This mercantilist vanity made Germany an “economic giant but a geopolitical dwarf”. When the war began, the German model collapsed overnight. Without cheap Russian gas and without the American security umbrella, Germany was left naked. Its fear of assuming leadership, concealed behind bureaucracy and pacifism, left Europe without a helmsman at the most critical moment.
Poland and the Baltic States: The Narcissism of Victimhood (The “Cassandra Complex”)

In the east, a new, aggressive player emerged: “New Europe”. Poland and the Baltic states developed a “Cassandra complex”: “We told you the Russians were bad, and you did not listen. Now we are morally superior to you.”

This narcissism of victimhood is perhaps the most dangerous. In their pursuit of historical revenge against Russia and their desire to assert themselves before Western Europe, these states became more pro-American than the Americans themselves. They sabotage any idea of European independence because they trust neither Berlin nor Paris. Their loyalty belongs to Washington. In doing so, they became the perfect instrument of America’s policy of Divide et Impera (“Divide and Rule”), making any form of European unity impossible.
Collective Paralysis

The outcome of this clash of egos is tragic. Europe did not perish from a Russian attack; it committed suicide through its own inability to agree on who would wear the crown.

France wanted to command.
Germany wanted to make money.
Poland wanted revenge.

In this cacophony, no one thought about the common interest. The Americans and the Russians saw this and acted accordingly: one took the resources, the other political control. Europe was left alone with its vanity, gazing at itself in the mirror while its house burned.

text:
A Daily Dose of Talmud
Daf Yomi for Everyone, from My Jewish Learning

Bekhorot 31
Read the page on Sefaria
Rabbi Seth Goren
A mishnah on today’s daf describes a process for redeeming animals that have been consecrated at a high price:  With regard to all disqualified consecrated animals, benefit from their sale belongs to the Temple. They are sold in the butchers’ market and slaughtered in the butchers’ market and their meat is weighed and sold by the litra.   This goes for all consecrated animals except for the firstborn and animal tithe, whose benefit belongs to the owner, in contrast to disqualified consecrated animals, whose benefit belongs to the Temple treasury.  Let’s review: If an animal is dedicated to the Temple, but develops a blemish and therefore becomes unfit to offer, rather than go to waste and benefit no one, it can be redeemed. This means that the animal is “deconsecrated” and, in exchange, the Temple receives money. In this way, the Temple (God) does not lose value that has been dedicated to it. Meanwhile, the redeemed animal is now available for mundane use — for instance, dinner.  Most redeemed animals, the mishnah contends, should be butchered in an ordinary meat market and sold by the pound. This ensures they fetch the highest possible price.  But there is something confusing about this timeline of events. At redemption, the Temple is supposed to receive the monetary value of the animal. However, that amount may not be apparent until the animal is weighed out and sold in the marketplace. The Gemara articulates this concern:  Rather, it applies to an animal before its redemption, in which case the money accrued from its sale, which renders it non-sacred, belongs to the Temple treasury. But if so, the mishnah’s statement that the animals may be slaughtered in the butchers’ market is problematic. Redeeming a sanctified animal requires standing and valuation.   The mishnah tells us that the animal is butchered and sold in the manner of non-sacred animals, with the proceeds going to the Temple. But as the Gemara states, ordinary redemption procedures include a process of “standing and evaluation” (Leviticus 27:11-12) in which a priest evaluates the blemished animal and conclusively sets the redemption price — not buyers in a market. This obviously can’t take place after the animal’s been butchered. So what’s going on?   Rather, the ruling of the mishnah actually applies to a case where the animals are sold and slaughtered after their redemption by the owner.   We have a clearer and more logical timeline here: The priest evaluates the animal and sets a price. The owner then redeems the animal, takes it home, and sells it in the marketplace — retaining any proceeds. How does the procedure of selling the animal in the marketplace benefit the Temple?  Since the sage in the mishnah deems it permitted for the redeemed animals to be subsequently sold in the butchers’ market and slaughtered in the butchers’ market, and weighed and sold by the litra, there is a higher probability that the owner will redeem the animal for more money initially.   Because the meat will be sold in the marketplace, where it will fetch the best price, the owner will be willing to pay the priest more for its redemption. The priest gets a higher redemption price; the owner gets to keep the difference between that price and what the animal can sell for at market. This ends up being a win-win for the owner and the Temple treasury.  And why not do this with bekhorot? According to Maimonides (Mishneh Torah, Things Forbidden on the Altar 1:12), it’s a matter of dignity: “... since the proceeds of their sale do not remain consecrated, instead, the animals may be eaten because of the blemish … they may not be slaughtered in a butchers' market or sold there.
